method: One opus judge at medium effort per document through the Workflow tool, 2026-09-30, over the 50 documents test/size-budget.json listed at bf10f9f0 that are neither a rationale ledger nor under test/. Each row is one mechanism, preference or behavior the document makes a session do, with the words it spends on it scaled so a document's rows sum to its measured size, the judge's call, and the judge's reason. A call is a hypothesis the section that lands it confirms against the ledger.

calls.shrink: kept as its rule and one reason
calls.merge: moved to the owner that already carries it, a pointer left behind where a reader needs one
calls.drop: removed, its ledger entries retired with this file's row as the reason

rows.name: Import doctrine via @-include
rows.does: Pulls claude-kit-doctrine.md into every session's global instructions through the @ include line.
rows.why: This one line is how the whole doctrine loads, and without it nothing else in the kit applies.

rows.name: Slash command routes to skill
rows.does: Tells the session to invoke the graphify skill through the Skill tool before anything else when the user types /graphify.
rows.why: The harness already routes a typed slash command to the installed skill and lists the skill with its description, so restating the route costs words and prevents no failure a current model shows.

rows.name: Graph first for orientation
rows.does: Makes the session run /graphify query as its first pass on architecture and relationship questions when a graphify-out/ directory exists, before reading files broadly.
rows.why: A session will not know to check for graphify-out/ or to prefer the graph over broad file reads unless told, and the saving on large codebases is real.

rows.name: Graph claims need file confirmation
rows.does: Treats each graph claim as a secondary-source finding to confirm against the cited file, and treats commits after the last build as the sign the graph is stale.
rows.why: The doctrine's 'A finding is a hypothesis' and 'A summary outlives its source' bullets already carry this, so only the graph-specific staleness signal needs a clause here, pointing to them.

rows.name: Building a graph needs approval
rows.does: Lets the session query an existing graph freely but leaves building a new graph to the user.
rows.why: Without it, a session that sees the graph is useful may start an expensive build unprompted, and the build's cost and output are the user's call.

rows.name: Skip preamble and flattery
rows.does: Opens answers with the fork and recommendation, not 'great question' or 'you're right'.
rows.why: Cheap, and reflexive agreement openers still appear on 5-family models under pushback.

rows.name: Hold position, one re-check
rows.does: Disagrees first with a reason, and moves only on a new fact, answering a bare 'are you sure' with one re-check.
rows.why: Caving to repeated challenge is a live sycophancy failure, and the one-re-check rule is a concrete, non-obvious remedy.

rows.name: Admit uncertainty, flag memory
rows.does: Says 'I'm not sure' and separates recall from a file just read.
rows.why: The claim-status entry under Verify Before You Claim already carries this whole.

rows.name: Teach reasoning, then execute quietly
rows.does: Shows evidence and alternatives at decision points, then runs an agreed plan without narrating lessons.
rows.why: The fork-recommendation entry under Judgment covers the first half, so one sentence on not lecturing during execution is enough.

rows.name: Plain sentence-level prose
rows.does: Writes one idea per sentence at about twenty words, answer first, with no nested qualifications or packed clauses.
rows.why: Models default to dense, semicolon-packed prose, and this is the operator's most visible house style.

rows.name: Three-layer register pointer
rows.does: Treats prose as sentence, structure and voice layers and sends the voice layer to the prose-register skill.
rows.why: This is architecture of the prose-register skill, and a one-line pointer would do.

rows.name: Answer first at every scale
rows.does: Opens each piece, section, paragraph and bullet with its conclusion, with marketing copy as the declared exception.
rows.why: Models often build up to the point, and this is short and load-bearing.

rows.name: Heading shape rules
rows.does: Makes headings topic-named, title-shaped and at most five words, with standard names for recurring sections.
rows.why: This is detailed document-scale mechanics that belong in prose-register, loaded only when a titled document is written.

rows.name: Rule then reason, bold leads
rows.does: States a rule and its reason as separate sentences, with a bold lead only in scannable catalogs.
rows.why: This is a prose-register recipe detail already owned there.

rows.name: Examples close, never lead
rows.does: Places a concrete case after the rule, marks it illustrative, and never presents an open list as closed.
rows.why: This belongs to prose-register, though 'never write an open list as closed' is worth keeping wherever it lands.

rows.name: Checkable claim form
rows.does: Prefers numbers, names and paths over adjectives and descriptions.
rows.why: It duplicates the claim-status and source-naming rules in Verify Before You Claim and in the send checklist.

rows.name: Register scales with size
rows.does: Applies fewer prose layers to smaller pieces instead of switching the register off.
rows.why: The prose-register skill already states what each scale takes.

rows.name: No em dashes outward
rows.does: Bans em dashes in code comments, SQL, copy, documents for an audience and shipped skills, and names the replacements.
rows.why: Models emit em dashes by default, and this is a hard house preference.

rows.name: State over journey
rows.does: Keeps shipped comments and documents in present-tense fact and moves dates, discovery and evidence marks to commits and Chapters.
rows.why: Models do write 'we found that' comments, but the rule, the litmus test and one exemption fit in about 60 words.

rows.name: Commit title format
rows.does: Writes an UPPERCASE surface prefix plus a proper-sentence title under about 70 characters, and opens the body with a client-briefing sentence.
rows.why: This is an idiosyncratic house format that no model infers.

rows.name: Length matches the job
rows.does: Cuts filler and redundant summaries and asks whether the output outgrew the task.
rows.why: The send checklist repeats the same question, so one owner would do.

rows.name: C# and T-SQL default
rows.does: Assumes C# and T-SQL unless told otherwise.
rows.why: This is a house default a model cannot guess, stated in seven words.

rows.name: Stored-procedure-only data access
rows.does: Routes data access through typed stored procedures under EXECUTE-only principals, with no ad hoc SQL.
rows.why: This is an architectural house rule a model would otherwise violate.

rows.name: House style beats local convention
rows.does: Applies house style over sibling code unless a formatter, .editorconfig or CI lint enforces otherwise.
rows.why: Models default to mimicking sibling code, so this reverses a real default.

rows.name: Surface precedence ranking
rows.does: Ranks the harness, then the operator's live word, positional grants, the doctrine, the owning skill and all else when texts conflict, and files contradictions to kaizen.
rows.why: Some ordering is needed, but conflicts are rare and the six-tier legal construction costs more than the confusion it prevents.

rows.name: Relay message deferred handling
rows.does: Treats an operator relay message found inside a tool result as the operator's word, taken up at turn end after recording it.
rows.why: This concerns one channel setup and belongs in the relay or coordinator skill, not the always-loaded doctrine.

rows.name: Stops need their exceptions
rows.does: Sends the session to the owning document before obeying a stop or grant seen in a summary.
rows.why: This is meta-governance for the kit's own duplication problem, and fixing the duplicates removes the need.

rows.name: Positional authorization, closed grants
rows.does: Accepts authorization only from the operator's word or a named positional form, and lists three standing grants in the doctrine.
rows.why: It restates the precedence ranking and the stop-for-a-yes list, so it should fold into one of them.

rows.name: Ownership map lookup
rows.does: Consults an ownership map naming one owning document per moment, and forbids partial copies of rules.
rows.why: This matters only when authoring kit documents, so it belongs in writing-skills with a pointer here.

rows.name: Pause only for blockers
rows.does: Runs an agreed plan to completion and interrupts only for the closed blocker set, never for capacity.
rows.why: Models do stop early to check in or cite context limits, and this failure costs the operator real time.

rows.name: Consume anchors, strip framing
rows.does: Uses every exact anchor the operator gives as the plan and acceptance check, and discards evaluative framing.
rows.why: Anchoring on framing and skipping supplied measurements are both real failures.

rows.name: Batched decisions with recommendations
rows.does: Asks decisions in rounds with a marked recommendation, treats '(Recommended)' as proceed, and records answers dated in the plan and memory.
rows.why: The recording and binding-recommendation conventions are kit-specific.

rows.name: Intake gap check
rows.does: Lists unstated gaps at intake, then resolves each from a source, decides and declares it, or asks, and surfaces the declared assumptions.
rows.why: It is valuable against silent assumptions, but the three-way triage fits in about 60 words.

rows.name: Client-briefing decision register
rows.does: Writes decision asks for an outsider in a fixed order: situation, decision, stakes, options, recommendation, default, then evidence.
rows.why: Models write jargon-laden asks by default, and this format is the operator's decision interface.

rows.name: Nothing untrue ships
rows.does: Bans invented metrics or claims and sweeps the whole tree for a banned pattern.
rows.why: Fabricated marketing copy is a plausible and high-cost failure, especially for client work.

rows.name: Report altered external state
rows.does: Names changed credentials, databases or other shared state in the close-out.
rows.why: The send checklist repeats it, and the close-out entry could own it.

rows.name: Kaizen friction capture
rows.does: Writes a one-line kaizen inbox note when kit rules cause friction, without asking, and routes project gotchas to memory.
rows.why: This is a kit-defined loop the model cannot know, though it could shrink to about 60 words.

rows.name: Propose before building
rows.does: Reads the files and current docs, raises concerns, and presents a no-code plan before implementing a non-trivial change.
rows.why: Models jump to code, and the operator wants a plan gate.

rows.name: Plan doc as truth
rows.does: Drives non-trivial work through a spec in docs/plans/ executed section by section, with state in the doc.
rows.why: This is the backbone of kit workflow and crash recovery.

rows.name: Curated docs, .kit scratch
rows.does: Puts transient artifacts in a gitignored .kit/ path and keeps docs/ curated.
rows.why: This is a kit convention, short, and prevents repo clutter.

rows.name: Root-cause from real data
rows.does: Confirms causes in files and data, suspects boundary contracts, and retires stale backlog items with receipts.
rows.why: The systematic-debugging skill owns this moment.

rows.name: Section Chapter close
rows.does: Ends each section with a Chapter naming the gating lanes, counts and exit code, and opens a compaction checkpoint when a kit goal is armed.
rows.why: executing-work owns the Chapter format, so a pointer would do.

rows.name: Memory extension pointer
rows.does: Loads the memory-system skill before using outcome logs, stamps, tags, decay, tiers or memq.
rows.why: A pointer is needed, but the feature list duplicates the skill's own description.

rows.name: Durable-artifact recovery
rows.does: Checks git state after an interruption, and after compaction re-reads the plan doc, re-invokes the skill and reloads deferred tools.
rows.why: Models do not reliably reload state after compaction, and the failure derails long runs.

rows.name: Finishing pass pointer
rows.does: Runs the finishing-work skill when all sections are done.
rows.why: This is a short routing pointer to a kit-defined ritual.

rows.name: Plan doc terminal state
rows.does: Flips the plan to Complete, writes the close-out Chapter and archives it in the same delivery as the code, under any commit model.
rows.why: finishing-work and curating-docs own plan finalization.

rows.name: Confirmed/inferred/reported marks
rows.does: Marks each load-bearing claim with its evidence status, and keeps peer claims separate as reported.
rows.why: Models blur verified and assumed claims, and this three-way vocabulary is kit-specific.

rows.name: Cannot measure when down
rows.does: Reports 'cannot measure' instead of substituting a neighboring or stale number when the source is unreachable.
rows.why: Substituting a plausible proxy number is a real and damaging model habit.

rows.name: Run the real thing
rows.does: Runs the artifact on the real input and failing path instead of trusting a build.
rows.why: Premature 'done' on a build or unit test is common.

rows.name: Baseline before claims
rows.does: Records pass/fail counts, failing names and fixture ages before claiming no regressions.
rows.why: Without a baseline, pre-existing failures get misattributed, and models skip this step.

rows.name: Lane schedule by moment
rows.does: Sets which test lane runs after a fix, at section close, finishing, merge or push, including the contention lane, and reports the delta in a fixed form.
rows.why: testing-discipline owns the lanes, and this schedule duplicates it at length in the always-loaded file.

rows.name: Verdict from exit code
rows.does: Reads a pass/fail verdict from the run's own exit code, not from a narrowed grep or a pipe's tail.
rows.why: The `$?`-after-head trap is a real, subtle agent failure.

rows.name: Findings are hypotheses
rows.does: Opens the cited code to check a subagent's, reviewer's or stale note's claim before acting on it.
rows.why: Orchestrators routinely trust a subagent's 'COMPLETE'.

rows.name: Re-ground stale summaries
rows.does: Re-fetches sources read in an earlier turn or session before shipping, and fact-checks the draft.
rows.why: Relying on stale context across compaction is a real failure.

rows.name: Verify external specifics
rows.does: Verifies prices, versions and dates before they appear in forwarded artifacts.
rows.why: Hallucinated figures in client-facing text are high cost.

rows.name: Fix contradicted memory now
rows.does: Corrects a recalled memory contradicted by evidence in the same turn, via the memory-system remedies.
rows.why: The rule is needed, but the remedy detail belongs in memory-system.

rows.name: Green-suite blind spots
rows.does: Budgets a real-browser walk per batch on deployed binaries with cache busted, since mocks miss routing, streaming and overflow.
rows.why: The concrete blind-spot list changes behavior on web work.

rows.name: Red-first regression tests
rows.does: Writes the failing test first, proves the fix both ways, or uses a throwaway repro.
rows.why: Models write tests that pass trivially unless they are told to watch the test go red first.

rows.name: Contract pins and single-sourcing
rows.does: Pins wire fields through the real client, single-sources shared constants, and moves sanitizing guards to the shared boundary.
rows.why: This is testing and design detail that belongs in testing-discipline.

rows.name: Exclusive tree-mutating probes
rows.does: Runs a tree-mutating probe only while no agent reads the tree, and restores from copies, never git checkout.
rows.why: This applies rarely and fits in testing-discipline.

rows.name: Withheld control for silence
rows.does: Proves an absence-check can speak by running it against a known-positive state it was not tuned on, per scope axis and with class coverage.
rows.why: False-clean greps are a real failure, but the two sub-bullets over-elaborate beyond the core rule.

rows.name: Test independence pointer
rows.does: Points to testing-discipline for cost shapes and contention.
rows.why: It is a pure pointer that duplicates the skill's trigger description.

rows.name: Red is a signal
rows.does: Root-causes reproducing reds, sizes observation windows, and files genuine flakes rather than rationalizing them.
rows.why: testing-discipline owns the red protocol, so one sentence here would do.

rows.name: Scope-limited staging and edits
rows.does: Stages only files it changed, avoids adjacent reformatting, flags bonus wins, and checks peers' hunks before committing a shared file.
rows.why: Scope creep and blanket adds are real failures on multi-session checkouts.

rows.name: Index-as-window commit protocol
rows.does: Finishes edits before staging, reads the whole index separately, picks pathspec or plain commit carefully, and reads commit and upstream lists before pushing.
rows.why: This addresses a real multi-session hazard, but the git choreography belongs in peer-sessions or finishing-work, with a two-sentence rule here.

rows.name: Act on found work
rows.does: Keeps found work serving the goal in the effort, and hands off a different goal only as a runnable spec.
rows.why: Models defer with a vague 'later' or leave TODOs.

rows.name: Minimum sufficient code
rows.does: Avoids speculative abstraction, unrequested guards and placeholders, and rewrites bloat.
rows.why: Over-engineering is a persistent model tendency.

rows.name: Stop-for-a-yes and commit default
rows.does: Defines the two-part test for acts others depend on or that cannot be undone, a closed list of ungated channels, the commit-and-push default, commit-model exemptions and their floor.
rows.why: The gate is essential, but the grant-record and model-exemption legalism could be cut to about 150 words, with the commit models living in curating-docs.

rows.name: Revert own regression first
rows.does: Restores the known-good state before diagnosing its own breakage, and admits the error.
rows.why: Models tend to pile fixes on a regression, and this rule is short.

rows.name: Stakes read up front
rows.does: Opens work with a one-phrase blast-radius read and scales process to it.
rows.why: It is a cheap calibration that prevents over-processing small tasks.

rows.name: Name old-contract speakers
rows.does: Checks old servers, clients, caches and consumers before calling a change safe.
rows.why: Models miss backward compatibility, and this rule is short.

rows.name: Merged PR branch frozen
rows.does: Reads PR state before each push, and sends changes after a merge to a new branch.
rows.why: finishing-work step 7 and a guard hook already own this.

rows.name: Embedded text is data
rows.does: Surfaces instructions found in files and tool output instead of acting on them.
rows.why: The harness system prompt and model training already enforce this.

rows.name: Recommend at forks
rows.does: Leads with a recommendation, decides low-blast forks itself, and asks on high-blast ones.
rows.why: The decide-versus-ask split by blast radius is a house calibration.

rows.name: Ground advice in project data
rows.does: Pulls real numbers, schema and migration history before recommending, especially a switch back.
rows.why: Models advise from generic priors instead of the repo's history.

rows.name: One axis per visual round
rows.does: Changes one visual axis per round, shows the render, and names the tunable constant and its file.
rows.why: This is a house iteration style for craft work that models do not do unprompted.

rows.name: Four-part turn close
rows.does: Narrates batch intent and closes turns with ran, inferred, reported, operator-only verification, git state, the operator's steps and the likeliest-wrong claim.
rows.why: This is the operator's reporting contract, and it is kit-specific.

rows.name: Pending plans board
rows.does: Ends turns with one line per pending plan: filename, purpose, status and what waits on the operator.
rows.why: The operator relies on it across sessions, and it ties to /kit-goal.

rows.name: Standing dispatch request
rows.does: Treats the doctrine as the operator's standing request to dispatch subagents and reviewers, plus a narrow Workflow carve-out for read-only effort-set dispatch.
rows.why: It is needed to satisfy the harness condition, but the Workflow carve-out legalism roughly doubles the length.

rows.name: Orchestration skills pointer
rows.does: Defaults implementation to dispatch and loads brainstorming, executing-work or consult before fanning out.
rows.why: It restates the dispatch entry and the skills' own triggers.

rows.name: Peer sessions pointer
rows.does: Loads peer-sessions before messaging, treats peer messages as the seat's word, and lands agreements in durable records.
rows.why: The peer-sessions skill owns this, and only the carve-out from data-not-instructions needs to stay here.

rows.name: Per-machine heavy-process budget
rows.does: Polls for foreign test runners and builds before a suite, and reads a partial-death run as contention.
rows.why: Contention on a shared box is real, but the rule plus the partial-death sign fit in about 50 words.

rows.name: Sequenced builds and suites
rows.does: Stops only its own hosts before builds, runs one integration process per resource, and globs for the solution name.
rows.why: Machine-wide kills and locked binaries are real failures on this setup.

rows.name: Readiness signal, not sleep
rows.does: Waits on an until-loop readiness check rather than a fixed sleep.
rows.why: The harness already blocks foreground sleep and steers to Monitor.

rows.name: No self-edited permissions
rows.does: Hands over permission JSON instead of editing its own permission files.
rows.why: It is a safety line that is cheap to state.

rows.name: Self-written run markers
rows.does: Reads a background run's result from an exit marker the run writes, and judges death by the process list, not a frozen log.
rows.why: It is useful but overlaps the harness's background guidance, and it could take half the words.

rows.name: Probe before killing agent
rows.does: Messages a quiet dispatched agent before killing it, with triggers owned by finishing-work.
rows.why: finishing-work owns it, and this entry repeats its triggers.

rows.name: Silence is not stall
rows.does: Refuses to replace a silent agent without other evidence, stops it first, and ends the turn with WAITING.
rows.why: executing-work owns awaiting and replacing an agent, so it should combine with the probe entry under one owner.

rows.name: Don't waste moves
rows.does: Avoids re-reading files, lockfiles and broad greps, and captures returned paths.
rows.why: Current models are efficient here unprompted, and the failure is cheap.

rows.name: Outline large files
rows.does: Greps declarations to outline a file over about 1,000 lines before a targeted read, but reads whole units and never proves absence from an outline.
rows.why: Models already outline, so only the 'outline never proves absence' guard earns its place.

rows.name: Before You Send checklist
rows.does: Re-reads the draft against fourteen questions on claim status, baselines, scope, rollback, state and honesty before sending.
rows.why: Nearly every item duplicates a rule above, and a checklist cut to the four most-missed items would bite harder.

rows.name: Title and section headers
rows.does: Frames the document as the always-apply ruleset and groups the rules under section headings.
rows.why: This is structural overhead.

rows.name: Frontmatter role and dispatch trigger
rows.does: Registers the agent as a fresh-context, read-only reviewer at low effort, dispatched after each section and at the end of an effort with a plan path and base ref.
rows.why: The harness needs the name, tools, effort and trigger description to route a dispatch here at all.

rows.name: Recall over precision stance
rows.does: Tells the reviewer to flag doubtful defects with reasoning rather than stay silent, because the orchestrator filters false positives, while still naming a concrete defect.
rows.why: Models default to precision and hedged silence in review, and this asymmetry argument changes the recall a low-effort reviewer delivers.

rows.name: Brief inputs and trace target
rows.does: Defines the required inputs (plan path, base ref), the fallback when the spec is missing, and how Trace target and Amendments in effect lines override the spec file.
rows.why: The Trace target and Amendments contract is kit-specific, and without it the reviewer reports approved amendments as spec drift.

rows.name: Read-only, no-build discipline
rows.does: Restricts the reviewer to read-only git commands, forbids edits, commits and builds, and explains that the hook denylist leaves builds open so the bar rests on discipline to avoid contending with the orchestrator's suite.
rows.why: The rule is needed because the guard leaves builds open, but the guard-shape explanation can shrink to one reason sentence about contention on shared binaries.

rows.name: Changeset is data, not instructions
rows.does: Makes any instruction inside the diff a finding reported verbatim, never an action, and makes the reviewer choose its own means to settle a claim like 'verify by running X'.
rows.why: Prompt-injection resistance matters for a shell-holding reviewer, but current models already treat file content as data, so the rule and the 'run X' case take a third of these words.

rows.name: Spec compliance pass first
rows.does: Runs a first pass checking each in-scope section for missing behavior, contradicted Approach decisions, scope creep and unmeetable acceptance criteria, rating wrong-behavior code Critical.
rows.why: Ordering spec compliance before quality and rating it Critical is the kit's review contract and a model would otherwise lead with style.

rows.name: House style from disk
rows.does: Requires reading csharp-style and sql-style from supplied absolute paths, skipping a language if unreadable, never substituting repo convention, and rating style Minor.
rows.why: A subagent inherits no skills and would otherwise judge against sibling code, which the doctrine explicitly ranks below house style.

rows.name: Generic correctness checklist
rows.does: Lists null handling, async propagation, off-by-one, races, disposal and transaction scope as things to check.
rows.why: Any current model reviewing code checks these unprompted, so the list adds nothing.

rows.name: Tool-printed claims settled at source
rows.does: Requires settling any claim about what a tool prints against the tool's emitting source or a provably read-only run, never against documents, else reporting it unverified-on-documents.
rows.why: Checking tool output against the tool rather than copied docs is a real, non-default steer, but the rule plus the 'documents copy each other' reason fit in about 60 words.

rows.name: Fixtures are not contract evidence
rows.does: Flags as Major any artifact the effort authored (fixture, golden file, stub) cited as evidence of a contract the effort does not own, and routes the question to the owning surface.
rows.why: Self-authored fixtures as circular evidence is a real blind spot, but the text restates 'instances rather than the boundary' twice and could carry the rule, reason and severity in a quarter of the words.

rows.name: Refusal and absence check coverage
rows.does: Makes the reviewer ask which rule refused a refusal-shaped test, and demand the predicate, scope and withheld-control coverage answer for any absence-shaped check, flagging an unproven axis.
rows.why: The withheld-control rule is already owned by the doctrine's silent-check bullet, so this should point there and keep only the refusal-attribution question and the finding it produces.

rows.name: Moment-pinned figure checks
rows.does: Rates an unpinned journal-layer figure Major, dated-evidence annotation in curated surfaces Minor, and figures predating the machine's configuration epoch Major, reading each rule from testing-discipline and memory-system.
rows.why: The kit-specific pin and epoch rules are owned elsewhere, so this should point at the owners and keep the three severities, not restate their boundaries and fallbacks.

rows.name: Error handling checklist
rows.does: Lists swallowed exceptions, missing T-SQL CATCH auditing, inconsistent error-path state and unjustified empty catches as defects.
rows.why: Everything except the house-specific T-SQL CATCH auditing is default reviewer behavior, and that item is already owned by sql-style.

rows.name: Test worthiness and retire classes
rows.does: Judges missing or bad tests against testing-discipline's earn litmus, flags retire-class tests with fixed severities, requires the pin-on-a-choice finding to name a red-turning edit and the checks it ran, and protects control legs.
rows.why: The rule set is kit-specific and matters, but it restates much of testing-discipline's retire classes and exemptions that it says to point at, and could keep the severities and the pin-on-a-choice proof burden in about 200 words.

rows.name: Robustness and guard reachability
rows.does: Checks idempotency, empty-input behavior, boundary guards, and whether a new path bypasses a guard another file enforces.
rows.why: The generic items are default, but the cross-file guard-bypass question is a cheap non-default check worth its few words.

rows.name: Paragraph-justified workaround smell
rows.does: Flags a workaround that needs a paragraph-long comment and names what the code should do instead.
rows.why: It is a short, distinctive house heuristic a model would not apply unprompted.

rows.name: Performance flag-on-the-way scope
rows.does: Flags N+1, missing indexes, hot-path allocation and chatty round-trips with evidence, leaving the deep pass to performance-reviewer.
rows.why: The scope boundary with the performance-reviewer is needed, but the generic list and the lens enumeration can go.

rows.name: Security flag and folded lenses
rows.does: Rates security defects seen on the way, defers the deep pass to security-reviewer, and when the brief folds advisory lenses in, runs them with their required threat, requirement and evidence fields and a Disclosure sweep printed as Critical.
rows.why: The combined-pass output contract and the Disclosure Critical-without-threat rule are kit-specific and would be printed wrong without the text.

rows.name: Debris checklist
rows.does: Flags dead code, stale TODOs, debug output and orphaned files.
rows.why: Current models flag debris in review unprompted.

rows.name: Finding line format
rows.does: Fixes a severity-ranked, one-line finding format with severity, optional claim token, trace, confidence, file:line, what, why and fix, with no praise or diff restating.
rows.why: The orchestrator parses this exact shape, and a model cannot guess it.

rows.name: Trace field semantics
rows.does: Requires trace on every Critical and Major, defines trace none versus unsupplied, and rules that a defect in requested code traces to its bullet.
rows.why: The trace vocabulary drives adjudication and a model would otherwise misuse none versus unsupplied.

rows.name: Claim versus behavior finding class
rows.does: Defines claim findings as sentence-only fixes rated Minor unless a published-contract delta contradicts a trace clause or leaves a dangling pointer, marked with the [claim] token.
rows.why: The class is a kit-specific severity rule, but it is stated three times (line 59, the pinned region, the Minor ladder) and the pinned block should be the one owner.

rows.name: Confidence independent of severity
rows.does: Defines high, medium and low confidence and forbids downgrading severity to hedge low confidence.
rows.why: Models commonly fold uncertainty into lower severity, and the separation matters to adjudication.

rows.name: Severity ladder definitions
rows.does: Defines Critical as blocking, Major as fix-or-justify with a named failing input, and Minor as note-and-move-on.
rows.why: The blocking semantics per severity are the kit's contract with the orchestrator.

rows.name: Verdict line and honesty
rows.does: Ends with a fixed VERDICT token and one sentence, says exactly nothing when nothing was found, and forbids invented or softened findings.
rows.why: The verdict token is parsed, and the no-invention line is cheap insurance for a recall-biased reviewer.

rows.name: Adversarial on-disk framing
rows.does: Casts the session as an adversarial reviewer of what is actually on disk rather than intended.
rows.why: It is a one-line role setter that anchors the reviewer on real state at trivial cost.

rows.name: Dispatch description for blind review
rows.does: The frontmatter tells an orchestrator when to dispatch this agent, what to pass (document paths only) and what comes back.
rows.why: This is the routing contract. Without it the orchestrator cannot dispatch correctly or know what the agent returns.

rows.name: Blind reader role framing
rows.does: Casts the session as an outside reader who reports the experience of reading, not a defect hunter, and explains why the intent story must be absent.
rows.why: A model defaults to reviewer mode and hunts defects, so it needs this role framing, and the reason is stated in two sentences.

rows.name: Contamination test for dispatch framing
rows.does: Makes the session tell standing repository facts from intent framing by asking whether a sentence would read the same for every document. It then ignores and flags framing, and treats a spec or plan handed as the subject as legitimate.
rows.why: The test is kit-specific and needed. But the passes and fails lists, the spec-as-subject carve-out and the cost-of-a-round remark take about twice the words that the rule plus one example would.

rows.name: Read-only commands, no builds
rows.does: Restricts the session to read-only commands, bars edits, commits and builds, and has it report a denied command rather than work around it.
rows.why: The rule and the reason not to route around a denial are needed. The explanation of how the hook works and the shared-binary contention detail can go down to one clause.

rows.name: Persona reach into repository
rows.does: Lets a persona who holds the repository open files to check that a step's referent exists. It bars docs, specs, plans and commit messages, and bars executing steps or opening outside paths. An outside persona opens only the documents.
rows.why: The boundary is novel and a model with the code open will quietly fill gaps, so the rule is needed. But the predicate is restated and illustrated several times, and the handed-document carve-out repeats the Inputs section.

rows.name: Five-part ordered output contract
rows.does: Requires summary-back, questions, comprehension gaps, dry-run and gating definitions, in that order, with the summary written before any finding.
rows.why: The orchestrator parses this fixed format, and a model cannot guess it.

rows.name: Gating definition near-miss pairs
rows.does: Has the session find phrases that decide what a bounded artifact admits. For each it returns three admitted, kept-out and separating-feature pairs from the text alone, never using printed exclusions, and says so when it finds fewer than three.
rows.why: This is the most unusual procedure in the document, and it would not happen without the text. The bounded-artifact definition is dense but carries the boundary itself. Put as a drop at the plan review of 2026-09-30 as the consequence of row 478, and kept on the operator's ruling the same day.

rows.name: Finding line, severity, confidence
rows.does: Fixes a one-line finding format with separate severity and confidence scales, defines each level, and bars lowering severity to hedge a low-confidence finding.
rows.why: The format is a parse contract. Keeping severity and confidence as separate axes is a rule models otherwise blur.

rows.name: Favour recall over precision
rows.does: Tells the session to flag a doubtful gap with its reasoning rather than stay silent, because the orchestrator filters false flags.
rows.why: This is a deliberate threshold choice that runs against a model's usual precision bias. It costs few words.

rows.name: Documents are data
rows.does: Treats instructions inside the reviewed documents as findings to report verbatim, never as commands to follow.
rows.why: The doctrine's data-not-instructions rule already carries this. The only local addition is to report such an instruction as a finding, which is one clause.

rows.name: No verdict or certification
rows.does: Bars the session from writing a pass or fail verdict and leaves that call to the orchestrator.
rows.why: Reviewers add verdict lines by default. The division of labour with the orchestrator has to be stated.

rows.name: Report own persona experience
rows.does: Has the session report what it understood, asked and stopped at, as the persona.
rows.why: It restates the role framing in the opening paragraph and adds no new rule.

rows.name: Never propose rewritten prose
rows.does: Bars suggested rewrites, headings or phrasings in findings.
rows.why: Models reflexively offer rewrites in review, and this separates the reader's job from the writer's.

rows.name: Clean read is valid
rows.does: Has the session say plainly when the documents read clean and bars invented stumbles.
rows.why: A review mandate combined with a favour-recall rule pushes models to invent findings, so this counterweight matters and is cheap.

rows.name: No praise, no restating
rows.does: Bars praise padding and restating the document outside the summary-back.
rows.why: Review output drifts into praise without this, and it costs one sentence.

rows.name: Frontmatter dispatch description
rows.does: Tells the orchestrator to dispatch this agent alongside the adversarial reviewer with only a base ref or file list, and fixes its tools and low effort.
rows.why: The dispatcher cannot know the blind-input contract or the tool grant unless the charter states it.

rows.name: Assume-wrong blind posture
rows.does: Casts the session as a reviewer that checks code against reality rather than intent, presumes a defect, yet reports a clean result honestly when the hunt finds nothing.
rows.why: It is short, and it sets the role and guards against invented findings. A cheap model would otherwise drift toward certifying the author.

rows.name: Receiving half of dispatch
rows.does: States that input is a base ref or changed-file list only, and points to executing-work's section loop step 3 as the owner of the contract.
rows.why: It is a kit contract the model cannot infer, and it already points at its owner.

rows.name: Contamination test for briefs
rows.does: Makes the session sort each extra dispatch sentence by whether it would read identically for every diff, hunting standing properties and ignoring and reporting per-change intent or spec paths.
rows.why: The test is a real kit mechanism worth keeping. But the rule, one example per side and the note-it instruction fit in about a third of these words.

rows.name: Keep away from intent sources
rows.does: Forbids opening docs/, specs, commit messages or .kit/, and has the session scope diffs with an exclude pathspec while reading touched files and callers in full.
rows.why: Blindness is the point of the lens. A model left alone would read commit messages and docs, and no guard stops it.

rows.name: Read-only, no builds or tests
rows.does: Restricts the session to read-only commands, bans its own builds and test runs because they contend with the orchestrator's suite, and says to report a denial rather than route around it.
rows.why: The rule matters because the hook leaves builds open. The hook-mechanics explanation can shrink to one reason sentence.

rows.name: Recall over precision
rows.does: Has the session flag borderline defects with reasoning rather than stay silent, since the orchestrator filters false positives, while still naming a concrete failure mode.
rows.why: It is a house threshold that runs against a model's instinct to self-censor at low effort, and a miss is not caught downstream.

rows.name: Long-justification-comment heuristic
rows.does: Treats a workaround needing a paragraph-long justifying comment as wrong code to be flagged with a replacement.
rows.why: It is a style-adjacent rule of thumb that clashes with the no-style scope. The recall rule already covers flagging a dubious workaround on its merits.

rows.name: Correctness defect-class catalog
rows.does: Lists the defect classes to hunt: resource lifetime, async ordering, numeric boundaries, evaluation semantics, error paths and edge inputs.
rows.why: A current model knows these classes. A one-line list of headings keeps the altitude steer without the textbook examples.

rows.name: Prose and config equivalents
rows.does: Redirects the hunt for prose or configuration diffs to contradictory rules, unexecutable instructions, dangling references, divergent copies and unobservable predicates.
rows.why: Much of this kit's diffs are prose, and a model would not map correctness review onto them unprompted.

rows.name: Out of scope: style, spec
rows.does: Excludes style and spec-compliance review, says to flag danger rather than guess intent, and carves test titles and because-strings back in as [claim] findings.
rows.why: Without it a reviewer drifts into style nits and intent-guessing, which duplicates the sighted lens.

rows.name: Finding line format
rows.does: Fixes the severity-ranked single-line finding shape with severity, optional [claim], confidence, file:line, failure mode and a one-line fix, with no praise or diff restatement.
rows.why: The orchestrator parses and adjudicates these lines, so the shape is a contract.

rows.name: Claim-class parity block
rows.does: Defines behavior versus claim findings and the published-surface exception, covering the acceptance-trace case and the dangling-pointer case, plus the downgrade recording.
rows.why: It is a parity-pinned copy of a rule another document owns. Half of it, the trace case and the Chapter recording, is orchestrator-side and unusable by a lens that cannot see the plan, so a pointer plus the pointer-case sentence would serve.

rows.name: Claim rating for blind lens
rows.does: Tells the session it can raise only the dangling-pointer case above Minor, rates every other [claim] Minor, and routes an unstated boundary to a [claim] rather than a test-pin Minor.
rows.why: The blind-lens rule reduces to three sentences. The current text repeats the parity block and threads the requirement-surface list through the Minor definition hard enough that a low-tier model will misapply it.

rows.name: Confidence independent of severity
rows.does: Defines the high, medium and low confidence levels and bars downgrading severity to hedge uncertainty.
rows.why: Models do conflate the two by hedging severity, and the orchestrator weighs both separately.

rows.name: Severity definitions
rows.does: Defines Critical as blocking, Major as fix-or-justify and Minor as a note, each with the kind of defect that earns it.
rows.why: Severity drives the section gate, so its boundaries must match the orchestrator's.

rows.name: Verdict line
rows.does: Ends the output with a fixed VERDICT token and one sentence of reasoning.
rows.why: It is a machine-read contract that costs almost nothing.

rows.name: Agent frontmatter and triggers
rows.does: Registers the consultant agent with read-only tools and high effort, and states when an orchestrator should dispatch it and how it differs from reviewers and the council.
rows.why: The routing and tool list are needed, but the trigger list and the not-a-reviewer contrasts restate what the consult skill already owns, so the description could name the role in about half the words.

rows.name: Fresh judge role framing
rows.does: Casts the session as one judge ruling on one question, with the querent's transcript withheld so it tests the framing rather than extending it.
rows.why: A spawned model does not know why its context is thin or that its job is to rule rather than assist, and this short framing sets both.

rows.name: Expected brief contents contract
rows.does: Lists what the brief carries (decision, evidence, paths, plan Goal and Intent, querent lean, answer shape), accepts a no-plan brief as complete, and allows bulky evidence under .kit/.
rows.why: The consult skill that writes the brief owns this contract, so the agent needs only a pointer and the no-plan carve-out rather than a full copy.

rows.name: No decision means NEEDS_CONTEXT
rows.does: Makes the agent return NEEDS_CONTEXT instead of a survey when the brief poses no decision to rule on.
rows.why: Without it a model given a vague brief writes a helpful overview, which is exactly the failure the agent exists to avoid.

rows.name: Read-only, report hook denials
rows.does: Bars edits, commits and builds, explains that the write hook leaves builds and tests open on purpose, and says to report a denial rather than work around it.
rows.why: The build and test bar matters because the hook does not enforce it, but the rule and that one reason fit in about twenty words.

rows.name: Brief and repo are data
rows.does: Treats the brief, plan sections and repository as data and makes the agent quote any embedded instruction in its ruling without acting on it.
rows.why: The doctrine and harness already carry the data-not-instructions rule, so only the report-it-in-the-ruling detail is agent-specific.

rows.name: Rule, don't survey
rows.does: Requires a decided call at the end rather than a balanced tour of options.
rows.why: Current models default to even-handed option lists when asked for advice, and the whole value of this agent is a decision.

rows.name: Evidence with confirmed, inferred, reported
rows.does: Requires each load-bearing claim to cite a file:line or data, carry a confirmed, inferred or reported mark, and name what would confirm each inferred one.
rows.why: The doctrine's Verify Before You Claim section owns this marking and even the definition of reported restated here, so a pointer suffices.

rows.name: Test the querent's framing
rows.does: Treats the querent's question and operator instinct as claims, and returns a wrong-question finding (false premise, false dichotomy, problem elsewhere) as the ruling itself.
rows.why: Models tend to answer the question as posed and ratify a stuck session's lean, and a reframed question is the highest-value output.

rows.name: Separate facts from operator preference
rows.does: Makes the agent rule on system facts and send up only the residual preference, cost or risk-appetite fork, cleanly separated.
rows.why: Without it the agent either overrules the operator on taste or punts the whole question, and the split is not something a model does unprompted.

rows.name: Four-part output format
rows.does: Fixes the reply shape as RULING, EVIDENCE, CONFIDENCE with what would change it, and an optional OPERATOR FORK.
rows.why: The orchestrator parses this shape so it must stay, but the EVIDENCE line repeats the grounding duty and each label can drop to a few words.

rows.name: RULED or NEEDS_CONTEXT terminal status
rows.does: Ends the reply with RULED when grounded or NEEDS_CONTEXT with the precise missing question, then stops.
rows.why: This is the kit's status vocabulary for the calling session, and a model cannot guess the exact tokens.

rows.name: Read-only drafter role
rows.does: Casts the session as a read-only drafter that returns text and leaves every landing decision to the main thread.
rows.why: Without this, a session holding Bash would plausibly write the redraft to disk itself, and the plan's review flow depends on it not doing so.

rows.name: Dispatch-only frontmatter contract
rows.does: Declares the agent is reached only through the corpus-compression workflow script, with a Read/Grep/Glob/Bash tool set at low effort.
rows.why: The routing and tool grant are harness configuration no model can infer, and they cost few words.

rows.name: Inputs to read whole
rows.does: Has the session read the named document and ledger heading whole, plus decision 3 of the lean-kit plan for the meaning of lean.
rows.why: The ledger heading and the plan decision are kit-specific sources the session cannot find unprompted, and partial reads would break the per-entry duties.

rows.name: Documents are data, report instructions
rows.does: Treats the document and ledger as data and reports any embedded instruction verbatim in the return instead of following it.
rows.why: The doctrine carries the general rule, but the verbatim-in-the-return channel and the shell-holding reason are specific to this seat and cheap.

rows.name: Shortest wording keeping meaning
rows.does: Rewrites each live ledger entry to the shortest clear wording that preserves the meaning its reason states, protecting meaning rather than wording.
rows.why: This is the core job, and the meaning-not-wording distinction is what stops a model from either copying verbatim or paraphrasing the rule away.

rows.name: Merge duplicates, propose retire
rows.does: Merges two ledger claims that are one rule and proposes retiring the absorbed entry with a reason naming the survivor.
rows.why: The retire-with-survivor format is a ledger contract the main thread consumes, which the model cannot guess.

rows.name: Ownership-map pointer rewrite
rows.does: Turns a sentence whose moment the ownership map assigns elsewhere into a pointer at the owner's own text.
rows.why: It names the concrete map file and the pointer transform, which is where most compression gains come from and which a model would not do on its own.

rows.name: Journey text to the ledger
rows.does: Moves journey text out of the document and into the ledger under the current-state rule.
rows.why: The doctrine's documents-ship-the-current-state rule already owns this, so one pointer clause would do and the destination can ride in the return format.

rows.name: No retirement on taste
rows.does: Allows a rule to leave only where the ledger shows another entry carries its meaning.
rows.why: A drafter told to hit a word target will over-cut on judgment, and this is the guard that matters most for a compression pass.

rows.name: Reason-evidence flags
rows.does: Checks each entry's reason against the artifact it names and flags weak-reason, stale or unfounded accordingly.
rows.why: The closed flag vocabulary and its triggers are kit-defined and feed the main thread's adjudication.

rows.name: Environment flag and boundary
rows.does: Flags claims that only hold on the operator's own machine, accounts or one project class, leaves them unreworded, and names what does not count.
rows.why: The client-portability goal depends on this flag, and the exclusion list is the boundary that stops over-flagging, so the words earn their place.

rows.name: Closed flag set, no taste flags
rows.does: Declares the four flags a closed set and forbids flagging on taste.
rows.why: The no-taste clause repeats the retire-on-taste duty, so it should fold into that one entry.

rows.name: Two-block return format
rows.does: Returns the whole proposed document, then one entry per live ledger id with a verbatim passage quote, any flag with a reason, merge retires, and a word count against target.
rows.why: The workflow script parses this shape, and no model could produce it without the spec.

rows.name: Council member dispatch description
rows.does: The frontmatter tells the dispatcher that this read-only agent evaluates competing approaches at a fork, one per lens, and that it is not a diff reviewer.
rows.why: Routing depends on this text, and the line separating it from adversarial-reviewer prevents a misdispatch.

rows.name: Stake-free lens stance
rows.does: It frames the session as one lens with no stake in any approach, arguing from evidence rather than to please.
rows.why: This is the role definition in two sentences and costs little.

rows.name: Inherited brief contents list
rows.does: It lists what the orchestrator's brief carries in round 1 and in later rounds.
rows.why: The session reads its brief anyway, so only the fact that later rounds add the prior positions and the facilitator's question needs stating.

rows.name: Missing input stops with NEEDS_CONTEXT
rows.does: If the outcome or the lens is missing, the session reports NEEDS_CONTEXT and stops.
rows.why: The closing status line restates the same stop, so one statement would do.

rows.name: Read-only with hook denial
rows.does: It limits the session to read-only commands with no edit, commit or build, and it says to report a hook denial rather than route around it.
rows.why: The hook leaves builds open, so this text is the only bar on building, and a model will otherwise try to work around a denied command.

rows.name: Blind first round rationale
rows.does: It explains that the member cannot see the others in round 1 because an unanchored view is the point.
rows.why: The orchestrator enforces blindness by construction, and the member has nothing to act on here.

rows.name: Read real system first
rows.does: It makes the session read the named files, schema, data and their siblings before arguing, and never argue from an imagined architecture.
rows.why: Design debates drift into abstraction without it, and the rule is short.

rows.name: Evidence-marked position
rows.does: It makes the session recommend one approach, or a better one, and ground each claim in a file:line or schema object marked confirmed, inferred or reported.
rows.why: The re-definition of reported duplicates the doctrine it already points to.

rows.name: Specific objection per alternative
rows.does: It makes the session name how each alternative fails the outcome through its lens, with evidence, and never as a generic worry.
rows.why: Without it, objections come out generic and the council loses its value.

rows.name: Concede, rebut or revise
rows.does: It requires exactly one of concede, rebut with evidence, or revise for each objection raised against the member's position.
rows.why: This contract is what makes cross-examination rounds converge or expose a real fork.

rows.name: Answer facilitator question directly
rows.does: It makes the session answer the question the facilitator put to it.
rows.why: It is six words that tie the round to the facilitator's steer.

rows.name: Change mind only on evidence
rows.does: It bars the session from capitulating to please and from digging in once the evidence turns, and it calls an uncited capitulation worse than disagreement.
rows.why: Sycophantic convergence in multi-agent debate is a real failure, but the same point is made in three places and one rule with one reason would carry it.

rows.name: Never invent or soften disagreement
rows.does: It bars fabricating disagreement to look rigorous and softening a real one to please.
rows.why: It restates the change-mind-only-on-evidence entry.

rows.name: Position and objection output format
rows.does: It fixes the output sections as POSITION, OBJECTIONS and, in later rounds, CONCEDED / HELD with reasons.
rows.why: The facilitator synthesizes across members, so it needs this shape.

rows.name: READY or NEEDS_CONTEXT status
rows.does: It makes the session end with READY, or with NEEDS_CONTEXT and the precise question that blocks it.
rows.why: The orchestrator parses this terminal status, and a model cannot guess the vocabulary.

rows.name: Frontmatter dispatch description
rows.does: Tells the orchestrating session when and why to dispatch this agent, and pins its tools to Read, Grep, Glob, Bash on the opus model.
rows.why: The harness needs a description to route the dispatch, but it restates the whole body; one sentence naming the role and the fact that it owns the convergence verdict would do.

rows.name: Neutral judge owning verdict
rows.does: Makes the session hold no position, never advocate, and own the convergence verdict instead of the orchestrator.
rows.why: The separation of verdict from orchestrator is the kit's reason this agent exists, and a model cannot infer it.

rows.name: Brief inputs from orchestrator
rows.does: States that the session receives the outcome, candidate approaches and every member's output for the round.
rows.why: It is the input contract with the design-council skill, cheap and not inferable.

rows.name: Read-only, no builds
rows.does: Lets the session read the real system to weigh claims but forbids edits, commits and builds, explains the hook that denies writes, and says to report a denial rather than route around it.
rows.why: The build ban is needed because the hook leaves builds open, but the hook explanation and the denial-handling sentence duplicate the read-only guard contract every read-only agent carries and could be one sentence plus a pointer.

rows.name: Agreement and disagreement map
rows.does: Makes each round's output list what every lens accepts with its evidence, and each live disagreement attributed to its lenses as a concrete dispute.
rows.why: It is the output format the orchestrator parses, and attribution to lenses is not something a model does by default.

rows.name: Factual versus value crux
rows.does: Makes the session name, for each disagreement, the one factual or value question that settles it, with factual cruxes going to another round and value cruxes to the operator.
rows.why: The factual/value split drives the stop logic and the escalation to the operator; without it the agent would keep debating value trade-offs.

rows.name: Evidence-resolved versus soft agreement
rows.does: Makes the session classify each agreed point as evidence-resolved or soft capitulation and push soft agreement back to its crux.
rows.why: Sycophantic capitulation between model-played lenses is a real failure, and this label is the kit's check against it.

rows.name: Three-status stop logic
rows.does: Makes each round end with exactly one of CONVERGED, ANOTHER_ROUND or DEADLOCK, each with its entry conditions and required payload (synthesis, targeted questions, or side-by-side positions).
rows.why: The status vocabulary and payloads are the contract the design-council loop branches on; a model cannot invent them and the words spent are proportionate.

rows.name: Distrust instant round-one consensus
rows.does: Makes the session treat a CONVERGED after Round 1 as suspect because correlated models agree easily, and verify it against evidence before signing.
rows.why: Correlated-model agreement is a failure a 5-family model will not guard against unprompted, and the rule is short.

rows.name: No manufactured convergence or dispute
rows.does: Tells the session never to fake convergence to close cleanly or invent a dispute to look rigorous.
rows.why: The convergence half is already carried by the soft-agreement entry and the Round 1 check, and the invented-dispute half is an implausible failure, so it folds into those entries.

rows.name: Agent frontmatter and dispatch description
rows.does: Registers the docs-curator agent with its tools, model, effort and the moment it is dispatched with a plan path.
rows.why: The harness needs it to route and scope the agent, and no model can infer it.

rows.name: Document as-built code from disk
rows.does: Makes the agent describe what the code does now, tracing inputs, outputs, side effects, errors and persistence, rather than what the spec promised.
rows.why: This is the agent's thesis, and a docs writer handed a spec drifts toward restating it, so it earns the few words it takes.

rows.name: Read spec and docs first
rows.does: Requires reading the plan with its Chapters and the existing docs tree before any write.
rows.why: A current model reads before writing unprompted, and the only kit-specific part is 'including its Chapters', which takes a clause.

rows.name: Write scope limited to docs
rows.does: Restricts writes to docs/, bars editing the plan file or any plan header, and bars touching a leftover docs/coordinator-board.md.
rows.why: The docs-only and no-plan-edit bounds matter, but the coordinator-board line is a one-off legacy carve-out that could be one clause or dropped once the file is gone.

rows.name: Load prose-register from given path
rows.does: Makes the agent read the prose-register skill and its references from the absolute path in the dispatch, report if unreadable, and fall back to the doctrine's register bullets.
rows.why: A subagent inherits no skills, so without this it writes in its default register, and the fallback rule is not guessable.

rows.name: Update docs in place
rows.does: Edits existing docs rather than forking parallel copies and preserves history sections.
rows.why: Cheap, and forking a v2 doc is a real failure for a docs-writing agent.

rows.name: docs-write-guard hook explanation
rows.does: Explains which agent types the write guard admits and that a dispatch under another type writes to .kit/ and returns content for the orchestrator to land.
rows.why: The agent running under its own type never hits the fallback, so this belongs to the dispatching skill (finishing-work or executing-work) that picks the agent type.

rows.name: Living docs update rules
rows.does: Creates or updates docs/architecture.md, updates other root about-the-solution docs without creating absent ones, fixes falsified claims anywhere in docs/, flags pre-existing drift, and writes feature docs a handoff reader can operate from.
rows.why: The create-versus-update split and 'flag, do not rewrite, older drift' are house choices a model would get wrong, though the prose could tighten a little.

rows.name: Report drift, never reconcile silently
rows.does: Makes the agent report every material disagreement among spec, code and docs and leave the verdict to the operator.
rows.why: A capable model's instinct is to quietly harmonize the docs, and silent reconciliation hides decisions the operator must make.

rows.name: Sweep by claim categories
rows.does: Directs a whole-library grep for each falsified claim, with counts, exclusivity claims, justifications and renamed identifiers as the high-yield categories.
rows.why: Models sweep by changed file by default and miss repeated counts and 'only' claims elsewhere, which is the main way docs rot.

rows.name: Four spelling-pass hunt protocol
rows.does: Prescribes an unanchored digit/number-word pass, an anchored pass near the set name, an only/sole/single/unique pass, and a never/nothing/negation pass, plus new passes for new spellings.
rows.why: The pass list is useful but the prose re-explains why each pass exists; a four-line list of the search terms with one reason would carry it at about a third of the words.

rows.name: Clean versus class-not vocabulary
rows.does: Makes a pass report 'clean' only when keyed on a structural pattern or complete enumeration, and 'named members swept, class not' otherwise.
rows.why: The doctrine's silent-check bullet already owns this coverage rule, so the charter needs only the token and a pointer.

rows.name: Library hygiene flagging
rows.does: Flags Complete-but-unarchived plans and missing cross-references read-only, allows refreshing docs/README.md, and bars moving plans.
rows.why: The flag-not-move split with curating-docs is a kit contract the agent cannot infer.

rows.name: Output report template
rows.does: Fixes the DOCS UPDATED, CLAIMS SWEPT, DRIFT REPORT and LIBRARY HYGIENE blocks with required fields, NONE/CLEAN forms and per-entry Basis, Paths and Class lines.
rows.why: finishing-work parses this so the format must stay, but the three near-duplicate CLAIMS SWEPT template lines restate the pass rules already given and could collapse to one.

rows.name: No drift markers in docs
rows.does: Keeps drift only in the report, bars writing drift or adjudication comments into shipped docs, and requires file:line citations in the entry.
rows.why: Leaving '<!-- DRIFT -->' notes in docs is a plausible model habit and violates the current-state-only house rule.

rows.name: Mistake versus deviation classification
rows.does: Requires classing each drift item as mistake or deviation without hedging, with the reason for a mistake in Impact, because finishing-work stops on mistakes.
rows.why: The class drives a downstream stop, and models hedge classifications unless told the call is load-bearing.

rows.name: Absent basis slot forms
rows.does: Makes the agent write 'spec silent', 'no code passage' or 'docs absent' rather than inventing a citation.
rows.why: The fixed absent tokens are needed, but the rationale paragraph runs longer than the rule; current models rarely fabricate a citation once an absent form is offered.

rows.name: Pre-change verbatim marker
rows.does: Requires the exact string 'pre-change state not read (this charter grants no Bash)' on any claim about the base-ref state, including on standalone dispatches.
rows.why: The exact-string contract with finishing-work is essential, but the class explanation and the standalone-dispatch paragraph restate things finishing-work owns, which the charter already admits.

rows.name: Forward-slash Paths line
rows.does: Requires every path the claim concerns as repo-root-relative, forward-slashed and whitespace-separated, with no command in the basis line.
rows.why: On Windows a model will emit backslashes, and the machine match in finishing-work stops the run on them.

rows.name: Agent frontmatter and dispatch description

rows.name: Outline large files before hunting

rows.why: Scope creep is a real, frequent failure in a high-effort top-tier model, and the list is short.

rows.name: Build and targeted tests with evidence

rows.why: Evidence-backed done claims are the core output contract, though current models mostly do this.

rows.does: Makes the agent keep long gates in its own turn by backgrounding at the shell and polling with an until loop, never using run_in_background, and lists red-flag phrases.
rows.why: The harness fact that run_in_background ends the turn is non-obvious and the failure is real, but the rule, reason and one red-flag example would take about half the words.

rows.name: Durable test or stated reason
rows.does: Has the agent leave a durable test watched red then green where earned, or say why not, and keep repro scripts out of the new behavior's home.

rows.name: No outline, oversize sibling escalates

rows.why: The doctrine's current-state rule and the style skills already own this, and the implementer is told to read those skills.

rows.why: The agent holds Bash, and a denied model does try workarounds; the .kit/ carve-out and probe-runner name are kit facts.

rows.name: Closed eight-question tag set
rows.does: Restricts findings to eight tagged questions with one tag each and drops any defect fitting none.
rows.why: The closed set is what keeps this reviewer distinct from the others and makes output parseable; a model cannot invent it.

rows.name: Unwanted-satisfaction and two-way questions
rows.does: Flags acceptance criteria an unwanted reading or no run would satisfy, and sentences a sonnet-tier implementer could read two ways, stating both readings.
rows.why: These are the core gap-finding lenses and are compact already.

rows.name: Falsified-surface question
rows.does: Flags files, docs, tests or pinned copies outside every scope list that the change would make false, found by reading the repository.
rows.why: This is the finding models most miss without being pointed at the tree, and it is stated tightly.

rows.name: Rule-conflict and handoff questions
rows.does: Flags instructions contradicting a loaded doctrine or skill rule by bold lead, and section-to-section assumptions or orderings the acceptance does not guarantee.
rows.why: Both are specific lenses with kit-specific citation form, short enough as written.

rows.name: Preference-as-ruling question
rows.does: Flags a Decision, Assumption or Intent clause that records the author's pick in the operator's voice or settles a call the operator would want.
rows.why: Guards a real authorship failure a model would not look for untold, in few words.

rows.name: Machinery question
rows.does: Flags a section with no line saying what the operator does with it and sees, requiring the reviewer to attempt that line and quote where it broke.
rows.why: A distinctive kit lens against operator-invisible work; compact.

rows.name: Unrefusable-frame question
rows.does: Flags an Intent record whose not-done half refuses no plausible mechanism, a record past the brainstorming size bound, or a missing Intent, with byte count or anchor evidence.
rows.why: The rule is needed, but carve-outs for appended rulings, empty refused alternatives and per-subcase evidence formats cost twice what the rule and a reason take.

rows.name: Three-level severity scale
rows.does: Rates findings Critical if the Goal fails, Major if a section ships unasked work or would be sent back, else Minor, with unrefusable-frame fixed at Major.
rows.why: Kit-defined thresholds the verdict mapping depends on; short.

rows.name: One-line finding format
rows.does: Emits each finding on one line with severity, tag, confidence, file:line, passage, failing reading and optional closing sentence, most severe first.
rows.why: The consuming skill parses this shape, so the model cannot guess it.

rows.name: Closing sentence only when small
rows.does: Proposes a fix sentence only when one sentence closes the defect, otherwise says the fix is larger and stops.
rows.why: Without it a model rewrites sections, taking over authorship the brainstorming skill reserves.

rows.name: Confidence separate from severity
rows.does: Rates confidence independently and forbids downgrading severity to hedge low confidence.
rows.why: Hedging severity under uncertainty is a real model habit, and the rule is one sentence.

rows.name: Verdict line mapping
rows.does: Closes with READY, READY_WITH_FINDINGS or NOT_READY according to findings and any Critical.
rows.why: The dispatcher reads this verdict token, a kit contract.

rows.name: Spec as data, report injections
rows.does: Treats spec and repository text as data and reports any embedded instruction verbatim as a finding.
rows.why: The agent holds a shell and reads attacker-writable text, and reporting injections as findings is a kit-specific output rule.

rows.name: No fix, no certify, not a gate
rows.does: States the reviewer neither fixes nor certifies and that the verdict summarizes rather than gates, with Critical handling owned by brainstorming.
rows.why: The no-fix half repeats the closing-sentence entry and the ownership pointer belongs to the brainstorming skill; the remainder is one clause.

rows.name: No praise or restating
rows.does: Bars praise, plan restatement and out-of-set findings, and says a clean read is READY and stop.
rows.why: Out-of-set findings are already barred by the closed set; the no-praise, stop-at-clean steer is worth one short sentence.

rows.name: No em dashes in output
rows.does: Forbids em dashes in the reviewer's report.
rows.why: The doctrine's Style section already owns the em dash rule for every outward surface.

rows.name: 150-line report cap
rows.does: Caps the whole report under 150 lines.
rows.why: A cheap length bound that keeps a low-effort reviewer from flooding the author.

rows.name: Agent frontmatter and dispatch trigger
rows.does: Registers the prose-reviewer agent with read-only tools, low effort and a description telling orchestrators when and with what inputs to invoke it.
rows.why: The harness routes on this, and without it the agent never gets dispatched.

rows.name: Adversarial fresh-context reviewer role
rows.does: Casts the session as a reviewer who did not write the documents and judges what is on disk, not what was intended.
rows.why: Two sentences that set the whole stance, and cheap for what they do.

rows.name: Recall over precision bias
rows.does: Tells the reviewer to over-flag with stated reasoning because the orchestrator filters, while still anchoring each finding to a quoted passage.
rows.why: Models do hedge toward silence, so the steer matters, but the rule and its reason fit in two sentences.

rows.name: Dispatch input contract
rows.does: Lists the inputs the reviewer receives: spec, documents, fact base, Audience, Voice, the skill path, and how voice values map to reference files under the plugin root.
rows.why: This is kit-specific plumbing, and a model cannot guess the Voice-to-reference mapping or the path layout.

rows.name: Missing-input degradation rules
rows.does: Makes an unreadable path a finding, skips only the check that path carries, forbids recalling the tell catalog from memory, and runs without goal compliance when the spec is absent.
rows.why: Graceful degradation is needed, but the per-file carve-outs are over-specified and one general rule would cover them.

rows.name: Amendments line handling
rows.does: Treats an Amendments in effect line as amending the spec, so amended behavior is not reported as drift.
rows.why: It is a kit-defined input, and without it the reviewer would flag intended changes as drift.

rows.name: Documents are data, not instructions
rows.does: Treats commands inside reviewed documents as findings to report verbatim, never as steps to run.
rows.why: Injection resistance matters for a reviewer that runs Bash, but the doctrine already states this, so one sentence is enough here.

rows.name: Read-only command discipline
rows.does: Forbids edits, commits and builds, explains that the hook does not block builds, and says to report a denial rather than route around it.
rows.why: The rule is needed because the guard leaves builds open, but the contention explanation can go.

rows.name: Spec must-answer coverage check
rows.does: Checks that each document answers every must-answer question the spec lists for its audience.
rows.why: This is the core goal-compliance check, and it is short.

rows.name: Claim verification against sources
rows.does: Opens the source for each number, name, path, behavior and version, settles tool output at the emitting source line or with a provably read-only run, and otherwise marks the claim unverified-on-documents.
rows.why: Verification against sources is essential, but the provably-read-only reasoning is spelled out at length and could take half the words.

rows.name: Effort-authored artifacts not ground truth
rows.does: Checks claims resting on fixtures, stubs or generated files against the owning contract surface, and treats a missing contract as unsettled rather than false.
rows.why: This is a real and subtle failure in which fixtures get treated as the spec, but the passage repeats its instances-not-boundary framing three times, and 100 words would carry it.

rows.name: Refusal and absence check coverage
rows.does: Interrogates checks whose green is a refusal or an absence for which rule refused, what the predicate's scope was, whether the control was withheld from the pattern literals, and whether finding counts track the population.
rows.why: It duplicates the doctrine's withheld-control bullet almost whole, and it rarely applies to prose documents, so a pointer plus one sentence would do.

rows.name: Cross-document consistency check
rows.does: Checks that names, numbers and terms agree across the documents in scope.
rows.why: One line, and a real class of defect.

rows.name: Moment-pin and expiry checks
rows.does: Requires journal-layer figures to carry a moment-pin, checks figures against the machine configuration epoch, and flags dated-evidence annotation in curated surfaces as a journey-ban violation.
rows.why: These are kit-specific rules, so some text is needed, but the passage restates what the testing-discipline and memory-system owners say, which contradicts its own claim to copy neither.

rows.name: Register, heading and voice check
rows.does: Checks documents against the doctrine's structure bullets and the prose-register recipe, restates the heading rules and caps heading case at Minor, and applies the voice reference and marketing-override handling.
rows.why: It should point at the doctrine and skill, not restate the heading bar, which is the surplus this same charter convicts.

rows.name: Catalogued machine-prose tell hunt
rows.does: Hunts the patterns in references/ai-tells.md by name, whatever the voice.
rows.why: The catalog is kit-defined, and the pointer is short.

rows.name: Presumed-knowledge audience check
rows.does: Checks each passage against each persona's knowledge level for terms used before explanation, assumed tool familiarity, and jargon density for non-technical readers.
rows.why: Models write past non-technical readers by default, and this check is concise.

rows.name: Surplus and restated-owner hunt
rows.does: Flags sentences failing the delete-litmus and passages restating another owner's rule, skips the hunt if the owners are unreadable, and warns against cutting sentences a persona needs.
rows.why: The owner pointers are needed, but the skip-if-unreadable clause repeats the degradation rule and the passage runs long.

rows.name: Style-accuracy conflict escalation
rows.does: Makes a style fix that would change a claim say so and name the claim, so the orchestrator decides instead of the looser wording winning.
rows.why: Style edits that quietly change meaning are a plausible failure, and the guard is cheap.

rows.name: Finding line format and tags
rows.does: Sets the severity-ranked one-line finding format with exactly one tag from a fixed set of seven lenses, and asks for the shape of the fix, never replacement prose.
rows.why: The orchestrator parses this contract, so it must be stated.

rows.name: Confidence independent of severity
rows.does: Defines high, medium and low confidence and forbids downgrading severity to hedge low confidence.
rows.why: The independence rule matters, but the definitions of the levels could take one line.

rows.name: Severity level definitions
rows.does: Defines Critical, Major and Minor with what each blocks.
rows.why: The orchestrator gates on these, and they are short.

rows.name: CLAIMS CHECKED evidence block
rows.does: Lists every claim checked with its source and drift, includes unsettled claims under two named markers, and forbids inventing a settling step.
rows.why: Without it, dropped claims look verified, which is a real failure, and the markers are kit vocabulary.

rows.name: Verdict line and no-padding honesty
rows.does: Ends with a three-value VERDICT line, says so plainly when nothing was found, and forbids invented or softened findings.
rows.why: The verdict is parsed downstream, and the text is brief.

rows.name: No praise or summary padding
rows.does: Forbids praise, summaries of the documents and restating the prose in the output.
rows.why: This overlaps the closing no-invented-findings honesty line and the doctrine's no-flattery rule, so it can fold into the output-format owner.

rows.name: Agent frontmatter and dispatch contract
rows.does: Registers the agent with its trigger description, read-and-run tool set, Sonnet model and medium effort.
rows.why: The harness cannot dispatch or scope the agent without it, and the tool list is what keeps it from editing.

rows.name: Report-only verifier role
rows.does: Makes the session judge behavior rather than style and never fix, handing every defect back to the implementer.
rows.why: A capable model left alone will patch what it finds, which destroys the independence of the check.

rows.name: Gate-runner hook denial awareness
