rows.does: Tells the session which writes a kit hook denies and that a denial must be reported, not worked around.
rows.why: The session needs to know a denial is intended, but the allowed-and-denied detail belongs to the hook and one sentence would do.

rows.name: Read plan and Chapters whole
rows.does: Makes the session read the whole plan, including acceptance criteria and deviation Chapters, before verifying.
rows.why: Without it the verifier checks against the spec as first written and misses recorded deviations.

rows.name: Unpinned new test finding
rows.does: Flags any test the diff adds that no Chapter Gate line names with the requirement it pins.
rows.why: This is a kit-specific bookkeeping contract that no model would check unprompted.

rows.name: Full build, real-defect warnings
rows.does: Runs the full build and reports only warnings that point at a real defect on changed lines.
rows.why: A current model runs the build unprompted, so only the rule that pre-existing warnings are out of scope earns words.

rows.name: Full suite with counts
rows.does: Runs the whole suite, not just the new tests, and records passed, failed and skipped.
rows.why: Running the full suite is the one part a model might skip, and it takes one sentence while the output format already carries the counts.

rows.name: Contention lane after suite
rows.does: Runs the repo's contention lane only after the suite finishes, takes its command from the brief, and records it separately.
rows.why: The contention lane is kit vocabulary, and running it concurrently or guessing its command gives a wrong result.

rows.name: NONE DEFINED carries evidence
rows.does: Requires a missing contention lane to cite what the brief said, so absence is not read as a clean pass.
rows.why: The rule is needed, but the output template's '(what the brief said)' already carries most of it, so the justification is padding.

rows.name: Flakiness is a finding
rows.does: Treats an intermittent failure as a finding and reruns once when anything looks flaky.
rows.why: Models tend to explain away a flaky red, and the rule is already short.

rows.name: Verify criteria by execution
rows.does: Requires each acceptance criterion to be proven by running, querying or inspecting output, never by reading the code.
rows.why: Sonnet-tier verifiers do pass criteria on plausibility, and stopping that is the reason this agent exists.

rows.name: UNVERIFIABLE with kind
rows.does: Marks a criterion that cannot be executed as UNVERIFIABLE with a reason and a kind, environment or operator-only.
rows.why: The two-kind vocabulary routes follow-up work downstream, and a model cannot invent it.

rows.name: SQL script idempotency check
rows.does: Checks deployment-script guards and, with a test database available, runs the script twice to confirm the rerun succeeds.
rows.why: The shell-then-ALTER convention is house style, and a double run is an unusual check a verifier would not think to do.

rows.name: Sandbox user state before probing
rows.does: Points HOME, USERPROFILE and store-root variables at a temp directory before any probe.
rows.why: A probe of default-path fallbacks will otherwise write to the operator's real state, and models do not sandbox unprompted.

rows.name: Mutation disclosure and restore protocol
rows.does: Makes the session disclose any live-state mutation, restore it from a pre-copy, and verify the restore by format and hash rather than mtime.
rows.why: Disclosure and the pre-copy restore matter, but the doctrine already states the copy-and-restore rule, so this can shrink to disclosure plus a pointer.

rows.name: Gates run in-turn
rows.does: Keeps builds and suites in the foreground, or polls them to completion within the turn, so the report carries the real exit code.
rows.why: A subagent that backgrounds a run and ends its turn returns an empty report, a real and recurring subagent failure.

rows.name: Fixed report format
rows.does: Sets the BUILD, TESTS, CONTENTION LANE, CRITERIA and VERDICT block the orchestrator parses.
rows.why: The orchestrator depends on this contract, and the model cannot guess it.

rows.name: Evidence per line, no softening
rows.does: Keeps unevidenced claims out of the report and forbids passing on 'obviously' or downgrading a FAIL.
rows.why: This repeats the verify-by-execution entry and the doctrine's verify-before-claim rule, so one owner would do.

rows.name: BLOCKED on missing environment
rows.does: Reports BLOCKED, naming the missing database, secret or runner, instead of guessing.
rows.why: It overlaps the UNVERIFIABLE environment kind and the VERDICT line of the format, so it belongs with them.

rows.name: Blind scope judge seat role
rows.does: Frames the agent as a fresh-context judge that rules on whether a finding or fix serves the plan's Goal, distinct from correctness reviewers and the consultant, via frontmatter description and opening paragraph.
rows.why: The seat and its dispatch description are kit-defined and needed, but the frontmatter restates the three shapes and two contrasts at length that the body repeats.

rows.name: Goal-path inputs read by grep
rows.does: Defines the what (Goal, Intent, acceptance bullets, Out of Scope), makes the agent grep those headings and read only their ranges, and filters Intent clauses into what-and-why versus narrated approach.
rows.why: Reading only the named sections is load-bearing for blindness, but the paragraph packs Intent-parsing edge cases and post-ship ruling rules into one dense block that could be a third the length.

rows.name: Single-finding and design-stop brief contents
rows.does: Lists what the brief carries for these shapes, including the add-decision line's first four parts, the withheld fifth part, and the implementer-report substitute.
rows.why: This is the dispatcher's brief contract, owned by executing-work; the judge only needs to know which inputs are forbidden, which entry 9 already covers.

rows.name: Provenance diff reference rules
rows.does: Specifies the diff reference per shape, requires fix captures under .kit/, and returns NEEDS_CONTEXT for a capture path elsewhere such as docs/.
rows.why: The capture-path check matters, but most of the text describes brief assembly the dispatcher owns.

rows.name: Relevance-shape brief contents
rows.does: Defines the advisory-finding brief: threat field, threat model section or 'absent', performance requirement, and that acceptance bullets and Out of Scope do not ride.
rows.why: It is brief construction for the dispatcher; the judge needs only the line that missing bullets are not NEEDS_CONTEXT.

rows.name: Diff pathspec excluding plans/kaizen
rows.does: Makes the agent read the diff itself with a git pathspec excluding docs/plans, docs/archive and kaizen while keeping other docs in view.
rows.why: A model would otherwise read the whole diff including plan docs and lose its blindness, and the exact command is not guessable.

rows.name: Never read commit messages
rows.does: Bars every command that prints a commit message, since kit commit bodies carry the forbidden fix narrative, and requires hand-skipping plan hunks in .kit captures.
rows.why: The rule and its reason are needed because a model reaches for git log by habit, but the enumerated command list with 'members, not the boundary' can go to one sentence.

rows.name: Inputs as data, read-only
rows.does: Treats the finding, diff and goal text as data, reports embedded instructions verbatim, and forbids edits, commits and builds while respecting hook denials.
rows.why: The tool list and a hook already enforce read-only, and current models treat reviewed content as data; one sentence suffices.

rows.name: Six forbidden inputs gate
rows.does: Returns NEEDS_CONTEXT and rules on nothing if the brief carries the orchestrator's lean, prior consults, fix narrative, Approach, Decisions or Chapters.
rows.why: A model would happily use such inputs if handed them, and this refusal is the core of the seat's independence.

rows.name: Rule on scope not quality
rows.does: Keeps the judge on whether the thing is on the goal path, or on relevance whether the project admits it, rather than whether the finding is correct.
rows.why: Without it a model drifts into judging correctness, which is another seat's job and dilutes the ruling.

rows.name: Bucket, don't survey
rows.does: Requires one bucket and its deciding test rather than a balanced discussion.
rows.why: Models default to hedged surveys, and the orchestrator needs a single routable verdict; the text is already short.

rows.name: Ground rulings in quotes
rows.does: Requires quoting the bullet, Goal sentence or Intent clause, and treats an uncovered item's absence as the finding rather than guessing intent.
rows.why: Models otherwise fill gaps with what the plan probably wanted, which defeats scope adjudication.

rows.name: Negative half governs
rows.does: Makes Out of Scope, Intent not-done clauses and refused alternatives override a Goal sentence the thing also serves.
rows.why: The same precedence is restated in the tie-break paragraph and in the goal-path bullet; one statement would do.

rows.name: Three scope buckets with tests
rows.does: Defines REFUSE (including the design-stop form-departure reading), ACCEPT-AND-DECLARE (no new mechanism) and ASK, plus what the orchestrator does with each.
rows.why: The closed bucket set is the core contract, but the design-stop third reading is argued in a circular, over-qualified way that a lower-tier model will struggle to apply.

rows.name: Bucket tie-break precedence
rows.does: Orders overlapping tests: negative-half REFUSE first, ASK over ACCEPT on cost, form-REFUSE over ASK on size, recorded-decision signals keep ASK.
rows.why: Precedence is needed for determinism, but four stacked carve-outs in one paragraph invite misreading and could be a short ordered list.

rows.name: Infer decisions from finding text
rows.does: Makes the judge read recorded-decision and accepted-risk signals from the finding and goal path alone, defaulting to ASK where a signal points at an unreadable section.
rows.why: It resolves a real contradiction between the ASK tests and the forbidden sections, which a model could not settle on its own.

rows.name: Relevance-shape buckets
rows.does: Defines CONFIRM, REFUSE and ASK for security and performance advisory findings against the threat model, deployment or stated requirement, with REFUSE never resting on absence.
rows.why: A separate closed set is kit-defined and needed, but the prose repeats the quote-the-sentence rule and the both-ways case several times.

rows.name: Whole-changeset two questions
rows.does: At finishing, asks what was built that nothing asked for and what was promised that nothing delivers, distinct from qa-verifier's criteria check.
rows.why: This is a unique kit review pass with a specific framing a model would not produce unprompted.

rows.name: Per-shape output formats
rows.does: Specifies BUCKET, GROUNDS and RECOMMENDATION fields per shape and BUILT-BUT-UNASKED and ASKED-BUT-UNBUILT lists for the whole changeset.
rows.why: The orchestrator parses these fields so the format must be stated, but the GROUNDS and list-item text re-explains bucket semantics already given above.

rows.name: RULED or NEEDS_CONTEXT status
rows.does: Ends every report with a status line, defining NEEDS_CONTEXT as forbidden or missing input and treating an empty list as a result.
rows.why: A machine-readable terminal status is a kit contract the dispatcher depends on, and it is already brief.

rows.name: Orchestrator downstream routing notes
rows.does: Tells the judge how the orchestrator records each bucket: refusal in the plan doc, drift in the Chapter and board recap, ASK via BLOCKED or close-out.
rows.why: These are the orchestrator's acts, owned by executing-work and finishing-work, and do not change what the judge rules.

rows.name: Frontmatter trigger and blocking summary
rows.does: Tells the dispatcher when to invoke the reviewer and restates which findings block a close.
rows.why: The trigger is needed, but the description restates the blocking rules that the body already owns in full.

rows.name: Fresh-context reviewer role framing
rows.does: Casts the agent as a security reviewer for SOC 2-facing systems that judges what the code does rather than what the implementer intended.
rows.why: The role line matters, but the fresh-context rationale is something a current model does unprompted once it is told it is a reviewer.

rows.name: Read-only Bash with guard
rows.does: Restricts Bash to read-only inspection, warns that builds contend with the orchestrator's suite, and says to report a denial rather than route around it.
rows.why: Without it the agent would run builds and tests that contend with shared binaries or try to work around the hook, and both failures cost the orchestrator real time.

rows.name: Brief input lines contract
rows.does: Defines how the agent reads the Trace target and Amendments in effect lines and how section scope differs from finishing scope.
rows.why: These brief fields are kit-defined, so the model cannot interpret them without the text.

rows.name: Disclosure list sweep
rows.does: Makes the agent sweep every in-scope document for items on the brief's Disclosure list and report each hit as a blocking Critical.
rows.why: This is a kit-specific gate that blocks with no citation, and a model would not know the list exists or that it blocks.

rows.name: Read the security model first
rows.does: Has the agent find docs/security-model.md, verify against it, skip its accepted risks, and still check that their preconditions hold, with the TRUSTWORTHY case as the example.
rows.why: Without it the agent re-raises accepted risks as noise and misses preconditions that have eroded.

rows.name: Threat model section shape
rows.does: Defines the fixed four-part Threat model section and bars Criticals or Majors against attacker classes it excludes.
rows.why: The format and the out-of-scope rule are kit-defined and are what keeps severity grounded.

rows.name: Absent threat model handling
rows.does: Makes the agent run the full checklist, open with 'threat model: absent', and tag its Criticals 'threat: absent' for the adjudicator to rule on.
rows.why: This is a kit protocol string that downstream routing reads, so the model cannot guess it.

rows.name: False security-claim findings
rows.does: Treats a security doc or boundary comment that contradicts the code as an at-least-Major finding, cited by file:line, that must be fixed or refuted and never deferred.
rows.why: The rule and its Major floor are needed, but the reason given for the floor explains close-pass routing at more length than the rule needs.

rows.name: Procedure-only architecture invariants
rows.does: Explains that granted procs are attack surface and that privilege lives inside EXECUTE AS procs, applied only where the model is confirmed.
rows.why: The house architecture framing is needed context, but a 5-family model knows the blast-radius reasoning, so a short statement would do.

rows.name: Dynamic SQL in EXECUTE AS
rows.does: Rates concatenated dynamic SQL inside an impersonating proc Critical by default and requires sp_executesql with typed parameters.
rows.why: The Critical-by-default severity is a house call that a model would otherwise rate lower as a code smell.

rows.name: Identifier-name parameter ban
rows.does: Flags any proc that takes a table, column or schema name as a parameter, whatever its current callers.
rows.why: This is a cheap, specific house rule that a model might excuse when the current callers are safe.

rows.name: Inline SQL is Major
rows.does: Rates inline SQL in application code as Major even when parameterized, and Critical when a user-influenced value is concatenated.
rows.why: A model would normally pass parameterized inline SQL, so the house severity has to be stated.

rows.name: Deployment and impersonation hygiene
rows.does: Flags dbo objects, non-EXECUTE or PUBLIC grants, role changes, loginable impersonation targets, privileged connection strings, and cross-database reach.
rows.why: The house specifics are needed, but several items, such as sa in connection strings and PUBLIC grants, are ones a current model already checks.

rows.name: Generic OWASP checklist
rows.does: Lists authz/IDOR, secrets, logging and PII, input validation, crypto and dependency-scan checks, each mapped to an OWASP category.
rows.why: A current model covers standard OWASP checks unprompted, so only the house-specific items, such as Serilog, audit proc payloads, and RandomNumberGenerator, earn words.

rows.name: Second-producer guard check
rows.does: Asks whether the change opens a new path to a surface that another file's sanitizer or clamp guards only for its first producer.
rows.why: The doctrine already carries the rule that a guard belongs at the shared boundary, so this entry should point there as a check instead of restating it.

rows.name: Non-.NET surface checks
rows.does: Extends injection, eval, path traversal and secrets checks to JS/Node, shell and the kit's own hooks, and runs npm or pnpm audit.
rows.why: Naming the kit's hooks as in scope matters, but a model already knows the injection checks it lists.

rows.name: Two-question permission grant audit
rows.does: Audits Bash allow rules for mutation and for reach beyond their purpose, and explains prefix-matching semantics and why deny rules cannot carve out options.
rows.why: The permission-rule semantics are non-obvious and needed, but the text spends about three times the rule's length on hedges, the measured-versus-inferred provenance, and hook exceptions.

rows.name: Finding line output format
rows.does: Fixes the one-line finding shape with severity, trace, threat, confidence, file:line, fix, and OWASP/SOC2 tags.
rows.why: The orchestrator parses this kit-defined format.

rows.name: Trace field rules
rows.does: Requires a trace on every Critical and Major that names the plan bullet, Goal or Intent the code fails, with 'none' and 'unsupplied' as distinct values.
rows.why: The field is kit vocabulary that the agent needs, but the note that it is read for the record rather than for routing is orchestrator-side detail the reviewer does not act on.

rows.name: Threat citation on Criticals
rows.does: Requires a threat field on every Critical, treats an uncited Critical as a Major, and explains that the adjudicator confirms or refuses it.
rows.why: The citation rule is essential, but the adjudicator's downstream flow is restated here after the frontmatter and the security-model section already cover it.

rows.name: Confidence independent of severity
rows.does: Rates confidence separately from severity and forbids downgrading severity to hedge uncertainty.
rows.why: Models do blend the two, and the instruction is short.

rows.name: SOC 2 tag vocabulary
rows.does: Lists the SOC 2 criteria to tag and says to omit a tag rather than guess.
rows.why: The tag list is useful, but the no-tag-stuffing caution is stated twice.

rows.name: Verdict line and thresholds
rows.does: Ends the report with a CLEAR, ADVISORY or BLOCK verdict and defines which findings earn each.
rows.why: The orchestrator reads this kit-defined verdict contract.

rows.name: Honest severity both ways
rows.does: Tells the agent not to inflate theoretical issues or let a real injection slide late in the effort, and defines Critical.
rows.why: Reviewers drift toward both inflation and late-effort leniency, and the Critical definition anchors the verdict.

rows.name: Clean changeset one-liner
rows.does: Says a clean changeset gets a one-line report.
rows.why: A current model does this unprompted once it has the verdict format.

rows.name: Output style frontmatter flags
rows.does: Registers the style as Kit, keeps the default coding instructions, and forces it on for the plugin.
rows.why: The harness needs this metadata to load the style, and it costs almost nothing.

rows.name: Reader is intelligent outsider
rows.does: Makes the session write for Scott as an intelligent outsider whose expertise varies by task, and points to the client-briefing bullet for where depth goes.
rows.why: The reader model matters, but the core's client-briefing bullet already says it, so one sentence here would do.

rows.name: Err toward overexplaining
rows.does: Tells the session to go past normal conciseness in explanation and insight passages and add one more sentence of why when unsure.
rows.why: This deliberately overrides a 5-family model's default terseness, and the tension with the doctrine's rule to match length to the job needs stating somewhere.

rows.name: Teach from work at hand
rows.does: Makes the session teach while it works, using this codebase's decisions and failures rather than generic lessons, with any example placed after the lesson.
rows.why: The house choice is real, but the case-after-rule sentence repeats the core's concrete-case bullet, and the core's teach-the-why bullet already covers most of the rest.

rows.name: Insight block format
rows.does: Requires a starred Insight block of two or three non-obvious points before and after significant work.
rows.why: This is a kit-defined visual format that no model produces unless it is told.

rows.name: Decision block format
rows.does: Requires a scales-glyph Decision block showing the fork, the options, and why the winner won whenever the session makes a call within its own remit.
rows.why: This is a kit-defined format, and a model would otherwise bury the reasoning in prose or leave it out.

rows.name: Decision block versus decision ask
rows.does: Keeps decisions that are Scott's to make out of the Decision block and routes them to a decision ask, and allows either block to be skipped when nothing is non-obvious.
rows.why: Without this line a model could use a Decision block to decide things that belong to the operator, which is a real scope failure.

rows.name: Mandatory memory block
rows.does: Requires a Memory block naming the record, its surface, what changed and why, every time the session deliberately writes, logs, adds or stamps in the memory store, and never for a read alone.
rows.why: This is a kit-specific audit trail tied to memq surfaces, and without a rule that it is mandatory, memory writes would go unannounced.

rows.name: Core pronoun mapping and parity marker
rows.does: States that 'I' and 'me' in the core mean Scott, and marks the core as a byte-identical copy of the doctrine that a parity test pins.
rows.why: This scaffolding exists only because the core is duplicated, so it goes away if the doctrine becomes the single owner.

rows.name: Skip preamble, no flattery
rows.does: Bans openers like 'great question' and puts the fork and the recommendation first.
rows.why: This is a verbatim copy of a doctrine bullet that CLAUDE.md already loads in every session.

rows.name: Disagree up front, hold evidence
rows.does: Makes the session state disagreement first, change position only on a new fact, and answer a bare challenge with one re-check.
rows.why: This is a verbatim duplicate of the doctrine bullet, and the rule is worth keeping only once.

rows.name: Confirmed, inferred, reported marking
rows.does: Makes the session admit uncertainty, separate memory from a file it just read, and tag each claim with its status.
rows.why: This is a verbatim duplicate of the doctrine, and the doctrine's Verify section owns the rule.

rows.name: Teach why at decisions
rows.does: Makes the session show its reasoning and alternatives at design points, then execute an agreed plan without lecturing at each step.
rows.why: This is a verbatim doctrine duplicate, and it overlaps this document's own Teaching section.

rows.name: Plain prose sentence rules
rows.does: Sets the sentence layer: one idea per sentence, about twenty words, no packed qualifications, and precision gained by adding sentences.
rows.why: This is a verbatim duplicate of the doctrine bullet, and the prose-register skill also owns it.

rows.name: Single register, three layers
rows.does: Declares that all prose takes one register with sentence, structure and voice layers, and points to the prose-register skill.
rows.why: This is a pointer duplicated from the doctrine, and the prose-register skill owns the mechanism.

rows.name: Answer first at every scale
rows.does: Makes every piece, section, paragraph and bullet lead with its conclusion, with marketing copy as the only override.
rows.why: This is a verbatim doctrine duplicate.

rows.name: Heading and structure rules
rows.does: Makes headings short, title-shaped topic names, puts the thesis first under each heading, gives tables question-shaped columns, and leaves small pieces without headings.
rows.why: This is a long verbatim doctrine duplicate that prose-register also owns, so it is the heaviest redundant block in the file.

rows.name: Rule then reason
rows.does: Makes the session state a rule and then its reason as separate sentences, with a bold lead only in scannable catalogs.
rows.why: This is a verbatim doctrine duplicate.

rows.name: Concrete case closes passage
rows.does: Makes an example come after the rule and reason, appear only when needed, and be marked illustrative, and forbids writing an open list as closed.
rows.why: This is a verbatim doctrine duplicate, and this file's own Reader and Teaching sections restate it again.

rows.name: Checkable claim form
rows.does: Makes claims use numbers, names and paths instead of adjectives and vague descriptions.
rows.why: This is a verbatim doctrine duplicate.

rows.name: Register scales with piece
rows.does: Sets how much of the register applies to an untitled passage, a titled piece and a full document, and points to prose-register.
rows.why: This is a pointer that duplicates both the doctrine and the prose-register skill.

rows.name: Client-briefing decision ask
rows.does: Makes each decision ask plain-language and self-contained, in a fixed order of situation, decision, stakes, options, recommendation and what happens if unanswered, with evidence at the end.
rows.why: The format matters and a model would not produce it unprompted, but the doctrine already carries it verbatim.

rows.name: Cadence and four-part close
rows.does: Makes the session lead each tool batch with a one-line intent and end substantive turns with what ran, what was inferred, what a peer reported, what only the operator can verify, git state, and the claim most likely wrong.
rows.why: This is a verbatim doctrine duplicate of a real kit mechanism, so it needs one owner, not two.

rows.name: Pending plans board
rows.does: Makes turns that end with plans in flight list each plan with its docs/plans filename, purpose, status, order and what waits on the operator.
rows.why: This is a verbatim doctrine duplicate tied to kit-goal.

rows.name: Before You Send checklist
rows.does: Runs a fourteen-question self-check before sending, covering claim status, sourcing, baselines, scope, rollback, size, gates, old contracts, altered state, subagent directives, real runs, honesty and plan updates.
rows.why: This is a verbatim doctrine duplicate, and most items restate rules that the doctrine and skills state in full, so the copy here adds nothing.

rows.name: Keep design conversation in main thread
rows.does: Bars delegating the design conversation itself to a subagent.
rows.why: A kit that defaults to dispatch would otherwise tempt a session to farm out the dialog, and the one-line rule is cheap.

rows.name: Memory recall and applied stamp
rows.does: Opens with memq recall and stamps any recalled record that changes the design with memq touch --applied.
rows.why: memq and the applied stamp are kit tooling a model cannot know, and the outcome signal depends on the stamp.

rows.name: Backlog read and retirement naming
rows.does: Reads docs/backlog.md, surfaces bearing items with dates, and names covered items in the spec so the close-out prune retires them.
rows.why: The backlog-to-prune link is a kit contract a model would not follow unprompted.

rows.name: Read real code via Explore
rows.does: Reads the relevant code with the Explore subagent before designing, never against guessed signatures.
rows.why: The doctrine's Execution Loop already requires reading involved files and not guessing signatures, so only the Explore vehicle is new here.

rows.name: Set aside forwarded remedies
rows.does: Reads a forwarded write-up for its diagnosis and discards its proposed remedy before sketching.
rows.why: Models anchor hard on a supplied solution, and this short steer counters that.

rows.name: Split oversized requests into sub-specs
rows.does: Gauges size first and splits a request spanning independent subsystems into separately cycled sub-project specs.
rows.why: Useful, but a current model scopes reasonably and the rule plus its subsystem definition fits in two sentences.

rows.name: One question at a time
rows.does: Asks the single most design-changing question and waits, tying this to route (c) of the intake gap check while routes (a) and (b) are declared.
rows.why: It is a house choice that overrides the doctrine's batching default, so the carve-out must be stated.

rows.name: Probe edge cases and corners
rows.does: Lists edge cases, failure modes, integration points, consumers and re-run idempotency to explore.
rows.why: A 5-family model probes these unprompted, and only the idempotency note is project-specific.

rows.name: Options, recommendation, open disagreement
rows.does: Presents real options with tradeoffs, a reasoned recommendation, and disagreement with the operator's framing.
rows.why: The doctrine's Directness and Judgment sections already own this in full.

rows.name: Offer design council at forks
rows.does: Offers the design-council skill, with its cost, in the same turn a hard or material fork is recognized, never auto-running it.
rows.why: The council is a kit mechanism and the offer-not-run and same-turn rules would not arise unprompted.

rows.name: Contract scout sweep for scope
rows.does: Runs a separate banded Explore sweep whenever a touched name, rule or shape appears in more than one file, and writes Files in scope from its return.
rows.why: Missed contract surfaces are a real failure, but the trigger, vehicle and citation rule need about half the words, and banding already lives in executing-work.

rows.name: Plan sketch with Assumptions block
rows.does: Presents a goal-approach-sections sketch carrying an Assumptions block and a one-line Intent summary, iterated to approval.
rows.why: The Assumptions block is what makes approval cover declared gaps, a kit contract a model would not produce.

rows.name: Spec path naming and curation
rows.does: Writes the spec to docs/plans/<project>_<content-type>_v<n>.md without overwriting, then runs curating-docs' create path.
rows.why: The naming and curation hook are kit conventions downstream tooling reads.

rows.name: Intent section contents and bound
rows.does: Writes an Intent record with frame, done and not-done, refused alternatives, dated rulings and provenance, in client-briefing register under about 4,000 bytes checked with wc -c.
rows.why: The record is valuable for later sessions, but the part list and bound can be stated in about 100 words without the amendment and placeholder edge cases.

rows.name: Gating definition drafting rule
rows.does: Requires any phrase deciding what a bounded artifact admits to close its set in idiom or name three exclusions, with a deletion test and carve-outs.
rows.why: Ambiguous membership rules do cause drift, but the definition of the definition is itself dense enough to cost more than it prevents; one rule and one reason would do.

rows.name: Inline spec self-review
rows.does: Rereads the spec once to fix placeholders, contradictions, scope drift and double readings, with no second inline pass.
rows.why: A current model does a self-check when asked, so a one-line pointer suffices.

rows.name: Sweep and Goal coverage check
rows.does: Confirms every sweep surface is in some Files in scope or Out of Scope, and every Goal claim is owned by a section, Operator Verification, or struck.
rows.why: This traceability check catches real under-delivery and a model would not run it unprompted.

rows.name: Intent refusal naming test
rows.does: Makes the author name one mechanism the not-done half would refuse, rewriting the record if none.
rows.why: The Intent template already requires refused alternatives, so this extra test adds ceremony for a rare failure.

rows.name: Jev coverage check
rows.does: Runs kit-jev-check.js to score each section against fixed topics and records one of four closing-line forms in the recap, gating nothing.
rows.why: It gates nothing, its score is only a pointer to re-read, and its four recorded forms and retry rules cost far more than the thin-section risk the blind read already catches.

rows.name: Blind reader dispatch and adjudication
rows.does: Dispatches the blind-reader agent on the spec with a no-context implementer persona and adjudicates each question as answered, assumed or asked, recording the counts.
rows.why: A fresh-context read is the main defense against specs only the author can follow, and the agent and recap line are kit-defined.

rows.name: Gating litmus with paired members
rows.does: Compares author and reader gating-definition lists, places six members per definition, classes results crossed, unplaced, under-length or pass, and records a litmus line.
rows.why: An elaborate four-outcome protocol guarding a failure the blind read and plan review already surface, at a cost well beyond its yield on a 5-family model.

rows.name: Plan reviewer dispatch at fable
rows.does: Dispatches plan-reviewer with the spec path alone at fable and high effort via Workflow, falls back to Agent at low effort, waits rather than downgrading, and adjudicates findings.
rows.why: The review is worth keeping, but the dispatch template and capacity rules belong to executing-work, so this can point there in a few sentences.

rows.name: Review skip conditions
rows.does: Lets a one-or-two-section spec skip blind read, litmus and plan review with a stated reason, and lets an external-engine worker record the skip.
rows.why: Without the stated escape a model would either run full review on trivial specs or skip silently.

rows.name: Commit model in header
rows.does: Records Review-Only, Branch-and-PR or Commit-and-Push in the header, defaulting to Commit-and-Push, with each model described.
rows.why: The doctrine and curating-docs already define the three models and the default, so this should point rather than restate.

rows.name: Model tier per section
rows.does: Assigns haiku, sonnet, opus or fable per section by defined criteria, with haiku requiring a named sibling and gate.
rows.why: The tier bands are kit-defined dispatch instructions and a wrong tier wastes spend or produces bad work.

rows.name: Locus line and inline rule
rows.does: Puts Locus: inline on its own line only for unbriefable sections, keeps Model: a bare token naming the model that runs, and questions fable plus inline.
rows.why: The parser contract matters, but the rule and its reason fit in about half the words.

rows.name: Briefability bar and tier upgrades
rows.does: Requires a cheap-tier section be buildable from its text alone and lets executing-work upgrade but never downgrade tiers.
rows.why: This is the standard that makes cheap tiers safe and a model would not infer it.

rows.name: Tests line as intent
rows.does: Adds a Tests: line naming behaviors and risks to lock, stating intent never design, as a floor amendable on contact.
rows.why: Keeping plans out of test design is useful, but the floor-not-ceiling and phrasing clauses repeat testing-discipline and can compress to two sentences.

rows.name: Document section review inputs
rows.does: For a document deliverable, carries Audience, questions per persona, Voice, fact-base paths, and Disclosure when an outside reader exists.
rows.why: These inputs feed kit reviewers and the disclosure list guards a real client-facing risk.

rows.name: Fable spend is not cost
rows.does: States that a tier never decides whether to spend, Fable use is included, and exhaustion handling lives in other skills.
rows.why: Executing-work and finishing-work own capacity and draw rules, so this is a restatement.

rows.name: Fable sessions design, not execute
rows.does: Restricts a Fable-led session to design work and hands execution to a fresh execution-model session via the plan doc.
rows.why: A house routing choice a model would not follow unprompted, and it guards real spend.

rows.name: Prefer rich references
rows.does: Prefers runnable checks, rubrics, mockups or reference implementations over prose, on a References: line.
rows.why: Short, and it shifts specs toward verifiable acceptance.

rows.name: Spec format template
rows.does: Supplies the exact markdown shape of header, Goal, Intent, Approach, Sections, Out of Scope, Operator Verification, Open Questions and Chapters.
rows.why: It is a machine contract external tooling parses, so it must be exact.

rows.name: Assumptions format and freeze
rows.does: Fixes the one-line assumed-date-route-reversal bullet form, shows assumptions in the recap first, and freezes the section at approval except for deliberate amendments recorded as drift.
rows.why: The format and freeze are needed for the external fingerprint, but the Intent-amendment and execution-time variants can be tightened.

rows.name: Status born In Progress or Ready
rows.does: Sets Status to In Progress for a run starting now and Ready for a parked spec, which session start treats differently.
rows.why: Session-start tooling keys on this and a model cannot guess it.

rows.name: Machine contract pointer
rows.does: Notes the header is a parsed machine contract owned by curating-docs and that Assumptions is inert to the parser.
rows.why: curating-docs owns the frozen shape, so a one-line pointer is enough.

rows.name: Skip spec for trivial work
rows.does: Declines a spec for trivial changes and offers to just do the fix when a brainstorm turns out trivial.
rows.why: A loaded skill otherwise pulls a model into full ceremony on small work, and the guard is cheap.

rows.name: Skill trigger description
rows.does: Routes the session into this skill on branch-cleanup requests or the SessionStart nudge's reapable or stranded flags.
rows.why: Without it the skill never loads, and the named nudge vocabulary ties it to a kit hook.

rows.name: Reapable versus stranded vocabulary
rows.does: Defines the nudge's two flags and orders stranded recovery before any sweep.
rows.why: The terms come from a kit hook the model cannot know, and the ordering prevents deleting a branch that still holds unlanded work.

rows.name: Integration ref resolution order
rows.does: Makes the session treat origin/develop, else origin/main, else origin/master as the merge target.
rows.why: A model would often pick main by reflex and miss develop-based flows, which changes the merged set.

rows.name: Merged-only auto-delete rule
rows.does: Limits automatic deletion to branches in git branch --merged against the integration ref, with upstream-gone alone being only a report.
rows.why: A model tends to treat a gone upstream as merged, which loses squash-merge leftovers and stranded commits.

rows.name: Protected branch list
rows.does: Keeps develop, main, master, the current branch, the default branch and outside worktrees untouched.
rows.why: Stated twice, in Safe Set and Hard Rules, so one statement would do, though the list itself is needed.

rows.name: Worktree reap scope
rows.does: Removes only clean worktrees under .claude/worktrees/ on a reapable branch, without --force.
rows.why: The .claude/worktrees/ path is kit-specific, and a forced removal destroys uncommitted work irreversibly.

rows.name: Fetch prune stop gate
rows.does: Runs git fetch --prune first and stops without deleting if it fails or no integration ref resolves.
rows.why: Cheap guard against computing the merged set from stale refs, and short already.

rows.name: Numbered reap procedure
rows.does: Walks resolve, compute merged set, record tip SHA, remove worktree, then git branch -D.
rows.why: A current model knows these git commands, so only the record-SHA-first step and the order need stating.

rows.name: Two-part report with restore lines
rows.does: Reports reaped items each with a restore command and lists left-alone items with their reason.
rows.why: The restore line is what makes a mistaken delete undoable, and a model would not emit it unprompted.

rows.name: Stranded branch recovery procedure
rows.does: Confirms stranded commits, cuts a fresh recover branch off the integration ref, cherry-picks, pushes and opens a new PR.
rows.why: The load-bearing rule is never reuse the merged frozen branch; the cherry-pick mechanics are known to a current model.

rows.name: Stranded delete exception gate
rows.does: Allows deleting a stranded original only once the recovery branch is pushed at the same hash and git cherry shows no + line, and the branch is in no worktree.
rows.why: The check is needed but is stated in both Recovery step 5 and Hard Rule 1, so one owner would do.

rows.name: Remote auto-delete setting note
rows.does: Tells the session the operator may enable auto-delete head branch on merge in repo settings.
rows.why: It is optional operator advice that changes no act the session performs in this skill.

rows.name: Frontmatter trigger description
rows.does: Routes the session to load this skill at the floor shapes or on an operator request for a second opinion, and away from diff review and design-council.
rows.why: Loading needs a trigger list, but this one restates the whole floor, the design-stop exception and the sibling boundaries, which the body repeats.

rows.name: Fresh read-only ruling judge
rows.does: Defines the consult as one read-only consultant agent, blind to the transcript, that rules on one question, tests the querent's framing and ends with an implementable answer.
rows.why: The role and its rule-not-survey contract are kit-defined and a model cannot infer them.

rows.name: Counted floor over feeling
rows.does: Makes the session check named trigger shapes rather than its own sense of being stuck, because stuck sessions feel almost done.
rows.why: Models reliably under-escalate while believing they are close, so a countable floor changes behavior cheaply.

rows.name: Second failed attempt trigger
rows.does: Fires a consult on the second failed attempt at one problem, while deferring to executing-work's tier-escalation ladder when review Criticals repeat a class.
rows.why: The trigger is needed, but the ladder carve-out and seesaw instance spend many words on a boundary executing-work already owns.

rows.name: Consult before decision BLOCKED
rows.does: Makes the session consult before raising a decision BLOCKED, sending the operator only the surviving preference, cost or risk fork with the ruling attached, and naming what goes straight up.
rows.why: The consult-first gate prevents premature operator interrupts and matters, but the design-stop substitution clause is a cross-reference executing-work owns.

rows.name: Debugging dead end trigger
rows.does: Fires a consult at a systematic-debugging dead end before stopping to report.
rows.why: Short and names a moment a model would otherwise end with a stop-and-report.

rows.name: General license for uncovered decisions
rows.does: Licenses a consult for any hard-to-reverse or load-bearing decision the spec does not cover, rather than guessing.
rows.why: Without it a model guesses silently on uncovered decisions, and the text is cheap.

rows.name: Design stop routing
rows.does: Names the design stop as a floor shape whose judge is executing-work's step 4 judge, not the consultant, because that judge must not receive the querent's lean.
rows.why: Executing-work step 4 owns the design stop's brief, dispatch and ruling, so a pointer would do here.

rows.name: Rulable versus operator spec gaps
rows.does: Makes the session rule factual spec gaps itself through a consult and send the operator only preference, cost or risk-appetite forks.
rows.why: Models tend to push factual questions to the operator, and this split is the skill's core payoff.

rows.name: Consult brief contents
rows.does: Requires the brief to carry the decision, evidence, paths, Goal and Intent by path, the lean labeled as an instinct to test, and what an implementable answer looks like, or get NEEDS_CONTEXT back.
rows.why: The labeled lean and the Goal/Intent reference are kit contracts that let the fresh judge test framing, and a model would not assemble them unprompted.

rows.name: Bulky evidence to scratch path
rows.does: Sends bulky evidence to the gitignored .kit/ path and passes it by path in the brief.
rows.why: The doctrine and curating-docs already own the .kit/ scratch rule.

rows.name: Section scope excludes design stop
rows.does: States that the brief, model, adjudication and sibling sections apply to the consultant only and never to the design stop.
rows.why: It repeats the design-stop exception already stated in trigger (e) and the frontmatter.

rows.name: Fable high with Opus fallback
rows.does: Dispatches the consultant on Fable at high after executing-work's capacity reading, falling back to Opus at max through Workflow agent() with the Reviewer Dispatch template, and notes the standing dispatch grant.
rows.why: The model routing and fallback are kit-specific and needed, but the standing-dispatch restatement and template justification pointer belong to their owners.

rows.name: Static model choice
rows.does: Forbids choosing the consult model by how hard the question looks.
rows.why: One sentence that blocks a plausible downgrade on seemingly easy questions.

rows.name: Adjudicating the ruling
rows.does: Treats the RULING, EVIDENCE, CONFIDENCE and OPERATOR FORK return as a hypothesis checked against real code, records adopted and discarded parts in the Chapter, and sends a surviving fork up as the BLOCKED.
rows.why: The return format and Chapter record are kit-specific, but the verify-before-adopting half restates the doctrine's finding-is-a-hypothesis rule.

rows.name: Consult versus sibling instruments
rows.does: Distinguishes the consult from design-council and the diff reviewers.
rows.why: The frontmatter already draws the same boundaries, so the body section duplicates it.

rows.name: Seat definition and owner pointers
rows.does: Defines the coordinator as one exclusive seat per machine and points at peer-sessions, role and kit-goal as owners of claims, the directory contract and authority.
rows.why: The session needs the definition, but three paragraphs of which document governs which can be two sentences.

rows.name: Board path and machine naming
rows.does: Puts the board at coordinator/<machine>/board.md in the memory store and spells how the machine identifier differs from the HOSTNAME: Role session name.
rows.why: The path is kit-only knowledge, but the memq 40-character hostname edge case is rare detail.

rows.name: Event-driven wake, 4-hour heartbeat
rows.does: Makes the seat wake on messages and pings, arm only a 4-hour reconciliation timer, and never arm the chassis's 15 to 60 minute one-shots.
rows.why: The override of the standing-watch pacing needs stating, but the same reasoning appears twice.

rows.name: Cold-start tick order
rows.does: Makes the seat arm the wake before any read, then read the board, report a missing board to the operator, and hold until the operator answers.
rows.why: Arm-first and the no-board gate are real kit rules, but the stamp self-check and directory-versus-file detail swell step 2.

rows.name: Closed set of four functions
rows.does: Limits the seat to four functions: operator interface, cross-repo sequencing, machine-resource arbitration and kaizen.
rows.why: This is a short scope boundary a model could not infer.

rows.name: Status round polling threshold
rows.does: Makes the seat read worker state from registry entries and message a worker only when its Status-updated stamp is older than 4 hours and the operator's open question depends on it.
rows.why: Without the threshold a model over-polls, but path screens and branch-tip staleness make one bullet 390 words.

rows.name: Kaizen inbox dispositioning
rows.does: Makes the seat judge kaizen notes against the kaizen bar and fold survivors into the owning repo's spec or backlog without asking the operator per note.
rows.why: The kaizen skill owns the bar and the dispatch mechanics, so this file only needs the grant and a pointer.

rows.name: BLOCKED funnel intake
rows.does: Makes the seat learn of blockers from worker messages or goal-blocked events, read the note only through kit-goal.js status, and treat a missing note as uninformative.
rows.why: The sources and the CLI are kit-only facts, but the disposition of each event field in turn is excessive.

rows.name: Two-leg event screening
rows.does: Makes the seat screen an event's project path, join its session id to the registry and roster for a live, no-live or unestablished reading, and require a readable plan doc before it briefs.
rows.why: Treating events as unauthenticated claims matters, but the three-reading join guards a local forgery threat a single rule would cover.

rows.name: Brief channel and relay race
rows.does: Sends the brief over the seat's allowlisted relay thread or keyboard in decision register, never gated on the broker's own ping, and names an unboarded escalation as untracked.
rows.why: The channel choice is needed, but the external-broker architecture note adds no act.

rows.name: Blocker answer return path
rows.does: Makes the brief name the worker's reply address in advance, relays answers given to the seat in quoted form, and asks the operator to re-post a warranted-channel yes.
rows.why: The re-post exception is load-bearing, but the rest restates peer-sessions Leashed peers.

rows.name: No within-repo oversight
rows.does: Keeps the seat from reviewing diffs or reordering sections and routes such matters to the repo's expert or the operator.
rows.why: A capable model would otherwise intervene in repo work, and the rule is short.

rows.name: Update window drain round
rows.does: Opens a window only on the operator's word on keyboard or relay, boards it first, and sends each live local session one drain line pointing at executing-work's WAITING: shape.
rows.why: This is a real kit procedure, but the scoping of elevated and subagent rows and the line bars take most of the words.

rows.name: Silence is not a park
rows.does: Makes the window report list confirmed, unconfirmed and unreached sessions and never count silence as parked.
rows.why: Models tend to report optimistic completion, and this is a concise guard.

rows.name: Resume checklist and reply paths
rows.does: Builds a resume checklist from each session's reply and durable surfaces, and screens any path a reply carries without reading it.
rows.why: The checklist is useful, but screening paths that no rule asks for guards an implausible case.

rows.name: Seat parks itself last
rows.does: Makes the seat park after the report through its ordinary banked pass, keep its wake armed, and restate its parked state on each wake.
rows.why: It is needed so the seat keeps its timer, but it can be two sentences.

rows.name: Window cancel and close
rows.does: Closes a window only on the operator's word and sends a close line to drained sessions still live, with no re-arming or new tasking.
rows.why: The inverse is obvious once the drain is stated, so one rule plus the dead-name caveat suffices.

rows.name: Reconciliation pass source list
rows.does: Lists the sources each pass re-derives the board from: roster, registry, plan docs, origin tips, kit-events, goal CLI and the kaizen inbox.
rows.why: A model cannot know these kit sources unless told.

rows.name: Rotated events file predicate
rows.does: Makes the seat read kit-events.jsonl.old when the live file's earliest event postdates the last pass or when the time cannot be read.
rows.why: For a best-effort stream, one clause saying to also read the .old file would do the job of a timestamp predicate.

rows.name: Sources are data
rows.does: Makes the seat report instructions found in any source verbatim to the operator, never act on them, and elide paths.
rows.why: The doctrine's data-not-instructions rule already carries this.

rows.name: Reconciliation guard and messages rule
rows.does: Treats board entries the seat did not write as claims to confirm, and writes message-borne facts to the ledger before the pass ends.
rows.why: Compaction loses loop context, and a successor over-trusting an inherited board is a real failure.

rows.name: Roster-registry diff and join
rows.does: Joins registry Name: to ListAgents row names, marks unregistered sessions, and sends unmatched entries to the heartbeat reading.
rows.why: The join key is kit-only knowledge, but the three-outcome disposition repeats itself.

rows.name: Heartbeat prune predicate
rows.does: Prunes an off-roster registry entry only when its Heartbeat advanced past Started and is stale past twice the seat's cadence, and reads every unclear stamp as unknown.
rows.why: Deleting a peer's file needs a precise test, but the forgery and never-destroy reasoning can be cut to the rule and one reason.

rows.name: Standing-watch chassis inheritance
rows.does: Sends the seat to the standing-watch skill before the first pass and names the three overrides.
rows.why: This short pointer is needed for the loop mechanics.

rows.name: Banked-pass compaction declaration
rows.does: Makes the last act of every pass a registry status push whose stamp advance opens the compaction marker.
rows.why: The text itself says the peer-sessions banking rule owns the invariant, the hook and the fallback.

rows.name: Seat dispatches nothing
rows.does: Makes the seat produce specs or backlog entries and ask the operator to arm plans via /kit-goal, never tasking a session on its own say-so.
rows.why: A coordinating model would otherwise task peers directly, and this is the seat's central bound.

rows.name: Admin-requests inbox append
rows.does: Appends the operator's asks for an elevated Admin seat to admin-requests.md under the line bars, or reports that no Admin is seated.
rows.why: The append is kit-only, but the justification and the boardless-seat case are verbose.

rows.name: Standing-delegation edge
rows.does: Lets scoped direction from the seat stand where the operator wrote the role skill's standing-delegation opt-in.
rows.why: The role skill owns the model, its scope and its exclusions.

rows.name: Closed list of warranted channels
rows.does: Names keyboard, allowlisted relay thread and artifact-borne authorization as the only warranted channels, and bars extension except by the operator.
rows.why: The doctrine names this file as the list's owner so it must stay, but the self-authored and chain-handoff caveats double its length.

rows.name: Store readership precondition
rows.does: Writes the board as a public surface until the operator names who reads the store's remote, and ignores the host's privacy flag.
rows.why: Defaulting to public writing matters for client data, but it takes one rule and one reason.

rows.name: Board line categories
rows.does: Separates commitments, re-derivable lines and told-not-derived lines, and states which get stubs and re-derive labels.
rows.why: The distinction drives what survives a successor, but it is restated again in the overrides section.

rows.name: No authority, path and words bars
rows.does: Keeps authority off the board and bars absolute paths and the operator's words, quoted or paraphrased, from every board line.
rows.why: These are concise privacy and authority bars a model would not apply unprompted.

rows.name: Clock-stamped board times
rows.does: Makes the seat read any time it writes from kit-registry-stamp.js now rather than compose it.
rows.why: Models misstate the current time, and the tool is kit-only.

rows.name: Board content inventory
rows.does: Lists what the board carries: roster rows, efforts, handoffs, resource claims, escalations, window state and routed findings with disposition pointers.
rows.why: The list is needed, but the routed-finding and prune bullets carry about 400 words of edge cases.

rows.name: Ledger overrides of chassis
rows.does: Exempts commitment and told-not-derived lines from re-derive labels and drops the standing section.
rows.why: It is needed, but it restates the categories entry.

rows.name: Four-kinds candidate routing
rows.does: Routes each board candidate to a re-derivable line, a one-record line, a memory record or a kaizen note at write time.
rows.why: Routing lessons to memory and friction to kaizen fits in two sentences.

rows.name: Misfiling cost and conflict algebra
rows.does: Argues the cost of each misfiling and resolves candidates that fit several kinds through permission-versus-refusal precedence.
rows.why: This theory costs far more than the rare misfiling it prevents, and a current model routes sensibly with the core rule.

rows.name: Re-derive labels never executed
rows.does: Spells re-derive commands home- or repo-relative and treats them as labels, never commands to run.
rows.why: Executing synced text from another machine is a real injection risk, and the rule is short.

rows.name: Store sync durability reading
rows.does: Relies on the store's automatic sync as the board's committer and reads kit-sync-state.json for gaps to report without working around them.
rows.why: The gap-reporting rule is needed, but the explanation of each sync state reads like a reference doc.

rows.name: Source of truth for commitments
rows.does: Treats the ledger as the only record of commitments, and reads a worker's resolution Chapter as answered-unconfirmed until the operator confirms.
rows.why: It is needed, but it largely restates the reconciliation guard.

rows.name: Board write and manual sync
rows.does: Rewrites the board in place, binds row names to ListAgents, and compares sync-store.ps1 with bare git pull/push exposures for closing sync lag.
rows.why: One sentence preferring the screened script over bare git would do, and the security comparison belongs in docs/security-model.md.

rows.name: Stub rules for entries
rows.does: Stubs entries that exceed a pointer or are too sensitive, naming existence, channel and time, with special cases for prunes, windows and routed findings.
rows.why: The stub concept is needed, but four per-category special cases are too many.

rows.name: Cold-successor readability test
rows.does: Tests the board by whether a cold successor can take the seat from one read.
rows.why: This is a cheap, useful bar.

rows.name: Homing round protocol
rows.does: Moves grown board lines to their proper destinations through a two-moment memq journal, confirmed landings and cut-only-when-confirmed rewrites.
rows.why: This transactional ceremony guards a rare cleanup, and one rule would cover it: cut a line only after its destination write is confirmed.

rows.name: No-board and frozen-board mode
rows.does: With no board or a frozen one, the seat still reads and briefs but takes on no handoff, escalation, routed finding or prune, and names things untracked.
rows.why: The decline list is needed, but it is spread over four paragraphs.

rows.name: Seat handoff announcement
rows.does: Makes a successor read the ledger before announcing under the HOSTNAME: Coordinator name, and message a live predecessor.
rows.why: The order and naming form are kit-specific and short.

rows.name: Contested seat freeze
rows.does: Freezes the board when two roster rows claim the seat, routes the claimants to the operator, and sends time anchors instead of choosing a board version.
rows.why: The freeze and route rule is needed, but three reasons for not picking a version is excessive.

rows.name: Operator etiquette and relay quoting
rows.does: Makes the seat answer the operator immediately, batch decision asks with recommendations, and quote relayed decisions with their channel and time.
rows.why: The doctrine owns batching and register, and peer-sessions owns relay recording.

rows.name: Delta report against last pass
rows.does: Reports to the operator only what changed since the board's last recorded pass, or a full report labeled as such when no baseline exists.
rows.why: Without it, models re-list the whole state each time.

rows.name: Trigger on any C# work
rows.does: The frontmatter description makes the skill load for any C# edit, even when style is not named.
rows.why: Without a broad trigger the skill never loads on routine C# edits, and every other rule in the document goes unapplied.

rows.name: Read full reference first
rows.does: Sends the session to references/csharp-style.md for the full pattern reference before it writes code.
rows.why: The model cannot know the reference file exists, and the checklist cites it (reference section 1).

rows.name: Period-terminated imperative section comments
rows.does: Makes every in-method section comment a short imperative title ending in a period, with no history or narration and only a rare WHY comment.
rows.why: This is the signature house trait and a model would not produce it unprompted, but the sentence on the doctrine's prose register repeats the doctrine, and the rule is stated again in the checklist.

rows.name: Group and label related items
rows.does: Separates groups of related items with whitespace and a label comment.
rows.why: The checklist's grouped-fields and DI-grouping lines already carry this rule in a more concrete form.

rows.name: Idempotent DI registration
rows.does: Makes code safe to re-execute and has DI registration use AsImplementedInterfaces().PreserveExistingDefaults().
rows.why: The checklist repeats the exact registration call, so one owner would do, and the general idempotence clause is too vague to change behavior.

rows.name: Region banners organize classes
rows.does: Wraps every class section in #region/#endregion and forbids removing existing regions.
rows.why: Current models lean toward removing regions as dated style, so the rule and its antipattern are both needed, though the checklist already carries the canonical order.

rows.name: Mimic a sibling file
rows.does: Has the session copy the layout of an existing file of similar shape, and fall back to the exemplar when there is no sibling.
rows.why: A current model mimics nearby code unprompted, so only the bound matters: sibling mimicry happens inside this style.

rows.name: Style precedence over repo
rows.does: Ranks a mechanically enforced repo contract above this style and this style above legacy sibling code.
rows.why: The doctrine's Defaults section states the same precedence nearly word for word, so this copy is a second owner.

rows.name: Method exemplar code block
rows.does: Shows one complete method: validation, return-value default, try/catch with a period-ended log line, and comments that tell the story.
rows.why: One concrete exemplar shows the whole method shape more cheaply and reliably than prose, and an agent copies it directly.

rows.name: Three-grep outline for large files
rows.does: Has the session outline a C# file over about 1,000 lines using three specific regexes for types, members and regions before reading any range.
rows.why: The doctrine points here for outlining, so the patterns are worth keeping, but a model can grep declarations unaided and the payoff is token savings in rare cases.

rows.name: Regex pitfall explanations
rows.does: Explains three quiet failures of the grep patterns (the word boundary, the default-parameter filter, and optional modifiers) plus an interface-specific member pattern.
rows.why: This much regex defense for an optional outlining aid costs more than the failure it prevents, and the doctrine already says an outline never proves absence, so a whole-file search catches any miss.

rows.name: Region labels read verbatim
rows.does: Has the session treat repeated record entries as confirmation and read #region labels verbatim as the file's map.
rows.why: Reading labels verbatim is a mild but useful steer; the record-duplication note is trivia a model resolves on its own.

rows.name: File-scoped coarse namespaces
rows.does: Has new files use file-scoped namespaces, leaves existing block-scoped files alone, and keeps namespaces coarse rather than mirroring folders.
rows.why: Coarse namespaces that ignore folders go against the IDE default a model would follow, and leaving existing files alone prevents churn.

rows.name: No change-narrative comments
rows.does: Forbids comments that narrate updates or prior versions.
rows.why: The doctrine's current-state rule and Core Philosophy point 1 already own this.

rows.name: No null-forgiving operator
rows.does: Bans the ! operator in favor of null-conditional and null-coalescing.
rows.why: A model uses ! freely to silence warnings, so this house choice needs stating.

rows.name: No inline SQL
rows.does: Routes data access through stored procedures with CommandType.StoredProcedure.
rows.why: The doctrine's Defaults section owns the stored-procedure rule, though this local reminder is cheap.

rows.name: Lazy options, cost-ordered middleware
rows.does: Resolves configuration lazily at request time and orders middleware so cheap rejection runs before expensive work.
rows.why: These are non-obvious architectural choices a model would not infer, and the words are few.

rows.name: Class skeleton checklist items
rows.does: Sets region order, _camelCase readonly grouped fields, constructor parameter layout, and a // Save Services. opener.
rows.why: These exact layout rules are house-specific and cannot be guessed.

rows.name: Modern C# idiom checklist
rows.does: Requires default over null, is null patterns, ??=, collection expressions and spreads, the Async suffix, and CancellationToken last and passed down.
rows.why: Most of these are what a current model writes unprompted; the distinctive part is default over null and spreads over ToArray/Concat.

rows.name: Usings, logging, DI checklist
rows.does: Sets using order with no blank lines and no file headers, period-ended log messages through ILogger or Serilog, and DI in Assembly/RegisterServices.cs grouped by domain.
rows.why: The file locations and the log-message period are house facts a model cannot know.

rows.name: Inline interface, Interfaces folder
rows.does: Has a class declare its interface inline, with the interface file under Interfaces/.
rows.why: The folder convention is house-specific and cheap to state.

rows.name: XML docs only when earned
rows.does: Allows /// summary docs on public members only where they add more than the signature.
rows.why: This is stated in both Core Philosophy point 1 and the checklist, so it needs one owner.

rows.name: Comments tell the story
rows.does: Closes the exemplar with the test that section comments alone should narrate the method.
rows.why: It is a one-line self-check that makes the comment rule verifiable.

rows.name: Example names are placeholders
rows.does: Tells the session to substitute project namespaces for the Acme examples and to mirror a sibling file's layout in an in-style repo.
rows.why: A current model rarely copies placeholder names verbatim, but the follow-a-sibling rule is worth one sentence.

rows.name: Using-directive ordering
rows.does: Orders usings System first, then a loose mix of third-party and project namespaces, with no blank lines between groups.
rows.why: The order is idiosyncratic and not inferable, but the prose plus a full example block states it twice.

rows.name: Coarse file-scoped namespaces
rows.does: Keeps one namespace root per project with no folder sub-namespaces, file-scoped for new files, none in plugin assemblies.
rows.why: Models default to folder-mirrored namespaces, so without this they would produce the wrong shape.

rows.name: No file header
rows.does: Makes files start with using directives, with no copyright or author block.
rows.why: A current model writes no file header unprompted in C# unless a sibling has one.

rows.name: Interfaces folder placement
rows.does: Puts every interface in Interfaces/ rather than beside its implementation, restated in the service template.
rows.why: A house layout choice the model cannot guess, and cheap to state.

rows.name: Region blocks in fixed order
rows.does: Organizes each class into Constants, Variables, Constructor, public groups, and Private Methods regions with nested private sub-regions and aligned endregion lines.
rows.why: This is the signature trait and runs against the modern default of no regions, so the skeleton earns its words.

rows.name: Field naming and label groups
rows.does: Names private fields _camelCase, consts camelCase or SCREAMING_SNAKE, and groups fields under // Values., // Mapper., // Services. style labels.
rows.why: The label comments and the split const casing are non-standard and would not appear without the text.

rows.name: Single constructor layout
rows.does: Writes one constructor with eight-space parameter indent, a dangling close paren, a // Save Services. comment, and inline AutoMapper construction.
rows.why: The odd indentation is needed, but the example repeats the skeleton already shown in the region section.

rows.name: Method signature formatting
rows.does: Ends async names with Async, puts CancellationToken last, and lays multi-parameter signatures one per line with a dangling paren.
rows.why: Async suffix and token-last are defaults a model already follows; only the dangling-paren layout is house-specific.

rows.name: Section comments narrate method bodies
rows.does: Splits every method body into blocks under Title Case, period-terminated, imperative intent comments with a stock vocabulary and no history or why.
rows.why: The document calls this the heart of the style, and models otherwise write sparse or explanatory comments.

rows.name: Modern C# body idioms
rows.does: Prefers early return default, is null, ??=, var, LINQ method syntax, collection expressions, explicit parens on named initializers, and interpolation.
rows.why: Most items are what a current model writes anyway; only explicit-parens initializers, default over null, and collection spreads need stating.

rows.name: Worked method body example
rows.does: Shows a full ProcessFormAsync body demonstrating sections, return-value variable, try/catch logging and default return.
rows.why: Useful as a pattern, but it overlaps the new service template almost line for line, so one example would do.

rows.name: Async pattern rules
rows.does: Passes tokens down, keeps Task signatures on sync helpers via Task.FromResult, uses ConfigureAwait(false) only in background services, and bans ValueTask.
rows.why: The ConfigureAwait scoping and ValueTask ban are house choices a model would not infer.

rows.name: Logging conventions
rows.does: Logs via ILogger<T> or static Serilog Log matching the file, with a fixed catch shape, method-prefixed Debug traces and period-terminated messages.
rows.why: Period endings and the method-name prefix trace are non-obvious and the dual-logger rule prevents mixing.

rows.name: Swallow-and-log exception handling
rows.does: Catches generic Exception, logs, returns default, adds finally for background loops, never throw ex, and defines no custom exception types.
rows.why: Swallowing and no custom exceptions run against a model's defaults, so the text changes output.

rows.name: Nullable annotations, no bang operator
rows.does: Enables nullable reference types, annotates nullable returns, discards unused returns with _, and forbids the null-forgiving operator.
rows.why: The ban on ! and the discard habit are choices a model would otherwise violate.

rows.name: Autofac registration shape
rows.does: Registers every type with AsImplementedInterfaces and PreserveExistingDefaults under uppercase period-ended domain labels in RegisterServices.cs.
rows.why: The project-specific registration pattern is needed, but three near-identical code blocks plus a fourth in the template repeat one line.

rows.name: IOptionsMonitor for settings
rows.does: Injects IOptionsMonitor<T> rather than IOptions<T> and reads CurrentValue at use time.
rows.why: A defensible alternative the model would not pick by default, stated cheaply.

rows.name: Type suffix and verb vocabulary
rows.does: Fixes class suffixes (Service, Handler, Helper, Notification, legacy Repository), method verb prefixes, and I-prefixed interfaces.
rows.why: The I prefix and common suffixes are universal; only the legacy Repository note and verb meanings add information.

rows.name: MediatR notification pattern
rows.does: Makes notifications plain data holders with a Caller set via nameof, handlers in Handlers/, published with an inline-built notification.
rows.why: The Caller convention is project-specific and handlers depend on it, so omission would break the contract.

rows.name: Models folders and settings DTOs
rows.does: Places models under purpose folders and writes settings as get/set DTOs, never records, with collection-expression initializers.
rows.why: The folder taxonomy and no-records rule are house choices a model cannot infer.

rows.name: Whitespace basics
rows.does: Indents four spaces, no tabs, one blank line between methods and regions.
rows.why: A current model does this unprompted and any committed .editorconfig governs anyway.

rows.name: New service template
rows.does: Provides a full skeleton for a new service plus its registration and interface file location.
rows.why: It restates the region skeleton, constructor, method body and registration examples already given, so one canonical skeleton should own it.

rows.name: Skill trigger description
rows.does: Loads the skill at plan completion, when a new plan is registered, or when a docs tree needs tidying.
rows.why: The trigger surface is how the skill gets loaded at all, and the symptom list is compact.

rows.name: Finished means archived and indexed
rows.does: Defines a plan as finished only once it is archived, the backlog is pruned, cross-references are in place and the index is current.
rows.why: Without this, a session stops at flipping the Status to Complete, and the sentence costs little.

rows.name: Three-zone docs taxonomy
rows.does: Places stable docs at the docs/ root, active plans in docs/plans/, finished plans in docs/archive/, and live next-steps in docs/backlog.md.
rows.why: This is a kit-defined layout that the hooks and the other skills depend on, so a model cannot infer it.

rows.name: Coordinator-board file carve-out
rows.does: Tells a curating pass to leave any docs/coordinator-board.md where it is, because that file is a leftover of the coordinator seat's board.
rows.why: It guards a legacy migration artifact that belongs to the role skill, and most projects will never contain the file.

rows.name: Separate append disciplines
rows.does: Keeps append-only Chapters with the plan, and keeps the backlog pruned-live for cross-effort items.
rows.why: The taxonomy table's Discipline column already says this.

rows.name: Archive via git mv, re-add
rows.does: Confirms the plan is Complete with a final Chapter, moves it with git mv, then re-adds it so worktree edits are staged, using the RM status as the tell.
rows.why: The git mv staging gotcha is non-obvious, and missing it silently commits a pre-finalization copy of the doc.

rows.name: Repoint links after move
rows.does: Greps the moved plan for ../archive/ links and rewrites them for the plan's new location.
rows.why: A model moving a file rarely re-checks its relative links, and the broken links go unnoticed.

rows.name: Related-section cross-referencing
rows.does: Links a plan to the plans it builds on or supersedes through a Related section, marks superseded plans, and adds one-way pointers when the other plan is already archived.
rows.why: It is a house convention, and the one-way rule keeps the archive immutable.

rows.name: Most-recent-four index chain
rows.does: Updates both README indexes and keeps a matching chain of the four most recently archived plans on the 'Completed plans are in' line.
rows.why: The exact format is kit-specific, and the two indexes drift apart without it.

rows.name: Archive in same close-out
rows.does: Requires archiving in the close-out that finished the work, never later or in a batch.
rows.why: It is cheap and prevents plans piling up in docs/plans/.

rows.name: New plan registration path
rows.does: When brainstorming writes a spec, adds it to the active list, cross-references it, and records design-time next-steps in the backlog.
rows.why: Nothing else prompts indexing at plan creation.

rows.name: Quarterly backlog snapshot moves
rows.does: Moves done backlog items into docs/archive/backlog-YYYY-QN.md instead of striking them through in place.
rows.why: It is a defensible house choice that a model would not guess.

rows.name: 90-day backlog aging adjudication
rows.does: Names active items parked more than 90 days for a promote, retire or keep call, with a dated re-adjudication format and backfilled dates for undated items.
rows.why: The rule and the date format are needed, but the edge cases on undated items and young repositories could be cut to one line.

rows.name: Offer prune from session-start
rows.does: Offers the prune pass in one line when the session-start block reports an item past the threshold.
rows.why: It ties a hook signal to an action, and the text is short.

rows.name: Retrofit audit-propose-apply
rows.does: Audits an old docs tree read-only, proposes the migration and waits for approval, then applies it with moves and never deletes a file.
rows.why: A current model already asks before a bulk reorganization, so only the steps and the never-delete rule need to stay, not the blocker-set pointer prose.

rows.name: Strict parser contract framing
rows.does: Warns that an external engine parses plan docs with case-sensitive, line-anchored rules, and that a wrong value silently falls back to a default.
rows.why: This explains why exact shapes matter, and a model would otherwise reword the headers freely.

rows.name: Status header value rules
rows.does: Requires the Status value to be exactly Complete to read as terminal, and defines In Progress and Ready, with Ready as a parked pre-arm value.
rows.why: The exact-value rule is essential, but the Ready discussion and the pointers into executing-work's stand-down roughly double its length.

rows.name: Commit Model header and PR cadence
rows.does: Requires the Commit Model value to open with one of three tokens, and parses trailing prose to decide between a pull request per section and one draft pull request per plan.
rows.why: The token rule belongs here, but the pull-request lifecycle detail is finishing-work's to own and is only restated here.

rows.name: Disjoint header rule
rows.does: Declares with 'Disjoint: yes' that a plan may run beside a blocked plan, and defaults to not disjoint.
rows.why: This is an engine-specific flag that a model cannot know.

rows.name: Sections and Model line shapes
rows.does: Fixes the Sections of Work heading, the '### N.' section headings, and a bare-token Model line whose decorated values silently fall back to sonnet.
rows.why: The silent sonnet fallback on a decorated value is exactly the failure a model would cause.

rows.name: Chapters block and Completed forms
rows.does: Fixes the Chapters heading as the approval-fingerprint boundary, the Chapter heading, the three accepted Completed-line forms, and the Next line.
