rows.why: A wrongly phrased Completed line leaves a section open forever, and a model would plausibly write one.

rows.name: Kit-side reader looseness details
rows.does: Describes how the session-start hook, the status line, the kit-goal lib and the chapter nudge each read plan docs more loosely than the engine does.
rows.why: This is maintainer documentation of hook internals and does not change what a session writes, apart from the 'Complete (archived)' nag, which fits in one sentence.

rows.name: Which skills instance rows
rows.does: Points to the brainstorming and executing-work templates as the normative instances of the contract rows.
rows.why: Those skills already carry the templates, so a single pointer line would do.

rows.name: Contract change control
rows.does: Makes any change to a row's shape a coordinated, versioned change with the OS repo, and exempts values a row already decides.
rows.why: It stops drive-by edits that would break an external consumer.

rows.name: Optional heading placement rules
rows.does: Places Dispatch Authorization above Sections of Work, and Intent and Assumptions outside the sections block and above Chapters, with mid-run additions recorded in a Chapter.
rows.why: The placements matter because a misplaced heading truncates the parse, but the rationale and the template walk-through could be about a third as long.

rows.name: Templates pointer
rows.does: Seeds the README, index and backlog skeletons from references/templates.md.
rows.why: The pointer is cheap, and it keeps the shape consistent across projects.

rows.name: Antipatterns list
rows.does: Forbids forking parallel doc copies and editing archived plans for new work.
rows.why: The archived-plan rule already follows from the taxonomy, and a current model updates docs in place unprompted.

rows.name: Seed docs from skeletons
rows.does: Makes the session build a new or retrofitted docs/ library by copying these skeletons, substituting <project> and deferring style to the doctrine.
rows.why: This is the file's reason to exist, and the frame costs few words.

rows.name: Three-folder library taxonomy
rows.does: Fixes the layout: stable solution docs at the docs/ root, active plans in plans/, and finished history in archive/, each folder carrying its own README.
rows.why: The layout is kit-specific and needed, but the index, plans and archive READMEs restate the same folder roles three times.

rows.name: Plan file naming and versioning
rows.does: Names plans <project>_<content-type>_v<n>.md and makes the session bump the version instead of overwriting a prior plan.
rows.why: The doctrine points here for the file name, and a model would pick an arbitrary name without it.

rows.name: Status header drives lifecycle
rows.does: Tells the session that a plan's Status header value (Ready, In Progress or Complete) decides whether hooks show it as parked, offer it for resume or flag it as unarchived.
rows.why: The hooks key on these exact strings, and a model cannot guess the contract.

rows.name: Archive finished plans via git mv
rows.does: Moves a Complete or abandoned plan into archive/ with git mv in the same close-out, keeping its Chapters intact.
rows.why: The curating-docs SKILL owns the archive step, and this file repeats it in three READMEs.

rows.name: Related section cross-references
rows.does: Makes the session add a ## Related section when one plan relates to or supersedes another.
rows.why: It costs almost nothing, and a model would not add the section consistently without being told.

rows.name: Archive immutability rule
rows.does: Forbids editing or deleting archived plans and routes new work to a new cross-referenced plan.
rows.why: The rule matters, but one sentence carries it where the file spends a whole README's Rules block plus the folder-map line.

rows.name: Backlog active-only with quarterly pruning
rows.does: Keeps backlog.md to active items only and moves done items into archive/backlog-YYYY-QN.md instead of striking them through.
rows.why: The convention is needed, but the file states it in four places: the index, the archive README, the backlog preamble and the Snapshots section.

rows.name: Dated backlog items and re-aging
rows.does: Gives every backlog item a parked date in a fixed shape, puts a fresh date first when an item is kept at the aging check, and backfills a date for any item that lacks one.
rows.why: The surfacing layers parse the first date on each line, so the exact format is load-bearing and cannot be inferred.

rows.name: Backlog versus plan Chapters
rows.does: Keeps per-plan history in the plan's Chapters and reserves the backlog for next-steps that span efforts.
rows.why: Without this line a session would log plan history into the backlog, and the placement rule is short.

rows.name: Backlog snapshot file template
rows.does: Gives the append-only quarterly snapshot file its format, one dated line per item with its outcome.
rows.why: It is a compact format that the pruning mechanism depends on.

rows.name: Index and plan-list placeholders
rows.does: Makes the session list active plans with one-line descriptions, or write "None at present." when the list is empty.
rows.why: A model fills an index unprompted, so only the empty-list wording carries anything the model would not do anyway.

rows.name: Stable-doc and plan purpose prose
rows.does: Carries descriptive boilerplate inside the skeletons: what the library is for, that a plan is the single source of truth, and that the archive is the project's memory.
rows.why: This is template filler that repeats doctrine the session already holds, and a model writes equivalent framing unprompted.

rows.name: Trigger and scope routing
rows.does: The frontmatter description says when to load the council: at a material, hard-to-reverse design fork. It also routes code review to adversarial-reviewer and a stuck mid-run session to the consult skill.
rows.why: Routing against sibling skills is kit-specific and needed, but the long parenthetical contrasting it with the consult could be a single clause.

rows.name: Opening purpose statement
rows.does: Summarizes the protocol: lenses argue through a neutral facilitator, and evidence, not capitulation, settles each disagreement.
rows.why: It restates what sections 2 to 5 already make the session do, and it adds no action of its own.

rows.name: Three roles, orchestrator not judge
rows.does: Defines the orchestrator, the council-member agents and a separate design-facilitator agent, and bars the orchestrator from judging convergence.
rows.why: A model left alone would judge convergence itself, and the separation between orchestrator and facilitator is the whole point of the design.

rows.name: Operator opt-in check
rows.does: Makes the session confirm the operator opted in before dispatching any agent.
rows.why: The cost-and-yes step in Frame already gates the dispatch, so this second gate is redundant, and it sits awkwardly beside the doctrine's standing dispatch request.

rows.name: Frame fork as outcome
rows.does: Makes the session state the decision as an end state, with example wording, rather than as a pre-chosen solution, and list the candidate approaches.
rows.why: Models tend to frame a fork as its favored solution, which biases the whole council, and the example makes the rule stick.

rows.name: Default lenses and swaps
rows.does: Sets the default lenses to performance, maintainability and risk-security, with the last reading docs/security-model.md, and allows swapping in a data-model lens or a steelman of the unfavored option.
rows.why: This is a house default the model cannot guess, and the steelman swap guards against a lopsided council.

rows.name: Name cost, await yes
rows.does: Makes the session state the cost as seats times the round cap and proceed only on the operator's yes.
rows.why: A multi-agent fan-out spends real money, and the formula is cheap to state.

rows.name: Blind parallel first round
rows.does: Dispatches members separately and in parallel, each with a verbatim brief of outcome, approaches, lens, paths and the read-only rule, and none sees another's brief or output.
rows.why: Independence is what makes the council worth running, and a model would otherwise share context or run the members serially.

rows.name: Evidence-grounded positions only
rows.does: Requires each position to rest on evidence the member actually read, plus its strongest objection to each alternative, and gives ungrounded claims no weight.
rows.why: This belongs to the council-member charter, which is the surface doing the work, so one owner would do.

rows.name: Facilitator output and statuses
rows.does: Makes the facilitator return an agreement map, attributed disagreements with their cruxes, and a status of CONVERGED, ANOTHER_ROUND with per-member questions, or DEADLOCK.
rows.why: The orchestrator branches on this status vocabulary, so it has to know it, although the charter probably also carries the format.

rows.name: Capitulation versus evidence classing
rows.does: Makes the facilitator label each resolved point as evidence-resolved or capitulation, and flag uncited caving as soft convergence.
rows.why: This is the facilitator's job and belongs in the design-facilitator charter rather than restated here.

rows.name: Distrust one-round convergence
rows.does: Makes the session treat a first-round CONVERGED as suspect, since correlated models may simply be agreeing.
rows.why: Same-model agreement is a real failure, and a session would otherwise take early consensus at face value.

rows.name: Cross-examination re-dispatch
rows.does: On ANOTHER_ROUND, re-dispatches the named members as fresh agents with the transcript, their prior position and the facilitator's question. Each must concede, rebut with evidence or revise, and report what it held.
rows.why: The brief contents for a fresh agent are kit-specific, and without them the round degrades into restated positions.

rows.name: Stop conditions, cap three
rows.does: Stops the rounds on CONVERGED, on DEADLOCK, or at a round cap that defaults to three.
rows.why: The cap is a house number that bounds cost, and a model cannot infer it.

rows.name: Synthesis with forks prominent
rows.does: Presents the converged recommendation with evidence and trade-offs, and gives any unresolved fork prominence as the operator's decision, stating what each option optimizes for.
rows.why: Models tend to bury a dissent under a tidy recommendation, and this keeps the choice visible.

rows.name: No forced consensus on deadlock
rows.does: On a deadlock or a cap hit, makes the session return 'unresolved - standing positions follow' and show the positions without forcing agreement.
rows.why: Papering over disagreement is the failure the council exists to prevent, and the fixed phrase is cheap.

rows.name: Council informs, never decides
rows.does: States that the operator makes the call and the council only informs it.
rows.why: It takes ten words and pins decision authority.

rows.name: Record decision in plan
rows.does: Makes the session record the operator's decision and rationale in the plan doc, pointing to the doctrine's decision bullet.
rows.why: The doctrine's 'Surface decisions in batches' bullet already owns this, so a bare pointer would do.

rows.name: Operator cost envelope
rows.does: Says the operator can cut the roster, cap the rounds or decline at any point.
rows.why: The operator can always do this, and a model already honors a cut, so the section changes nothing.

rows.name: Provenance note
rows.does: Credits the Converge concept in DheerG/swarms and says the protocol runs without the experimental agent-teams harness.
rows.why: This is attribution and history, not instruction, and it drives no session behavior; it could move to a README or the commit history.

rows.name: Headings and title
rows.does: Structures the document into numbered steps.
rows.why: The numbered steps give a scannable order at trivial cost.

rows.name: No-stop completion contract
rows.does: Makes the session run every unblocked section to completion without progress stops, check-ins or capacity-based pauses, backed by an excuse table and red-flag phrases.
rows.why: Current models do stop early at section boundaries, so the rule is needed, but the rule, one reason and the red-flag phrases would do in a third of the words.

rows.name: Closed blocker set, BLOCKED prefix
rows.does: Limits stops to four blocker classes and requires the message to open with a literal 'BLOCKED: <need>' line followed by a client-briefing decision brief, with capacity refused as a reason.
rows.why: The Stop hook releases only on the exact prefix, so a session cannot guess this format.

rows.name: Expert ask before blocking
rows.does: Sends a blocker to a live expert seat, then notifies the coordinator, before declaring BLOCKED, without letting the ask gate the work.
rows.why: The route and the seats belong to peer-sessions and coordinator, so one pointer plus the never-gates rule would do here.

rows.name: Consult before decision blockers
rows.does: Runs a fresh-context consult on any decision-shaped blocker after the expert ask and before declaring, splitting fact questions from preference questions.
rows.why: The consult skill already owns its triggers, so this can be a one-line pointer.

rows.name: Public-board first-line cap
rows.does: Keeps the BLOCKED or WAITING first line under 120 printable ASCII characters, with repo-relative paths, because it travels to a coordinator board.
rows.why: The cap is needed but is stated twice here, along with readership analysis the security-model doc already carries.

rows.name: WAITING stop and park shapes
rows.does: Ends a turn with a 'WAITING:' lead that names pending dispatch ids when only background subagents remain, and handles operator-requested parks with hallmark checks on pending dispatches.
rows.why: The prefix and the dispatch-wait rule are kit-specific and needed, but the park sub-cases for probe windows and synthetic-only pairs make up most of the words and seldom fire.

rows.name: Leash binding and non-arming
rows.does: Tells the session that only the operator's typed /kit-goal arms a leash, and that a run with no leash, or one bound elsewhere, proceeds unleashed.
rows.why: The kit-goal skill owns the leash, so a single sentence saying never arm or clear it would do.

rows.name: Mid-run arriving plan intake
rows.does: Takes on a plan that arrives mid-run once its standing is verified, queues it after current work, asks for --append on leashed runs, and replies to the sender in peer vocabulary.
rows.why: The rule is needed for multi-session setups, but the standing check and reply vocabulary are peer-sessions' and are restated here.

rows.name: Handoff one-line announcement
rows.does: Says in one line that execution is switching to autonomous mode for N sections.
rows.why: It is cheap, and it gives the operator a chance to scope the run down that a model would not offer unprompted.

rows.name: Resume by rereading plan doc
rows.does: Reads the plan doc and all Chapters in full, and after compaction re-invokes the skill and reloads deferred tools before touching files.
rows.why: The doctrine's durable-artifacts bullet already states the compaction reload, so only the Chapters-are-state point is new.

rows.name: No approval re-ask, Status flip
rows.does: Treats a plan handed to the session as approved, flips its Status to In Progress, never flips Complete, and records the change in the first Chapter.
rows.why: Models reflexively ask 'shall I proceed?', and the Status value and fingerprint rules are kit contracts.

rows.name: Execution-time intake gap routing
rows.does: Lists each section's unstated gaps before dispatch, raises material ones as BLOCKED or asks, and records the rest on the Chapter's Assumptions line rather than the frozen Assumptions section.
rows.why: Where the answer is written is a kit contract, because of the fingerprint freeze, and a model would put it in the wrong place.

rows.name: memq recall at start
rows.does: Runs memq recall once before the first section and on resume, carries the relevant records forward, stamps applied ones, and checks for the wrong-store tells.
rows.why: memq is a kit tool that the model cannot know to run.

rows.name: External-engine stand-down
rows.does: Runs only the directed section when an external engine or KIT_EXTERNAL_ENGINE drives continuation, while still orchestrating and dispatching.
rows.why: It is a kit-specific contract, and a model would otherwise run the whole plan.

rows.name: Disjoint files from siblings
rows.does: Owns files disjoint from sibling sessions and never stages or commits another session's work.
rows.why: The doctrine's Scope and Safety section already carries this.

rows.name: Step 0 checkpoint clear
rows.does: Runs kit-compact-checkpoint.js clear at each section start on a leashed run, and reads a refusal as the new-session-id case to proceed unleashed.
rows.why: It is a kit hook verb that is needed for the compaction gate to work.

rows.name: Lightweight approach confirmation read
rows.does: Reads the files a section touches to confirm the spec's assumed mechanism before implementing, adjusting and noting any material difference.
rows.why: Current models read before editing unprompted, so only the no-fan-out bound and the note-in-Chapter part add value.

rows.name: Standing Brief Amendments grep
rows.does: Greps the plan doc's amendments block at every section open and treats each entry as binding in briefs and inline work.
rows.why: The block is a kit construct that is written mid-run, so a stale read is a real failure.

rows.name: docs/ writes stay main-thread
rows.does: Routes any section writing under docs/ to the main thread and records Locus: inline while keeping the tier.
rows.why: A guard blocks agent writes there, so without this rule dispatches fail.

rows.name: Dispatch Brief template
rows.does: Fills a required-field brief for implementers, including scope, acceptance, tests, sibling pattern, hostile-boundary reuse, the whole-worktree git prohibition, claim marking, the absence-check clause, style paths, the box budget and the grant audit.
rows.why: The field list is needed because agents inherit nothing, but the absence-check clause alone runs about 600 words that repeat the doctrine's withheld-control rule and could be a verbatim-copied short clause.

rows.name: Fable capacity reading
rows.does: Runs capacity-read.js before any fable override and acts on its dispatch, ladder-governs or downgrade verdict, with different handling for reviewer and implementer sites.
rows.why: The tool call is kit-specific and needed, but the per-site downgrade branches are over-elaborated.

rows.name: Inline locus rules
rows.does: Implements Locus: inline sections in the main thread, dispatches briefable untiered ones, and corrects legacy Model values.
rows.why: It is short, and the routing is kit vocabulary.

rows.name: Implementer status handling
rows.does: Routes NEEDS_CONTEXT, BLOCKED and DONE_WITH_CONCERNS returns to a re-dispatch, consult, design stop or out-of-scope route.
rows.why: The status vocabulary and its routes are kit contracts.

rows.name: Tier escalation ladder
rows.does: Escalates a haiku section after one failed round and higher tiers after two, compares the two rounds' Criticals to choose escalation or a premise consult, and counts wedges as environment faults.
rows.why: The escalate-or-consult rule is valuable, but the Fable-session branches and wedge accounting could be a quarter of the length.

rows.name: Subagents never stage or commit
rows.does: Keeps implementer edits unstaged so that the orchestrator's explicit git add after review serves as the scope check.
rows.why: Without it, agents commit by habit and the scope check disappears.

rows.name: Quiet agent and wait shapes
rows.does: Treats silence as work in progress short of the wedge hallmark, takes the first-turn reading, prefers the WAITING turn end over synchronous dispatch, and TaskStops an agent before replacing it.
rows.why: Stop-before-replace is needed, but the hallmark mechanics are finishing-work's and are partly restated here.

rows.name: Verify with evidence, fail-dangerous hunt
rows.does: Runs the build and targeted tests itself, reports gate numbers with tree state, reads implementer diffs, and hunts named fail-dangerous and call-site bug patterns.
rows.why: Models accept a subagent's DONE too easily, and the named pattern list catches real defects that suites miss.

rows.name: Tree-mutating probe exclusivity
rows.does: Runs a mutating probe only with no agents in flight, copies files to .kit/ first, restores from the copies, and never uses git checkout --.
rows.why: The doctrine's Tests section already carries this nearly word for word.

rows.name: Review roster and blind contract
rows.does: Dispatches the adversarial and blind reviewers in parallel, adds security and performance lenses on triggers and the document pair for Audience sections, and keeps every blind brief free of intent.
rows.why: The roster and the blind-brief property test are kit-defined, and a model would leak intent without them.

rows.name: Lens tiers, amendments, trace target
rows.does: Ranks lenses into correctness and advisory tiers and specifies which dispatches carry the Amendments in effect and Trace target lines.
rows.why: The rule is needed, but it is written as layered exceptions that a short matrix could state.

rows.name: Reviewer contention predicate
rows.does: Checks whether a sibling holds the repo's one shared resource, and if so carries a workspace-constraint line into reviewer briefs.
rows.why: The doctrine's box-budget rule covers this.

rows.name: Reviewer tier, effort, Workflow route
rows.does: Sets each reviewer's model one tier up, sets effort by an effort table, routes non-default effort through Workflow agent() with a required agentType, model and effort template, and handles re-aims and compensation.
rows.why: The agentType/model/effort template prevents a real safety gap, but the table plus its prose restatement plus the compensation theory run about three times longer than needed.

rows.name: Never pre-judge reviewers
rows.does: Forbids telling reviewers what to flag or how to rate, while allowing repo-wide defect classes that pass the blind property test.
rows.why: Models naturally steer reviewers toward agreement, so this is a real failure to guard.

rows.name: Round tree-state bracket
rows.does: Captures git status before and after each review round and treats an unexplained delta as an incident: restore, record, re-review, kaizen.
rows.why: The check is worth keeping, but the authorship-by-content reasoning is long for a rare event.

rows.name: Document Review Brief
rows.does: Fills a template for the blind-reader and prose-reviewer dispatches covering paths, Reader, Audience, Voice, fact base and prose-register paths.
rows.why: It is a kit input contract that the model cannot infer.

rows.name: Minor list and close pass
rows.does: Logs Minors to a .kit/ scratch file and fixes them in one pass after the loop ends, skipping any fix that would owe a round.
rows.why: Batching Minors is useful, but the file mechanics are over-specified.

rows.name: Advisory finding disposition
rows.does: Gives each security or performance Critical or Major one line of fix, defer or refuse, with a scope-adjudicator relevance ruling on fix-now and on cited security Criticals.
rows.why: It is one roughly 850-word paragraph of branching cases, and its core, disposition each finding and rule relevance on cited Criticals, fits in about 150 words.

rows.name: Claim versus behavior class
rows.does: Splits findings into behavior findings, which have a failure scenario, and claim findings, which are sentence-only, and rates claims Minor except on published contract surfaces with four allowed claim dispositions.
rows.why: The distinction stops review loops over wording, but it is stated across three places.

rows.name: Major provenance classification
rows.does: Classifies each correctness Major as spec-traceable, fix-introduced or new-requirement from its trace, verifying the trace both ways, and holds new-requirement Majors out of fix rounds.
rows.why: Holding unasked requirements prevents real scope creep, but the precedence and exemption prose is heavy.

rows.name: Per-round fix diff captures
rows.does: Captures a git diff of the section's scope at every round, plus --no-index appends for untracked paths, so that fix-introduced lines can be computed.
rows.why: The orchestrator can judge fix-introduced from the round it just ran, and the capture procedure costs more than a misclassification does.

rows.name: Held-finding judge and buckets
rows.does: Sends a new-requirement Major to an expert seat or the scope-adjudicator, adopts a refuse, accept-and-declare or ask bucket after a GROUNDS check, and records it as amendment bullets.
rows.why: An outside scope judge is useful, but the answer-window, NEEDS_CONTEXT and record-placement rules could be compressed by half or more.

rows.name: Add-decision line, design stop
rows.does: Writes a five-part add-decision line for each section and each fix-bound Major, and sends any fix adding an unnamed mechanism to the scope-adjudicator before building.
rows.why: Stopping unasked guards before they are built is a good gate, but its interactions with the escalation ladder and the reversal consult are over-enumerated.

rows.name: Fifth-round review backstop
rows.does: Stops a section on a fixed-first-line BLOCKED after five unresolved review rounds, with a phase analysis, a memq log, three-round continuations and freeze exceptions.
rows.why: A round cap is worth having, but this spends about 1500 words on precedence against other stops in a rare event.

rows.name: Loop termination and fix-delta bar
rows.does: Ends the review loop on the first round with no correctness Critical, no undisposed owed Major and no owed round, where a round is owed for outward actions, new modules or tests liable to be routed around.
rows.why: The exit condition is needed, but it can be stated as three bullets and a short bar.

rows.name: Recurrence amendment rule
rows.does: Amends the Standing Brief Amendments block when a behavior finding class recurs across sections, so later sections inherit the guard.
rows.why: It is a cheap way for learning to propagate, and a model would not do it unprompted.

rows.name: Close gate and adoption trigger
rows.does: Runs the section-close lane after fixes, and writes any adopted change to the brief inputs into the amendments block and the Intent section before the next dispatch.
rows.why: These are kit bookkeeping contracts that later dispatches depend on.

rows.name: Out-of-scope surface route
rows.does: Sends every surface outside Files in scope to a fold, an appended section, or a handoff or backlog entry, never leaves it only in a report, and never parks a correctness Critical.
rows.why: Models otherwise drop found work in reports, but the fold predicate and append mechanics can be tighter.

rows.name: Plan update, reopen earlier docs
rows.does: Marks the section complete, syncs the spec to deviations, and corrects documents from earlier sections that describe behavior this section changed.
rows.why: Stale earlier-section docs are a real, non-obvious failure.

rows.name: Applied-stamp adjudication
rows.does: Runs memq unstamped over the window since the last Chapter at each boundary, stamps or skips each record, and records the result on a Stamps line.
rows.why: It is kit-tool bookkeeping for memory telemetry, with modest value per section that does not justify the window warnings.

rows.name: Commit model application
rows.does: Applies Review-Only, Branch-and-PR first-green commits, or Commit-and-Push with a whole gate before any push to an install-surface main, and handles backlog entries riding along.
rows.why: The models are kit contracts, but the gate-moment and shared-file hold prose restates doctrine.

rows.name: Checkpoint open or boundary declare
rows.does: Runs kit-compact-checkpoint.js open after each Chapter, or boundary when unleashed, and flags a run nearing its limit while compaction is deferred.
rows.why: The hook verbs are needed, but the explanation of the valve and the refusals is long.

rows.name: Interim board entry
rows.does: Appends a headed interim entry with no Completed line after two review rounds with no closure, or on a deferral nudge, then opens the checkpoint.
rows.why: It is the recovery spine for long sections, and its shape is a machine contract.

rows.name: Consult pointer
rows.does: Distinguishes the consult from the expert ask and the reviewers and points to the consult skill.
rows.why: The consult skill already owns it.

rows.name: Orchestrator role and brief context
rows.does: Keeps the orchestrator as designer, keeps work inline only when it is design-entangled, tiny or mid-debug, and carries memory and standing directives verbatim because subagents inherit none.
rows.why: Models over-assume subagent context, so this prevents underbriefed dispatches.

rows.name: Files for bulk, inline reports
rows.does: Hands specs and diffs to agents as .kit/ files, and has reports return in the final message with bulky findings in scratch.
rows.why: It is a short house convention that keeps committed files and context clean.

rows.name: Disjoint parallelism, staggered sections
rows.does: Runs sections concurrently only on disjoint files, offset rather than in lockstep, and closes each the moment it clears.
rows.why: It is short, and lockstep batching is a common orchestration mistake.

rows.name: Guards outrank briefs
rows.does: Routes around PreToolUse guards rather than widening scope in a brief, and brackets ungoverned read-only dispatches with git status.
rows.why: A model would assume brief text controls agent capability, and it does not.

rows.name: Scout banding and returns
rows.does: Uses the default model for closed fact-checks and sonnet for discovery, never top-model recon, with file:line lead returns.
rows.why: It is a cheap cost-control default that a model would not pick unprompted.

rows.name: Serialize shared environment
rows.does: Keeps one agent per worktree on shared state and runs long suites through one controller.
rows.why: The doctrine's sequencing bullet owns this.

rows.name: Chapter format template
rows.does: Appends a Chapter with fixed fields: Completed, Implemented By, Metrics, Decisions, Failed approaches, Assumptions, Review Findings, Stamps, Gate, Next, Commit Model and Delta.
rows.why: The template is a machine contract that must stay, but the Gate field description alone runs about 500 words of probe-corpus quoting rules.

rows.name: Metrics and ruling tallies
rows.does: Defines how closed, consults, provenance tokens and rulings are counted, and reconciles why the tallies differ.
rows.why: It is experiment bookkeeping whose reconciliation rules cost more attention than a slightly miscounted metric costs.

rows.name: kit-size Delta reading
rows.does: Runs kit-size.js report against the project root on every Chapter and quotes the output verbatim with a moment-pin.
rows.why: It is a kit tool, but the path and caveat prose exceeds what the tool's own docs already own.

rows.name: Chapter machine contract hygiene
rows.does: Keeps author lines from opening with Completed:, Next: or #, pins every figure with its moment, and points to curating-docs for the frozen shape.
rows.why: Breaking the parsed shape silently breaks external tooling.

rows.name: Finishing handoff
rows.does: Invokes finishing-work at the end, even under Review-Only.
rows.why: Without it, a model stops at the last section.

rows.name: Ordered finishing steps with parallelism
rows.does: Runs the nine steps in order, with steps 2 and 3 dispatched together after step 1, then step 4 and step 5.
rows.why: The kit defines the sequence, and a model cannot infer it.

rows.name: Deduplicate against section reviews
rows.does: Tells the finishing reviewers what the section reviews already cleared, and folds the advisory lenses into one adversarial pass on small efforts.
rows.why: The cohesion-over-cleared-code point is worth keeping, but the rule for labelling folded lenses and routing their verdicts is overbuilt for how often it comes up.

rows.name: Finishing reviewer tier and route
rows.does: Dispatches every finishing reviewer at fable and high effort through the Workflow agent() Reviewer Dispatch template, falling back to the Agent tool.
rows.why: The tier choice and route are house decisions the model cannot guess.

rows.name: Unavailability trigger definitions
rows.does: Confirms that a gate could not run at its tier only from a dispatch error, a silent substitution, or two consecutive stopped dispatches, never from expectation.
rows.why: The two triggers need about 60 words, and the epistemics of what each trigger proves is commentary.

rows.name: Resolved-model transcript tally
rows.does: Parses message.model from the transcript's assistant lines, maps aliases to versioned ids, and classifies a run as zero-match, mixed or unreadable.
rows.why: Detecting substitution is real, but the handling of undefined, synthetic and unreadable cases is edge-case law that could live in a script or reference file.

rows.name: Wedge hallmark before killing
rows.does: Forbids killing a quiet dispatch unless it reads running, has shown no liveness for its window, and has not answered a SendMessage probe.
rows.why: Without this rule a model kills slow agents and discards their work, and the doctrine points here as the owner.

rows.name: Byte-growth liveness reading
rows.does: Measures transcript byte growth at the agent's own path with a live-sibling control, switches to assistant-line counts after the probe, and falls back to elapsed time.
rows.why: The instrument is needed, but its control and path caveats run far past what a rule plus one reason takes, and this detail belongs in a tool.

rows.name: Workflow probe addressing and run stop
rows.does: Probes a Workflow agent at its agent id, and TaskStops the whole run when that id cannot be recovered and the fallback windows have closed.
rows.why: The addressing quirk is harness-specific and cannot be guessed, and getting it wrong leaves a multi-hour wait.

rows.name: Never-started and synthetic-fault shapes
rows.does: Routes a dispatch with zero turns or synthetic-only lines on a pair of grep counts, using a user-line control, short five-minute windows and a stop-first re-dispatch.
rows.why: The harness fault is real, but the grep spellings, the control and the routing law are script material inflating a skill that every session loads.

rows.name: Hallmark evaluation cadence and timers
rows.does: Evaluates the wedge on three kinds of wake, arms self-wake timers for each window, and explains why synchronous dispatches are diagnosed after they return.
rows.why: The rule to arm a timer and check at wakes needs one paragraph, not four.

rows.name: Per-class window lengths
rows.does: Sets a growth window of 15 minutes and a probe window of 12 for review-class dispatches, 30 and 12 for the qa-verifier and docs-curator, and 5 and 5 for never-started, erring long.
rows.why: The numbers are needed, but the justification, including a measured 69-second property, is journey text and not a rule.

rows.name: Post-stop retry ladder by class
rows.does: Allows one same-model retry and then routes by class: reviewers compensate, qa and curator steps self-run, scouts are re-dispatched or dropped, and implementers go to executing-work.
rows.why: The class routing is kit-specific and needed, but the prose restates the chain bounds several times.

rows.name: Opus max compensation route
rows.does: Re-dispatches a failed reviewer through Workflow at opus and max effort under the same agentType, with a bare Agent-tool opus fallback.
rows.why: This is a concrete kit contract a model cannot invent.

rows.name: Record compensation and ungated gates
rows.does: Records the trigger, shapes, evidence and compensated-or-fallback status in the final Chapter and the close-out, so no downgrade passes unremarked.
rows.why: Surfacing a downgrade matters, but the evidence catalog repeats the triggers.

rows.name: Tree-state porcelain bracket
rows.does: Captures git status --porcelain before each of the review rounds in steps 1 to 4 and compares when each round returns, treating a delta as an incident.
rows.why: The check is worth one sentence, while the two paragraphs of blind spots (gitignored writes, ref plumbing) exceed what a session acts on.

rows.name: Compaction boundary during finishing
rows.does: Appends an Interim board entry and opens the compaction checkpoint when the deferral nudge fires between finishing steps.
rows.why: This is the kit-specific hook integration, and the skill says it is the only owner of it.

rows.name: Base ref derivation per model
rows.does: Derives the effort's base ref under each commit model, including the git-log walk to the first commit that added a Chapter, and records it as a sha.
rows.why: A wrong base silently scopes every review, and the derivation is non-obvious.

rows.name: Base ref sanity check
rows.does: Compares the changeset listing against the plan's Files in scope lines and surfaces unexpected entries, with three expected-surfacing exceptions.
rows.why: The check earns its place, but the exception list could be a single clause.

rows.name: QA verifier dispatch
rows.does: Dispatches the qa-verifier with the spec path for a full build, the full suite and evidence on every acceptance criterion, and fixes any FAIL before proceeding.
rows.why: The core gate is short and the kit names the agent.

rows.name: Two whole gates plus contention lane
rows.does: Runs the whole gate again after the last tree change with the contention lane beside it, and fills the Gate line from that run.
rows.why: The doctrine's lane bullet and step 6 already carry the timing of the gates.

rows.name: Operator-only unverifiable split
rows.does: Fixes an environmental blocker and re-runs, and carries only genuinely operator-only criteria into the handoff.
rows.why: Models do push effortful checks onto the operator, and this line prevents it.

rows.name: Advisory review dispatch and disposition
rows.does: Dispatches the performance and security reviewers over the whole changeset and fixes, defers or refuses each finding on the interim board.
rows.why: The dispatch is needed, and the disposition is executing-work's, restated here.

rows.name: Prose-only review waiver
rows.does: Skips the advisory reviews only when every file is prose and no document has an outside audience, treating SKILL.md and agent charters as config.
rows.why: The two predicates fit in 60 words, and the voiding cases are over-elaborated.

rows.name: Disclosure sweep blocking
rows.does: Has the security lens sweep documents against the spec's Disclosure list, and treats a hit as a blocking Critical.
rows.why: This is a confidentiality gate for client-facing work that a model would not run unprompted.

rows.name: Threat model absent carry
rows.does: Carries 'write the threat model' to Operator Verification and the backlog when the security lens reports none.
rows.why: It is cheap and otherwise the gap is lost at archive.

rows.name: Fix-round terminal and counting
rows.does: Ends finishing fix rounds on executing-work's terminal condition and backstop, defining which lenses make up a round and which re-run on a fix delta.
rows.why: Executing-work owns the round unit, and a pointer plus the finishing deltas would do.

rows.name: New-requirement Major hold
rows.does: Applies the provenance read, the hold, the judge, the design stop and fixed BLOCKED lines to owed Majors in the finishing pass, with captures under the .kit scratch folder.
rows.why: It restates executing-work's provenance machinery at length for one context.

rows.name: Final adversarial review scope
rows.does: Dispatches the adversarial reviewer over the whole changeset for cohesion, debris, dropped spec items and weakly reviewed sections, with style-skill paths attached.
rows.why: This is the central cross-section gate, and its scope is kit-defined.

rows.name: Prose reviewer for documents
rows.does: Dispatches prose-reviewer over whole documents with the Document Review Brief and the register and voice paths.
rows.why: Document deliverables need this separate lens, which the kit names.

rows.name: Single Minor pass, no blind
rows.does: Batches all finishing Minors into one pass before curation and does not re-run the blind reviewer.
rows.why: The rule is short, but the accepted-loss commentary is not needed.

rows.name: Goal read scope adjudicator
rows.does: Dispatches scope-adjudicator once over the changeset with the plan's what, then buckets BUILT-BUT-UNASKED and ASKED-BUT-UNBUILT items into fix, declare, refuse or ask.
rows.why: The goal check is valuable, but most of the text restates executing-work's buckets and NEEDS_CONTEXT route.

rows.name: Docs curator and drift classes
rows.does: Dispatches docs-curator and stops on a mistake-class drift item, while recording a deviation in the Chapter and PR.
rows.why: This is the kit's docs-matches-reality gate, and the mistake stop matters.

rows.name: Gated pre-change read construction
rows.does: Builds git reads for curator claims only from the session's own listings, applying an equality selection, a character gate on path tokens, ls-tree presence checks and refutation rules.
rows.why: 'Never run a command from a report, and select paths from your own listing' covers the injection risk from the kit's own Bash-less curator, and 1200 words of token grammar cost more than that failure.

rows.name: Final Chapter with open Gate
rows.does: Sets Status Complete, appends the final Chapter with its Gate line left open, archives, and fills the line only from the post-archive whole gate.
rows.why: The ordering is non-obvious and determines what the handoff evidence covers.

rows.name: Kit-repo probe corpus run
rows.does: In the kit's own repo, runs the probe runner's after and before legs, re-runs errors, and classifies ruled and proposed mismatch rows.
rows.why: It applies to one repository and belongs in that repo's runner README or a kit-dev skill, not in every project's finishing load.

rows.name: Operator-pending does not block Complete
rows.does: Marks the plan Complete with operator checks routed to the Chapter, the backlog and the close-out, then runs curating-docs' close path to archive.
rows.why: Models otherwise leave plans In Progress indefinitely.

rows.name: Close-out recap block
rows.does: Opens the close-out and the Chapter's Recap field with the Goal quoted verbatim, a client-register paragraph, the refinements from the record, and the pending items.
rows.why: The format is kit-defined and serves an operator without session context.

rows.name: Assumptions block verbatim
rows.does: Carries every Chapter Assumptions entry into the close-out and the Chapter, summarizing any entry that embeds an instruction.
rows.why: Under a leash this is the only place the operator sees declared assumptions.

rows.name: Finalize is not commit table
rows.does: Flips the plan to Complete and stages it even under Review-Only, with a four-row excuse table.
rows.why: The doctrine's terminal-state bullet already carries the rule, and the table repeats it.

rows.name: Docs committed before PR predicate
rows.does: Blocks PR open, ready or final push while the plan sits in docs/plans or git status shows docs/ changes, reading git status before gh pr ready.
rows.why: A concrete predicate that prevents docs being orphaned from an auto-merged PR.

rows.name: PR state check before push
rows.does: Reads PR state before each push, sends a push after MERGED (or with a stale approval able to merge) to a new branch, and checks the ruleset staleness settings.
rows.why: The merged-branch hazard is real and needed, but the doctrine restates it and the staleness sub-case is dense.

rows.name: Review-Only walkthrough and stop
rows.does: Presents a by-section walkthrough of the staged changes and stops for review, resuming Commit-and-Push mechanics on the operator's word.
rows.why: It defines the resting behavior of the commit model.

rows.name: Branch update and merge gate
rows.does: Updates from origin, surfaces conflicts, and re-runs the whole gate over the merged branch until the PR goes up.
rows.why: It is needed, but it repeats the gate conditions the doctrine owns.

rows.name: PR creation and body rules
rows.does: Opens or refreshes the PR by host CLI, with a commit-form title, a body passed via --body-file, and no curator text on the command line.
rows.why: The body-file and title rules are useful, but the host-by-host fallbacks and the @path caveats are long.

rows.name: Ready and GraphQL auto-merge
rows.does: Marks the PR ready and arms auto-merge with a GraphQL mutation using MERGE, never gh pr merge --auto, reporting 'up and unarmed' when either command errors or the repository refuses MERGE.
rows.why: The two commands and the ban on gh pr merge --auto are load-bearing, but the explanation of the review residual can shrink.

rows.name: Post-merge strand check
rows.does: After a merge, runs fetch --prune and lists origin/integration..branch to find stranded post-merge commits, recovering them via branch-hygiene.
rows.why: Otherwise post-merge commits silently vanish, and a model would not check.

rows.name: Reap plan branch and worktree
rows.does: Deletes the plan's own merged branch and clean worktree by one of three location routes, or records the reap as owed.
rows.why: branch-hygiene owns the reap mechanics, so a pointer with the own-branch-only bound would do.

rows.name: Commit-and-Push push and teardown
rows.does: Confirms everything is pushed, gates an install-surface push, and in a worktree merges to main, gates, pushes, then removes the worktree and branch.
rows.why: The teardown is needed, but the gate discharge rule restates the doctrine.

rows.name: Bank learnings to memory
rows.does: Saves durable discoveries to the kit memory store rather than the plan doc, fixes wrong recalled memories, and folds hygiene into the edits.
rows.why: Short, and it points learnings at the right store.

rows.name: Unstamped memory sweep
rows.does: Runs memq unstamped over the stretch the Chapter sweeps left uncovered, then stamps or skips each hit.
rows.why: The memory-system skill owns the sweep and its window rules.

rows.name: After-query supersede with receipt
rows.does: Runs memq find over learned terms, supersedes overtaken records, logs journal outcomes, and reports the terms and read strength.
rows.why: The step is kit-specific, but the tier rules belong to memory-system.

rows.name: Decay pass when stale
rows.does: Runs the decay pass when memory/decay-stamp is older than 14 days, deferring the rest to memory-system.
rows.why: It is a trigger plus a pointer, and memory-system owns the rest.

rows.name: memq recent digest
rows.does: Runs memq recent over the session span and carries its digest unparaphrased into the close-out.
rows.why: It is cheap and a kit-specific command.

rows.name: Memory sync state reporting
rows.does: Reports memory writes as PENDING sync unless the doctor -Fix path runs, carrying a WARN into the close-out and stopping on a FAIL.
rows.why: The PENDING rule is needed, but the hand-path detail is memory-system's.

rows.name: Kaizen inbox check
rows.does: Ensures kit friction is in the kaizen inbox and offers a pass only when the inbox has pending items.
rows.why: It is minimal and kit-specific.

rows.name: Skill trigger and purpose
rows.does: Loads the skill for a kaizen pass and says one-off capture does not need it.
rows.why: The frontmatter routes loading, and the purpose line is two sentences with nothing to cut.

rows.name: Inbox file layout
rows.does: Places notes in per-machine append-only kaizen/notes-<machine>.md files and briefs in kaizen/briefs/, one file each.
rows.why: The paths are kit-defined, and without them a session cannot find or write the inbox.

rows.name: Pending-items predicate
rows.does: Defines pending as any note line or any brief file, and uses it to gate offers and the SessionStart nudge.
rows.why: It is the single gate shared by the hook and the offers, so it needs one exact statement.

rows.name: Capture is standing-authorized
rows.does: Lets any session append a note without approval or seat routing.
rows.why: The doctrine's Kaizen Capture section already states this grant, so the skill should point to it.

rows.name: Note push delta check
rows.does: Before a gateless note push, reads git log @{u}..HEAD and takes the exemption only when the note commit is the whole delta.
rows.why: The rule is real and non-obvious, but the push/delta argument is repeated and fits in three sentences.

rows.name: Public-board cap on notes
rows.does: Requires relative paths and bars the operator's words from notes, sending any friction that cannot meet the cap to the operator.
rows.why: A model would not infer this privacy cap, but the cross-references to executing-work and security-model add length without adding the rule.

rows.name: Locate kit clone via signpost
rows.does: Resolves kitRepoPath from ~/.claude/claude-kit.local.json, then a memq operator record, then a ~/.claude-kaizen fallback, and never uses the plugin cache.
rows.why: Writing to the plugin cache is a plausible silent failure, and the lookup chain is kit-specific, although the memq command details could be tightened.

rows.name: Worth-a-note bar
rows.does: Lists what counts as kit friction and what goes elsewhere or is skipped.
rows.why: The doctrine's capture bullet carries the same bar, so one owner should hold the list and the other should point to it.

rows.name: Lesson over incident
rows.does: Has each note state the lesson one level more general than the incident.
rows.why: The doctrine states this almost word for word.

rows.name: Zero notes is normal
rows.does: Stops the session from inventing notes it has to talk itself into.
rows.why: The doctrine says the same thing, and current models rarely over-capture unprompted.

rows.name: Seat standing disposition authority
rows.does: Lets the coordinator and kit-expert seats disposition notes without an operator round, and bounds that authority by the capture bar, material decisions and artifact-only dispatch.
rows.why: The authority is kit-defined and needed, but the three bounds restate general doctrine and role-skill rules.

rows.name: Attended versus unattended pass
rows.does: Adds the operator's retro half when the pass runs on an ask, an accepted offer or a pending brief.
rows.why: It is short and decides whether to ask the operator for their friction.

rows.name: Pull then pick lane
rows.does: Runs git pull and reads merge-versus-fast-forward from its output, running the whole gate plus the contention lane after a merge, with a parent-count fallback.
rows.why: The doctrine already says a merge takes the whole gate, so the parent-count forensics are more than the failure costs.

rows.name: Per-file note reads with counts
rows.does: Reads each notes file in a separate call and records its count so the clear can reconcile against it.
rows.why: Losing output silently past the output cap is a real harness failure, and the count feeds the reconciliation.

rows.name: Four dispositions triage
rows.does: Sorts each item into apply now, promote to a spec, route elsewhere, or park in the backlog with a signal.
rows.why: The disposition vocabulary and each one's destination are kit-defined and drive every pass.

rows.name: Rewrite owning passage, never append
rows.does: Lands each accepted lesson by rewriting the whole owning passage and its rationale ledger, and refuses bare appended sentences.
rows.why: Models default to appending, which is exactly the accretion this kit fights, so the steer changes behavior, though writing-skills could own it.

rows.name: Brief writing and archive
rows.does: Writes a brief per apply-now item, applies it under writing-skills with baseline tests, and archives it.
rows.why: It is the core apply step, and it is already terse.

rows.name: Line-wise clearing with reconciliation
rows.does: Clears handled notes line by line, never truncates, and checks removed lines against the triage record before committing.
rows.why: Concurrent appenders make this real, but the two-sided count reconciliation is spelled out at about twice the length the rule needs.

rows.name: Whole gate before kit push
rows.does: Runs the whole gate and the contention lane before pushing an applied brief to the kit's main.
rows.why: The doctrine and executing-work step 7 already own this, and the text admits it only points there.

rows.name: Promoted spec commit model
rows.does: Sends a promoted spec through its own recorded commit model.
rows.why: This is already true of every plan under curating-docs.

rows.name: Upstream changelog watch
rows.does: When claude --version differs from the recorded version, diffs the Claude Code changelog against harness-assumptions.md, advances the version, and files falsified beliefs as notes.
rows.why: No model would do this unprompted, and harness drift silently breaks kit assumptions, but it could move to its own owner.

rows.name: Brief format template
rows.does: Gives a self-contained brief a five-line Friction/Change/Acceptance/Discipline template.
rows.why: A fixed format lets a fresh session execute a brief, and it costs very few words.

rows.name: Offering a pass
rows.does: Offers a pass in one dismissable line, only at close-out or wrap-up and only when items are pending.
rows.why: Without it, sessions would either never offer a pass or nag the operator with offers.

rows.name: Skill trigger description
rows.does: Loads the skill after an install or update, when a kit capability misbehaves, or on a request to run the doctor.
rows.why: The frontmatter is how the harness routes to this skill, and it is already short.

rows.name: Doctor search path order
rows.does: Makes the session try the installed plugin copy, then the configured clone, then the cwd repo root, and take the first that exists.
rows.why: The paths and the claude-kit.local.json key are kit-specific, so a model cannot guess them.

rows.name: Installed copy is verdict
rows.does: Treats the installed copy's report as the machine's verdict, uses a clone run only to check the clone, and prescribes claude plugin update when the cache lags.
rows.why: The rule is needed, but the INFO 'trails the checkout' detail and the per-step clone notes duplicate what the report itself prints.

rows.name: Verify doctor provenance first
rows.does: Checks for plugin.json beside the located doctor.cmd before running it, and surfaces it instead of running it if the check fails.
rows.why: Running an arbitrary doctor.cmd found at the cwd is a real code-execution risk, and a model would not check provenance unprompted.

rows.name: Invoke cmd not ps1
rows.does: Runs the .cmd wrapper rather than the .ps1 script.
rows.why: It is cheap and avoids an execution-policy failure the model could not predict.

rows.name: Check mode runs first
rows.does: Runs the doctor with no flags first, shows the PASS/WARN/FAIL lines, and summarizes each WARN or FAIL in one line with its remedy.
rows.why: It sets the default safe mode and the report shape, both of which are kit-defined.

rows.name: Fix only on operator word
rows.does: Runs -Fix only on the operator's word and lists the things -Fix repairs and deletes.
rows.why: The consent gate matters, but the enumerated repair list duplicates what the doctor's own prompts show and will drift as the doctor changes.

rows.name: Fix -Yes consent semantics
rows.does: States that -Yes only pre-answers consent already given, and requires asking in chat before an install through a tool shell whose stdin is redirected.
rows.why: Without the text a session would pass -Yes to get past the declined prompts on a redirected stdin and so bypass consent.

rows.name: Exit code interpretation
rows.does: Reads exit 0 with warnings as a working install and exit 1 as broken, or as a rejected flag when no report printed.
rows.why: The two meanings of exit 1 are not guessable, and misreading them sends the session to fix the install instead of the command line.

rows.name: Doctrine import WARN handling
rows.does: Reads a doctrine-differs WARN as plugin/clone skew that the refresh hook resolves, and forbids copying doctrine files by hand.
rows.why: The one needed rule is 'never hand-copy, the hook resyncs'. The skew edge cases can be cut to a line.

rows.name: Memory sync credential gate
rows.does: Makes the session read Memory sync before any push, treat every FAIL as credentials in reach, and apply the remedy for each FAIL class (unmanaged files, allowlist drift, leaks in history, unanswered probes).
rows.why: A credential leak into a synced repo cannot be undone, and the rule that -Fix cannot clear history leaks is exactly what a model would get wrong.

rows.name: memq shim line semantics
rows.does: Explains how the memq shim line compares ~/.claude/bin with the payload copies and when -Fix reinstalls them.
rows.why: The report line already names its remedy, so a sentence saying so would do.

rows.name: Embedder line semantics
rows.does: Distinguishes absent from unusable for the embedding stack, notes that -Fix asks before its roughly 400 MB install, and notes that an empty index is normal before the first query.
rows.why: Only 'an empty index is normal' and 'find still works lexical-only' prevent a wrong action; the rest restates the report.

rows.name: Memory database line semantics
rows.does: Interprets the INFO, WARN and FAIL states of the SQL Server memory index, including missing prerequisites, fallback to the local index, and memq db-sync clearing the queue and staleness WARNs.
rows.why: It is the longest section and mostly reference detail the report lines print. The kept core is 'db-sync clears queued/stale WARNs, not missing pwsh/node'.

rows.name: Post-fix recheck and disclosure
rows.does: Re-runs check mode after -Fix, reports which lines flipped, and names each machine change such as PATH, execution policy or installed software.
rows.why: The doctrine's run-the-real-thing and name-what-you-changed-outside-the-code rules already carry this, so a pointer would do.

rows.name: Opening purpose statement
rows.does: States that one shipped command validates the install and names each fix.
rows.why: It is orientation only and changes no action.

rows.name: Leash concept and state file
rows.does: Tells the session that /kit-goal writes .kit/goal-state.json in the tree and a Stop hook holds the session to plan completion across compactions.
rows.why: Kit-defined mechanism a model cannot infer, and the short framing is proportionate.

rows.name: Ordered multi-plan queue
rows.does: Explains that several plan paths arm one queue that advances per plan and releases only on the last plan's terminal state.
rows.why: The auto-advance semantics are invisible without the text and govern when a session may stop.

rows.name: Operator-only arming, no self-arm
rows.does: Forbids a session from arming or re-arming a leash itself and makes it ignore leashes bound to other sessions.
rows.why: A model eager to finish a plan might self-arm, and the CLI transcript gate alone only covers the arm path, so the rule matters.

rows.name: Native goal versus kit-goal
rows.does: Routes non-plan goals to native /goal and plan sequencing to /kit-goal.
rows.why: The skill description already carries this routing, so the body line duplicates it.

rows.name: Arm CLI invocation and refusal
rows.does: Gives the arm command and path, says to report its one-line result, surface refusals without retrying, and lists the only two flags.
rows.why: The command path and no-retry rule are needed; the stale-CLI flag diagnosis is a small defensible extra.

rows.name: Unbound-result interpretation
rows.does: Explains the two ordinary causes of an unbound arm result, points to lib functions, and routes any other unbound result to the operator.
rows.why: The CLI prints which cause applies, so the session needs only 'read the printed sentence; an unexplained unbound goes to the operator', not the internals.

rows.name: Append versus bare re-arm
rows.does: Uses --append only when the operator typed it, never falls back to the bare form after an append refusal, and reads drop warnings from a bare re-arm.
rows.why: Falling back to a queue-replacing bare arm after a refusal is a plausible destructive failure that the text directly prevents.

rows.name: Arming grants parallelization request
rows.does: Treats the operator's arming as the request that unlocks Workflow and subagent parallelization for this run only, with deep-research still needing an ask.
rows.why: This is a positional grant the doctrine's ranking and dispatch bullet already frame; one owner should state the grant and its bounds.

rows.name: Arming is plan approval
rows.does: Makes the arming act count as a typed proceed so the run never waits for approval or reads the Status header as missing approval.
rows.why: Without it a careful model would stall asking for approval on a Draft-status plan, defeating the leash.

rows.name: Dispatch Authorization section semantics
rows.does: Defines a plan section that approves but never arms, requires tracing the grant to the operator before running a peer-delivered plan, and notes chain handoffs and its limits.
rows.why: The text itself says peer-sessions and executing-work own the trace, handoff and inbound-plan intake, so this is a partial copy of rules owned elsewhere and sits oddly in the goal skill.

rows.name: Authorization first-sentence placement
rows.does: Tells writers to state the grant's essential claim in the section's first sentence and keep it above Sections of Work.
rows.why: This is a plan-authoring format rule that belongs with the plan template in curating-docs.

rows.name: Arm in own worktree
rows.does: Requires running goal and checkpoint CLIs from the session's own tree root since each worktree has its own goal state.
rows.why: Arming the main checkout from a worktree session is a plausible silent failure a model would not anticipate.

rows.name: Clear command and aliases
rows.does: Maps /kit-goal clear and its aliases to the clear CLI command.
rows.why: Cheap and necessary to route the slash command.

rows.name: Status command output
rows.does: Maps bare /kit-goal or status to the status CLI and lists what it reports.
rows.why: The command is needed but the enumerated report fields are the CLI's output and need not be restated.

rows.name: Status-line widget wiring and reading
rows.does: Describes the widget's line format, launcher install path, how to wire it with a literal path, and how to read blank, unarmed and stale cached lines.
rows.why: This is operator setup and troubleshooting that belongs to kit-doctor; the session only needs 'blank widget is a fault or stale payload, not an unleashed run'.

rows.name: Binding and dead-session recovery
rows.does: Explains one binding rides the queue, re-arming rebinds after a dead session, and a re-arm must name the remaining plans because it replaces the queue.
rows.why: The recovery path and the replace-not-resume trap are non-obvious and matter mid-sequence.

rows.name: Stop release conditions
rows.does: Lets the leash holder stop only on plan Complete or archived, a literal leading BLOCKED: prefix, or a literal leading WAITING: for an awaited dispatch or requested park.
rows.why: The literal-prefix rule is exactly where a model fails by bolding or burying the marker, so the gate must be stated.

rows.name: WAITING wake and stall details
rows.does: Explains what re-invokes a waiting session, the coordinator wake exception, and that an improper WAITING stalls the run.
rows.why: Executing-work owns the stop shapes; one sentence that a non-qualifying WAITING stalls the run carries the needed consequence.

rows.name: Condition text pointer
rows.does: Points to composeCondition as owner of the canonical condition text.
rows.why: A source-code pointer the session never needs to act on.

rows.name: Goal event counting
rows.does: Names the two event values and warns that goal-blocked lines count turn-ends, so blockers must be deduped by identity.
rows.why: Relevant only to whoever analyzes the event log, so it should be one caution sentence here or moved to the kaizen or doctor analysis owner.

rows.name: Trigger-list skill description
rows.does: Makes the harness load the skill on a long list of memq verbs, field names and hook names.
rows.why: A description that enumerates about 60 trigger tokens costs context on every session listing, and a dozen core triggers would route as well.

rows.name: Store resolution order internals
rows.does: Explains how memq picks the store from the pin, the worktree main root, the transcript filing and the cwd, including the repository-boundary and nested-worktree cases.
rows.why: The CLI resolves the store itself, so the session needs only the one fact that a worktree shares its main checkout's store.

rows.name: Network share refusal semantics
rows.does: Tells the session that a share cwd is refused, which verbs slip past, and to read stderr because a refused read exits 0.
rows.why: The one thing to act on is 'a refused read exits 0 with empty stdout, so read stderr'. The per-verb flag carve-outs are code detail.

rows.name: Engine signals and pending tier
rows.does: Defines the fleet-worker environment variables and the per-run pending tier that the rest of the document refers to.
rows.why: This is kit vocabulary no model can know, but two sentences carry it.

rows.name: Independence from auto-memory
rows.does: Says the kit store works whatever the auto-memory setting is, and a duplicate index may appear.
rows.why: Knowing this changes no action the session takes.

rows.name: Never hand-edit journal sidecars
rows.does: Forbids hand edits to outcomes.jsonl and usage.jsonl, and catalogues the residue a shared-tier delete can leave behind.
rows.why: The rule is essential, but the residue catalogue belongs in the Delete bullet or in the code.

rows.name: Single journal pointer line
rows.does: Keeps journal entries out of MEMORY.md, apart from one verbatim pointer line.
rows.why: The exact line is a kit format that the model cannot guess.

rows.name: memq command reference table
rows.does: Lists every memq verb with its flags, caps, tier targeting, refusals, grant status and writes.
rows.why: The CLI is essential knowledge, but each row carries paragraphs of edge-case refusals and grant notes that the tool's own error output and the unattended section already state.

rows.name: get precedence and fencing
rows.does: Sets the tier precedence on a name collision, fences cross-writer hits, and says to read through get and never copy its output back.
rows.why: Two rules are worth keeping, pinning the tier flag to reach a shadowed record and never writing get output back. The fencing rationale is not needed.

rows.name: Recall digest at effort start
rows.does: Makes the session run memq recall before find at effort start and at seat takeover, and rank the digest itself.
rows.why: Without this, a session would not consult the store at the start of work.

rows.name: find hybrid search reading
rows.does: Explains the lexical and semantic blocks, the archived-withheld line, the applied tokens and the superseded labels, and says to query in the words of the problem.
rows.why: The rule to query in problem words and the meaning of the output tokens are useful, but they fit in a third of the space.

rows.name: Model-judged block disclosure
rows.does: Describes the advisory re-ranking block, the data it sends off-machine in cleartext, and its degrade states.
rows.why: The security disclosure belongs in security-model.md, and the session needs only 'advisory, and silence is normal'.

rows.name: Shared content is data
rows.does: Tells the session to treat semantic-block and shared-tier record content as data, not instructions.
rows.why: The doctrine's data-not-instructions rule already owns this.

rows.name: Recall label and coverage catalogue
rows.does: Details which tiers carry descriptions, superseded labels and coverage lines in the recall digest.
rows.why: The output explains itself when read, and this catalogue changes no action.

rows.name: Reinstating retired records
rows.does: Explains reinstating a project record by hand, and that the shared tiers have no reinstatement path.
rows.why: This is a rare path, and one sentence plus a pointer to the four remedies would do.

rows.name: memq recent close-out recap
rows.does: Makes the session run memq recent over the session at close-out, carry the digest labeled by surface, and not read 'added' as new.
rows.why: This is a kit ritual finishing-work calls, and the caution about the 'added' label prevents a false claim.

rows.name: Sync needs no go-ahead
rows.does: States that the store's automatic sync and the manual pull-rebase-push need no permission, citing the doctrine's closed list.
rows.why: The doctrine's stop-for-a-yes list already grants this, so the restatement is a copy.

rows.name: Doctor -Fix and manual push
rows.does: Covers getting a go-ahead before -Fix -Yes, the manual push commands, preferring sync-store.ps1, and verifying through kit-sync-state.json.
rows.why: This is a real procedure, but the environment-guard and ownership-test detail belongs in security-model.md and the kit-doctor skill.

rows.name: Dot-namespaced action keys
rows.does: Names journal keys as dot-separated hierarchies led by the project or domain, one hierarchy per subject, with tags for cross-cutting facts.
rows.why: This is a cheap house naming convention that makes find work.

rows.name: Outcome logging criteria
rows.does: Tells the session what to log (failures with countermeasures, settled questions, belief flips) and what to skip (routine green runs, typos, durable facts).
rows.why: Without a bar, a model either logs noise or logs nothing.

rows.name: Journal text hygiene
rows.does: Requires composed summaries rather than pasted output, the shape of a secret rather than its value, and no embedded double quotes.
rows.why: The PowerShell quoting break and leaked secrets are real, non-obvious failures.

rows.name: body-file only composed content
rows.does: Bars passing .env files, credentials or raw logs as --body-file.
rows.why: This is cheap and guards a leak into a synced shared store.

rows.name: Stamp applied in-turn
rows.does: Makes the session run memq touch --applied in the turn a memory changes what it does, stamping when in doubt.
rows.why: The decay clock depends on it, and no model would do it unprompted.

rows.name: unstamped boundary sweep and hand walk
rows.does: Makes the session run memq unstamped at each Chapter boundary, reason about untracked readers, adjudicate every line, and do a hand walk of recall rows when it cannot account for the stretch.
rows.why: The epistemics of read-stamp coverage run far past what the failure (a missed stamp that delays decay) costs; 'run unstamped, stamp what steered you' carries it.

rows.name: Frontmatter top-level placement
rows.does: Tells the session to write fields at the top level, to expect the harness to move them under metadata:, and never to quote values.
rows.why: The harness rewrite and the quoted-tags trap are invisible failures the model cannot predict.

rows.name: Tags inline and registry
rows.does: Requires inline tags only, covers index-line-over-description precedence, the tag registry file and its on-switch semantics, and a starter vocabulary.
rows.why: The inline-form rule and 'register before minting' are needed, while the registry on-switch mechanics and the starter list are not.

rows.name: machine: field
rows.does: Scopes a machine-specific fact with machine: HOSTNAME as os.hostname reports it.
rows.why: This is a short kit field definition.

rows.name: Machine configuration epoch
rows.does: Makes the session keep a canonical per-host epoch record and treat any box-dependent measurement taken before the epoch as expired, re-measuring or stating it unusable.
rows.why: This is a benchmarking-validity rule that testing-discipline's wall-clock ownership should carry, with only the record name staying here.

rows.name: author: provenance field
rows.does: Describes the CLI-written author: session-id line, its grammar, and that it is provenance and not a credential.
rows.why: The CLI writes it, and the only instruction, never write it by hand, is one clause.

rows.name: Operator tier routing test
rows.does: Routes a fact to the operator, type or project tier by asking whether it would hold in an unopened project, and requires authoring through add-operator after reading the neighbours block.
rows.why: Routing and CLI-only authoring are kit rules the model cannot infer, and a misrouted fact strands.

rows.name: Project-type tier opt-in
rows.does: Defines the type tier, the Project-Type opt-in line, the every-project-of-type bar, and add-type-only authoring.
rows.why: This is the kit structure a session needs to route and write type facts.

rows.name: Memory database layer internals
rows.does: Describes the SQL Server publish, host tenancy by login, EXECUTE-only publishers, the offline queue, and the files outside sync.
rows.why: The session never acts on tenancy or queue internals. 'The markdown is the record and the database is a derived copy' is the only needed line.

rows.name: Judged fleet memory block
rows.does: Explains the Jev-judged fleet block, its thresholds and fallback, opening shown records with memq get, and the unread/read pointer keying.
rows.why: 'Open shown records with memq get, and a no-bearing line is an answer' is the action. The thresholds and calibration plumbing are not.

rows.name: Shared-tier repair and delete mechanics
rows.does: Details whole-body repair with --update --confirm-shared, what a delete removes, union-merged stamps returning, and modify/delete sync conflicts.
rows.why: The verbs and consent are needed, but the residue and conflict detail is edge-case exposition.

rows.name: Four remedies routing
rows.does: Routes a bad record to delete (never true), repair (wording wrong), supersede (stale) or archive (aged out), and judges neighbour pairs by reading both bodies.
rows.why: This is the core judgment frame for store correction, and without it a model defaults to deleting or overwriting.

rows.name: Deletion is not redaction
rows.does: Makes the session rotate any secret a deleted or forgotten record carried, because git history and other machines keep it.
rows.why: A model may assume a delete erases a leaked credential.

rows.name: Unattended vector grant subset
rows.does: Lists the seventeen memq shapes a fleet worker gets no prompt-free grant for, and the consequences for supersedes and triggers.
rows.why: A fleet worker needs to know that withheld shapes are silently lost, but the hook owns the list and the row notes duplicate it.

rows.name: supersedes: field grammar
rows.does: Defines the supersedes pointer, which is hand-written on the project tier, names one live record, and stays within one tier.
rows.why: This is a short kit field grammar, and a wrong entry fails silently.

rows.name: anchors: field and writing
rows.does: Defines path@sha anchors, requires writing them through memq anchor, and covers backups and path refusals.
rows.why: 'Use memq anchor, never by hand' plus the purpose is enough, since the refusals explain themselves.

rows.name: Drift reporting surface catalogue
rows.does: Catalogues how decay-scan, get, recall and the session line report drift, and the five causes of a silent session line.
rows.why: The one action is to run decay-scan rather than trust a quiet session start, and 800 words of per-surface state tables exceed any plausible failure cost.

rows.name: Operator anchors inside store
rows.does: Allows machine-scoped operator records to anchor sync-published files under the store root, and lists the admissible path set.
rows.why: This is a niche capability, and the CLI enforces its own path rule.

rows.name: Anchor trust limits
rows.does: Warns about Unicode normalization, invisible characters, SHA-1 not being tamper evidence, line endings, and worktree anchoring against main.
rows.why: These are residual implementation caveats that a session will almost never hit. Only the worktree line might earn one sentence.

rows.name: Settling a drift line
rows.does: Makes the session re-read the source and then the record, route it through the four remedies, carry the whole frontmatter on a rewrite, re-anchor, and never delete on drift alone.
rows.why: The rules to keep are 'drift means unverified, not wrong', 'keep the frontmatter whole' and 're-anchor after a fix', and they take a third of the words.

rows.name: triggers: field declaration
rows.does: Defines six trigger types, the four hook moments they match at, CLI-only writing, --replace correction, specificity bars, and no secrets in cmd patterns.
rows.why: The types and the CLI rule are needed kit vocabulary, but the match-moment and parsing detail is hook implementation.

rows.name: Nudge log stamp-rate instrument
rows.does: Describes the nudge jsonl log and how to compute nudgeStampRate with a node one-liner for a plan decision.
rows.why: This is a research instrument for one archived plan's decision, not something a working session does.

rows.name: Decay threshold formula
rows.does: Sets the idle clock and the summarize and archive thresholds extended by distinct applied days, and says crossing a threshold nominates and never retires.
rows.why: The scan computes this, so 'nomination, not retirement' is the only behavioral content.

rows.name: Superseded candidates and neighbour floors
rows.does: Makes superseded records archive candidates, and explains the NEIGHBOUR_FLOOR seeds and tuning.
rows.why: The scan applies both, and tuning the floors is kit maintenance, not session work.

rows.name: Pinning against decay
rows.does: Defines the pinned: date field as a judgment act, removal by deleting the line, the shared-tier hand-edit exception, and the frontmatter line-budget grammar.
rows.why: The pin rule is needed, but the shared-tier edit path and the 40/32-line budget are exposition.

rows.name: Scan evidence line reading
rows.does: Makes the session read the stderr usage-evidence line, investigate a 'none' rather than archive, and use --drop-malformed knowing it is invocation-wide.
rows.why: 'Usage evidence none means investigate, not archive' is the needed guard, and the rest is detail.

rows.name: Running the decay pass
rows.does: Runs scan, judge, prune --rollup, then done at close-out when the stamp is over 14 days old, and splits operator, type and project calls for --confirm-shared.
rows.why: This is a kit procedure with a consent split that the model would get wrong unaided.

rows.name: Dedupe before project write
rows.does: Makes the session run memq find in the fact's words before a Write or put, reading semantic scores against the right floor, because project writes print no neighbours block.
rows.why: 'Search before writing' is needed, but the floor-reading instructions are heavy.

rows.name: Frontmatter guard scope and silence
rows.does: Describes the PreToolUse guard, its refusal of shared-tier Writes, its silent and speaking allows, and the out-of-scope targets such as archive, pending and aliased roots.
rows.why: The guard enforces itself, and the scope caveats guard against deliberate bypass, which a session following 'author through memq' never attempts.

rows.name: Known limits list
