rows.does: Lists the type tier reachable only via a declaring project, a wedged lock recovered by hand, stamp undercount, archive index growth, flattened-path sync, and the two commit paths.
rows.why: The wedged-lock and declaring-project limits are actionable, and the rest restate earlier sections.

rows.name: Always-apply skill frontmatter trigger
rows.does: Makes the session load this doctrine at the start of any non-trivial task.
rows.why: The same text is already loaded globally through CLAUDE.md as claude-kit-doctrine.md, so a skill copy pays the token cost twice for one owner's content.

rows.name: No preamble, no flattery
rows.does: Makes the session skip openers like 'great question' and lead with the recommendation, and say 'I'm not sure' when unsure.
rows.why: Current models mostly comply already; one line holds it.

rows.name: Hold position under bare challenge
rows.does: Makes the session re-check once on a repeated 'are you sure' and hold unless the evidence thins.
rows.why: Sycophantic capitulation under pushback is still a real failure and the one-recheck rule is a concrete fix.

rows.name: Teach reasoning at decisions only
rows.does: Makes the session show reasoning and alternatives at design points but execute silently once agreed.
rows.why: A sound house preference that overlaps the fork-recommendation entry and needs one sentence.

rows.name: Plain prose sentence rules
rows.does: Makes the session write one idea per roughly twenty-word sentence, answer first, no nested qualifications.
rows.why: Real house style models do not default to, but the prose-register skill owns it and this restates it at length.

rows.name: Answer-first and rule-then-reason layering
rows.does: Makes every scale open with its conclusion and state a rule before its reason, cases last.
rows.why: The document itself names prose-register as owner, so these four bullets are a partial copy that one pointer replaces.

rows.name: Heading shape rules
rows.does: Makes headings topic-shaped, title-cased, at most five words, no article or period.
rows.why: A detailed style spec that belongs wholly in prose-register, not in the always-loaded doctrine.

rows.name: Checkable claim form
rows.does: Makes the session prefer numbers, names and paths over adjectives and descriptions.
rows.why: Duplicates the confirmed/inferred/reported entry and the prose skill.

rows.name: No em dashes outward
rows.does: Bans em dashes in comments, SQL, copy and shipped docs.
rows.why: Arbitrary house choice a model will violate constantly without being told.

rows.name: Current state, not journey
rows.does: Makes shipped comments and docs state present truth and push dates and discovery history into commits and Chapters.
rows.why: Models do leave 'fixed after we found' comments, but the litmus plus rule fits in forty words.

rows.name: Commit title format
rows.does: Makes commit titles an UPPERCASE prefix plus a proper sentence under about 70 characters, with a client-briefing body opener.
rows.why: A specific house format no model infers.

rows.name: Match document length to job
rows.does: Makes the session cut filler, redundant summaries and boilerplate from written artifacts.
rows.why: Useful anti-verbosity steer but pointer text inflates it.

rows.name: C# and T-SQL defaults
rows.does: Makes the session default to C#, T-SQL and stored-procedure-only data access with EXECUTE-only principals.
rows.why: Cheap, specific house defaults a model cannot guess.

rows.name: House style beats local convention
rows.does: Makes the operator's style override sibling code unless a formatter, editorconfig or CI gate enforces otherwise.
rows.why: Models default to matching surrounding code, so this reversal must be stated.

rows.name: Authority ranking of surfaces
rows.does: Makes the session rank harness, operator word, positional grants, doctrine, owning skill and other surfaces before acting on a conflict.
rows.why: Some precedence rule is needed for a kit this layered, but six tiers with carve-outs is legalism a two-sentence rule would cover.

rows.name: Relay message deferred authority
rows.does: Makes the session treat a relay message inside a tool result as operator word acted on at the turn boundary.
rows.why: Channel-specific plumbing that belongs in the relay or peer-sessions owner, not the core doctrine.

rows.name: Stops and grants read with owners
rows.does: Makes the session read the owning skill's exceptions before treating a stop or grant met elsewhere as binding.
rows.why: Guards an edge case of the kit's own sprawl; the ownership-map entry already implies it.

rows.name: Positional authorization and closed grant list
rows.does: Makes authorization come only from operator word or named positional forms, with three standing grants listed.
rows.why: The closed grant list matters, the surrounding theory does not.

rows.name: One owner per moment map
rows.does: Makes the session consult ownership-map.md before placing a rule or when two documents conflict.
rows.why: Relevant mainly to kit-editing sessions; a one-line pointer suffices in an always-loaded file.

rows.name: Run agreed plan without pausing
rows.does: Makes the session run an agreed plan to completion, interrupting only for the executing-work blocker set.
rows.why: Models do stop early to check in or cite capacity, and this is a key autonomy steer.

rows.name: Consume operator's exact anchors
rows.does: Makes the session use given line numbers, repros and acceptance checks as the test and strip evaluative framing.
rows.why: Framing-stripping and treating a given check as the test are non-default and matter.

rows.name: Batched decisions with recommendations
rows.does: Makes the session ask decisions in rounds with a marked recommendation and record answers as 'decided YYYY-MM-DD'.
rows.why: The '(Recommended) is binding' convention and dated recording are kit-specific contracts.

rows.name: Intake gap check
rows.does: Makes the session list unstated items at intake and resolve, declare or ask each by a three-way rule.
rows.why: Models build on unstated assumptions silently; the triage rule is compact and valuable.

rows.name: Client-briefing register for asks
rows.does: Makes every decision ask readable by an outsider, in a fixed order from situation to consequence of no answer.
rows.why: Needed since models leak internal identifiers into asks, but the six-part order can be half as long.

rows.name: Nothing untrue ships
rows.does: Makes the session never publish invented metrics or unhonored claims, and sweep the tree for banned patterns.
rows.why: Fabricated marketing numbers remain a plausible, high-cost failure for client work.

rows.name: Report out-of-code state changes
rows.does: Makes the session name altered credentials, databases or local state in the close-out.
rows.why: Cheap and models often omit side effects.

rows.name: Kaizen friction capture
rows.does: Makes the session jot a one-line kaizen inbox note when a kit rule causes friction, standing-authorized.
rows.why: The mechanism is kit-specific and needed, but the kaizen skill owns the bar so this needs two sentences.

rows.name: Analyze and propose before building
rows.does: Makes the session read involved files, flag concerns and present a code-free plan before implementing.
rows.why: Without it models start coding immediately on feature requests.

rows.name: Plan doc as source of truth
rows.does: Makes every non-trivial effort run from a spec in docs/plans/, executed section by section.
rows.why: The core kit workflow a model cannot know.

rows.name: Curated docs and .kit scratch
rows.does: Makes transient artifacts go to a gitignored .kit/ path, not docs/.
rows.why: Specific path convention, cheap.

rows.name: Root-cause from real data
rows.does: Makes the session confirm causes in files and data and suspect boundary contracts when consumers disagree.
rows.why: The systematic-debugging skill carries this.

rows.name: Chapter close per section
rows.does: Makes each section end with a Chapter naming the lanes, counts and exit code, plus a compaction checkpoint when a goal is armed.
rows.why: executing-work owns the format; the checkpoint script detail belongs there.

rows.name: Memory store extension pointer
rows.does: Makes the session load memory-system before using memq, tags, decay or tiers.
rows.why: A pointer is enough; the feature list is skill description text.

rows.name: Recovery from durable artifacts
rows.does: Makes the session check git state after interruption and re-read the plan, skill and deferred tools after compaction.
rows.why: Post-compaction re-grounding is not default behavior and losing it causes drift.

rows.name: Finishing pass and terminal plan
rows.does: Makes the session run finishing-work and flip the plan doc to Complete in the same delivery as the code.
rows.why: Needed, but finishing-work and curating-docs own the details.

rows.name: Confirmed, inferred, reported marking
rows.does: Makes every load-bearing claim legible as confirmed with evidence, inferred with what would confirm it, or reported from a peer.
rows.why: The three-state vocabulary is kit-defined and curbs overclaiming, a live failure.

rows.name: Cannot measure when source down
rows.does: Makes the session report 'cannot measure' rather than a neighboring or stale number.
rows.why: Substituting a nearby figure is a real and damaging model habit.

rows.name: Run the real thing
rows.does: Makes the session run or inspect the artifact rather than trust a passing build, and rank causes by likelihood.
rows.why: Premature 'done' remains common.

rows.name: Baseline before no-regression claims
rows.does: Makes the session record pass/fail counts and failing names before changing anything.
rows.why: Models routinely claim no regressions with no baseline.

rows.name: Lane selection per step
rows.does: Makes the session pick targeted, whole-gate or contention lanes by moment and report deltas against a same-lane baseline.
rows.why: testing-discipline owns the lanes; this copy restates a dense schedule the always-loaded file does not need.

rows.name: Verdict from exit code
rows.does: Makes the session read pass/fail from the run's exit code, not a narrowed grep or a piped head.
rows.why: The $? after pipe trap is a concrete, common error.

rows.name: Green suite insufficient for visual
rows.does: Makes the session gate visual and stateful work on a real observation, including a real-browser walk per batch.
rows.why: Two statements of one rule; merge into one short bullet.

rows.name: Findings are hypotheses
rows.does: Makes the session verify subagent COMPLETEs, reviewer verdicts and stale notes against the code before acting.
rows.why: Trusting subagent claims is a frequent orchestration failure.

rows.name: Re-ground stale summaries
rows.does: Makes the session re-fetch sources read in a prior turn or session before shipping and fact-check its draft.
rows.why: Post-compaction staleness is real and not self-corrected.

rows.name: No external specifics from memory
rows.does: Makes the session verify prices, versions and dates before putting them in forwarded work.
rows.why: Hallucinated specifics in client-facing text are costly.

rows.name: Fix contradicted memory now
rows.does: Makes the session correct a recalled memory the evidence contradicts in the same turn.
rows.why: Needed rule, but the four-remedies detail belongs to memory-system.

rows.name: Red-first tests and both-ways proof
rows.does: Makes the session watch a regression test fail before fixing and prove flags off and on.
rows.why: Models skip the red step without instruction.

rows.name: Test contract pinning details
rows.does: Makes the session drive the real client for wire fields, single-source shared constants and move guards to shared boundaries.
rows.why: Detailed test design that testing-discipline should own.

rows.name: Tree-mutating probe exclusivity
rows.does: Makes the session copy files before mutation probes and restore from copies, not git checkout.
rows.why: Rare-case procedure better placed in testing-discipline.

rows.name: Withheld control for silent checks
rows.does: Makes the session prove an absence-check can fire by running it on a known-positive, shape-matched case.
rows.why: A genuinely valuable and non-default rule, but the sub-bullets on axes and class coverage double its length.

rows.name: Test cost and red pointers
rows.does: Makes the session treat reds as signals, size observation windows, and defer to testing-discipline for flakes and cost.
rows.why: The window example is useful; the rest is pointer text.

rows.name: Stay in scope, stage exactly
rows.does: Makes the session stage only its own files, avoid adjacent reformatting and flag bonus wins with an undo.
rows.why: Blanket adds and drive-by edits are common and harm shared checkouts.

rows.name: Shared-index staging protocol
rows.does: Makes the session finish edits before staging, inspect the whole index, choose commit form, and check git show and git log before push.
rows.why: Protects against peer sessions sweeping hunks, a real risk here, but the git mechanics could move to a skill with a short rule left behind.

rows.name: Act on found work
rows.does: Makes the session finish found work serving the goal now rather than filing a vague later note.
rows.why: Countervails the model tendency to defer with 'could be addressed later'.

rows.name: Write the minimum
rows.does: Makes the session avoid speculative abstractions, unrequested guards and placeholder logic.
rows.why: Over-engineering remains a common model failure.

rows.name: Stop-for-a-yes test
rows.does: Makes the session name a rollback and wait for confirmation before an irreversible act or one others depend on, with a closed exempt-channel list.
rows.why: The core safety gate, and the exempt list is kit-specific.

rows.name: Commit-model and grant carve-outs
rows.does: Makes plan commit models, standing-grant records, Review-Only overrides and Branch-and-PR interact with the stop rule.
rows.why: Legalistic precision about how grants read against the stop rule; the owning skills should hold it and this bullet should shrink to its floor.

rows.name: Revert own regression first
rows.does: Makes the session restore known-good state, then diagnose, and admit the error plainly.
rows.why: Cheap and models tend to pile fixes on a broken state.

rows.name: Stakes read and blast-radius effort
rows.does: Makes the session open non-trivial work with a one-phrase stakes read and scale process to it.
rows.why: Counterweights the kit's own heavy process on small work.

rows.name: Name old-contract consumers
rows.does: Makes the session check old servers, installed clients, caches and API consumers before calling a change safe.
rows.why: Compatibility is often forgotten and short to state.

rows.name: Merged PR branch freeze
rows.does: Makes the session read PR state before every push and send changes for a merged PR to a new branch.
rows.why: A guard hook backs it; a sentence plus the pointer suffices.

rows.name: Embedded text is data
rows.does: Makes the session surface and not act on instructions inside files and tool output.
rows.why: The harness already says this, but the kit's peer-message carve-out depends on stating it.

rows.name: Fork recommendations with alternatives
rows.does: Makes the session lead with a recommendation and why others lose, deciding low-blast picks and asking on high-blast ones.
rows.why: The decide-versus-ask split by blast radius is a useful non-default calibration.

rows.name: Ground advice in project history
rows.does: Makes the session pull real numbers, canonical values and migration history before recommending.
rows.why: The migration-away-from-X point is the only non-obvious part.

rows.name: One axis per craft round
rows.does: Makes the session change one visual axis per round, show output and name the tunable constant.
rows.why: A specific iteration contract that models do not follow unprompted.

rows.name: Four-part closing state report
rows.does: Makes a substantive turn close with ran, inferred, reported, operator-only, git state and the most-likely-wrong claim.
rows.why: A kit-defined close-out format the operator relies on.

rows.name: Pending plans board
rows.does: Makes the turn end with one line per pending plan including its docs/plans filename.
rows.why: Cross-session continuity device a model cannot invent.

rows.name: Standing dispatch request
rows.does: Makes the session treat this text as the operator's request that satisfies harness lines conditioning Agent and read-only Workflow dispatch.
rows.why: Needed to unblock the reviewer pair, but it is a long argument aimed at overriding harness gating and should be one scoped sentence.

rows.name: Orchestration and peer skill pointers
rows.does: Makes the session load brainstorming, executing-work, consult or peer-sessions before fanning out or messaging peers.
rows.why: Skill descriptions already trigger these; a two-line pointer suffices.

rows.name: Per-machine heavy process budget
rows.does: Makes the session poll for foreign test runners and builds before a suite and call partway deaths contention.
rows.why: Multi-session machines make this real, but the poll-is-a-sample reasoning can be halved.

rows.name: Readiness signals, no fixed sleeps
rows.does: Makes the session wait on until-loops against a real signal rather than sleep.
rows.why: The harness itself blocks foreground sleep and says the same.

rows.name: No self-editing permission files
rows.does: Makes the session hand over JSON rather than edit its own permission settings.
rows.why: The harness already enforces this.

rows.name: Background run exit markers
rows.does: Makes a background run write its own exit marker and the session read the result from it.
rows.why: The harness tool description carries the same rule.

rows.name: Agent stall probe and replace
rows.does: Makes the session probe a quiet agent before killing it, TaskStop before replacing, and end the turn on WAITING.
rows.why: finishing-work and executing-work own it; two bullets of pointers duplicate them.

rows.name: Do not waste moves
rows.does: Makes the session skip re-reads, lockfiles and broad greps where a target is named.
rows.why: Current models already economize reads, and the harness tool text covers re-reads.

rows.name: Outline large files before hunting
rows.does: Makes the session grep declarations in 1,000-line files before reading a range, and read whole units whole.
rows.why: The absence caveat is valuable, but the sub-bullets are long for a common skill.

rows.name: Before-you-send checklist
rows.does: Makes the session re-check fourteen questions on claims, scope, baselines and handoff before sending.
rows.why: Every item restates an earlier bullet; a five-item list of the most-missed would carry it.

rows.name: Map purpose and ranking pointer
rows.does: Tells the session that this map serves the doctrine's one-owner bullet and answers only which skill owns a moment, with the ranking left to Which Text Governs.
rows.why: The doctrine bullet that sends readers here already says what the map is for, so this intro repeats the pointer back at its source.

rows.name: Row-reading legend
rows.does: Defines the three columns, says 'doctrine' means the skill body plus its mirror as one text, and says a hook or test in the owner column enforces rules owned by prose.
rows.why: The 'doctrine' alias and the hook-enforces-prose convention are kit-specific, and without them a reader could misread which text is authoritative.

rows.name: Map amendment rules
rows.does: Requires a row to move in the same change as the prose it describes, has skills add or remove their own rows, and routes any two-owner moment to Unowned rather than picking a winner.
rows.why: Nothing else stops the map drifting from the prose, and choosing an owner is explicitly the operator's call, which a model would otherwise settle on its own.

rows.name: Owner lookup: intake and design
rows.does: Routes design, Intent records, tier bands, scout sweeps, plan review, the Jev coverage check, the council, intake gaps and plan-doc format to their owning skills.
rows.why: The kit's skill boundaries are invented, and a model cannot guess that the Intent record or the Jev check sits in brainstorming step 9 or 10.

rows.name: Owner lookup: execution
rows.does: Routes the section loop, add-decisions, brief fields, review roster, backstop, fix-delta bar, threat-model citations, dispatch waiting and probing, capacity reading, checkpoints, consults, debugging, testing and style to their owners.
rows.why: The routing is needed, but many rows restate the rule's content, such as step numbers, paragraph names and 'what citing buys', where a moment name and an owner would do.

rows.name: Owner lookup: finishing and git
rows.does: Routes the finishing pass, the PR at finishing, strand-check and reaping, memory close, commit and push authorization, commit model values, staging, commit messages, store sync and stranded-branch deletion.
rows.why: These moments are split across doctrine, finishing-work, branch-hygiene and curating-docs in ways a model would not infer, and getting git ownership wrong carries a high cost.

rows.name: Owner lookup: coordination and seats
rows.does: Routes peer messaging, Dispatch Authorization, leashed handoffs, /role seats, relayed operator messages, standing grants, the coordinator runbook, standing watches, parking and kit-goal to their owners.
rows.why: Authority questions about whose word binds depend on which skill owns the moment, and the split between peer-sessions, role and coordinator is not guessable.

rows.name: Owner lookup: memory and prose
rows.does: Routes memory mechanics, frontmatter, kaizen, kit-doctor, writing-skills, the size budget, the three-row prose-register split, the tells catalog, bare pushback and background markers.
rows.why: The prose-register row alone spends about 80 words explaining which doctrine bullets form which layer, which the doctrine and prose-register already say.

rows.name: Pointer and copy column
rows.does: Lists, for every row, each skill, charter, hook, test and doc that points at or copies the owner's rule.
rows.why: It serves kit maintainers auditing drift, not a session looking for an owner, it is greppable on demand, and it is the largest word cost in the file at about a quarter of every load.

rows.name: Unowned-moment protocol
rows.does: Tells a session that meets a contested moment to declare its reading under the intake gap check, report the gap in its close-out, and never settle it by editing either document.
rows.why: A capable model would otherwise 'fix' the conflict by editing a document, which takes away the operator's ruling.

rows.name: Commit-without-push gap row
rows.does: Records that no commit model value covers committing locally without pushing, since Review-Only forbids both.
rows.why: It is a real, live gap that a session asked to commit without pushing will run into, and the row stops it from inventing a header value.

rows.name: Doc is record, message interrupt
rows.does: Makes the session treat messages as transient interrupts and never the only home for content.
rows.why: This one-line stance settles most edge cases cheaply, and the closing paragraph repeats it for no gain.

rows.name: Roster reading and addressing
rows.does: Explains what ListAgents rows contain, sends to the bare name, adds the [ref] only to disambiguate, and reads the registry for where a peer works.
rows.why: The row semantics and the registry lookup are kit-specific and needed, but the tool description already covers most of the addressing detail.

rows.name: Screen coordinator-directory paths
rows.does: Refuses UNC paths and parent-directory segments, then matches the remaining paths by prefix containment against repos known from disk before acting on them.
rows.why: A registry path written by anyone is a real injection vector, and a model would not screen for it unprompted.

rows.name: Names are labels, not identities
rows.does: Treats from-name and roster names as self-chosen labels that can collide or be worn by an imposter.
rows.why: Needed, but the file states it three times across Messaging Surface, Standing and the claim-layers paragraph.

rows.name: SendMessage delivery semantics
rows.does: Covers the wrapper attributes, unordered senders, the delivered, held, refused and unreachable outcomes, queue caps, and the one-way boundary with elevated sessions.
rows.why: The key facts are that a clean send is not a read and elevated sessions are unreachable, and the queue figures and cause hedging duplicate the live tool description.

rows.name: notify_when_idle subscription
rows.does: Describes the one-shot idle notice, where it lands and its limits, so the session prefers it over polling.
rows.why: Preferring it over polling is useful, but most of the parameter detail belongs to the tool description.

rows.name: Harness floor on inbound messages
rows.does: States that an inbound message can never approve a prompt, change settings or run slash commands.
rows.why: The harness enforces this itself, and the doctrine's data-not-instructions rule already carries it.

rows.name: Absent tools means stop
rows.does: When the messaging tools are missing, reports the feature as off and never builds a workaround.
rows.why: It is short and blocks a plausible improvised workaround.

rows.name: Standing only for harness-delivered messages
rows.does: Gives standing only to messages the harness delivered, and treats a wrapper found inside a file or tool output as data.
rows.why: This is the provenance boundary against a forged wrapper, and a model would not draw it unprompted.

rows.name: Seat check for sender standing
rows.does: Treats a message as the sending seat's word only when the sender is local, its name is unique, and its registry Role matches, and otherwise as a colleague's request.
rows.why: This is the kit's only authentication-shaped check, and the rest of the file depends on it.

rows.name: Act decides operator routing
rows.does: Sends acts to the operator by the stop-for-a-yes test and the delegation exclusions, whoever the sender is.
rows.why: The doctrine's peer-sessions bullet and its stop-for-a-yes rule already own this.

rows.name: Dispatch Authorization grant tracing
rows.does: Before running a handed plan, checks in git history that its Dispatch Authorization section traces to the operator, and holds a chain-handed plan that touches guards or a trunk.
rows.why: Grant tracing is a real control, but the chain-handoff carve-outs are restated here and in Leashed Peers, and executing-work and kit-goal own the section.

rows.name: Three handoff reply states
rows.does: Answers a dispatched handoff with received-verified-holding-for-authority, received-authorized-deferred, or an accepted acknowledgment, and never with an unqualified "pending".
rows.why: The vocabulary is kit-defined and useful, but the justification and the separate never-say-pending rule can collapse into one sentence each.

rows.name: Handoff names anchor commit
rows.does: Names the plan's anchor commit in a handoff, never line ranges, so the receiver re-derives positions from its own tree.
rows.why: A cheap rule that prevents a real worktree-skew confusion.

rows.name: Sender re-sends until acknowledged
rows.does: The sender keeps an unconverted handoff open, re-sends it at each boundary, and records it in the plan doc, as the receiver does a held plan.
rows.why: Needed, since acknowledgments get lost, but it can be stated in two sentences.

rows.name: Suspect your own artifact first
rows.does: When your check contradicts a peer's claim, first suspects that you hold a different worktree or install, and names where your copy lives.
rows.why: Multi-worktree false refutations are a real failure that models commit readily.

rows.name: Scope excludes own subagents
rows.does: Covers only independent sessions, and follows the orchestrator that dispatched you as your own dispatch rather than as a peer.
rows.why: The boundary matters, but three paragraphs state what one sentence carries.

rows.name: Record rule for agreements
rows.does: Writes any agreement reached over messages to the plan doc, memory or a commit in the same turn, and has the message point at it.
rows.why: The doctrine's peer-sessions bullet states this rule word for word.

rows.name: Four sanctioned message uses
rows.does: Limits messaging to liveness checks, shared-tree negotiation, handoff Q&A and warm consults, which share the live-state class that qualifies a new use.
rows.why: The live-state test is a good filter, but the four bullets mostly point elsewhere.

rows.name: Roster decides liveness
rows.does: Treats the roster's busy-or-idle reading as the liveness verdict, and asks the coordinator before declaring an unlisted session dead.
rows.why: It prevents a false death call on an elevated or absent session, which is otherwise likely.

rows.name: Coordinator status round pricing
rows.does: Allows a one-line status poll only when a registry entry is stale and an operator question depends on it, and grants that ask no authority.
rows.why: The coordinator skill owns this round, so a pointer and the authorizes-nothing line would do.

rows.name: Worker blocker ask and notice
rows.does: Before declaring BLOCKED, asks the live expert once, without waiting on the answer, and notifies the coordinator on declaring.
rows.why: The Worker seat bullet restates this at greater length, so it needs one owner.

rows.name: Update window drain round
rows.does: The coordinator sends each session a drain line, sessions park at a safe boundary and reply, and the drain authorizes nothing, least of all a push.
rows.why: It is a real kit protocol, but the coordinator skill and executing-work own the content, and the file repeats the authorizes-nothing rule.

rows.name: Never block on peer reply
rows.does: Proceeds on a declared assumption or the doc's answer, and never waits on a busy peer's silence.
rows.why: Short, and it prevents deadlocked runs.

rows.name: Roles are stewardship not privilege
rows.does: Treats a seat as a label for what a session tends, never as authority, and places delegation in the operator's record only.
rows.why: The core line matters, but the role skill owns the delegation model, and this restates it.

rows.name: Coordinator and Expert seat duties
rows.does: Defines the coordinator's one-per-machine seat and the expert's duties of spec authorship and answering warm consults within source-bounded limits.
rows.why: These seat definitions are kit-specific and consumed across skills.

rows.name: Worker seat blocker protocol
rows.does: Specifies at length whose answer may prevent a BLOCKED declaration, the public-board cap, repo-relative paths, and the coordinator notice.
rows.why: The rules are real, but one bullet of about 850 words carries the security-model rationale that docs/security-model.md already owns, and a lower-tier model will not parse it.

rows.name: Admin seat perimeter and inbox
rows.does: Defines the sandbox-gated Admin seat, which reports every action, never produces work product, routes peer requests to the operator, and is reached through admin-requests.md.
rows.why: The open-mandate seat needs its bounds stated, and a model cannot infer them.

rows.name: Seat tier and step-down table
rows.does: Assigns each seat a model tier, a cadence and an observable gate for stepping down a tier.
rows.why: Only an operator arming a seat reads it, so it belongs in the role or brainstorming skill, and the running session gains nothing from it.

rows.name: Seats open set
rows.does: Lets a new seam take a new seat, and keeps a seat's defaults from making an inbound message authoritative.
rows.why: It repeats the stewardship paragraph.

rows.name: Kaizen capture as self-append
rows.does: Has each seat append kit friction to the inbox itself, within the public-board cap.
rows.why: The doctrine and the kaizen skill own capture, and each seat bullet repeats it a third time.

rows.name: Seat compaction boundary checkpoint
rows.does: Declares a compaction boundary through a registry status stamp or the kit-compact-checkpoint.js boundary verb, after a three-question check, and defines each seat's banking moment.
rows.why: The hook mechanics and marker lifetimes belong in the role skill or the hook docs, and the session needs only the three-yes test and the command.

rows.name: Consent marker operator-only
rows.does: Writes the compaction consent marker only on the operator's explicit instruction over a warranted channel.
rows.why: Otherwise a seat could release its own gate, and nothing else prevents it.

rows.name: Claim layers authenticate nothing
rows.does: Explains that the name, handshake, registry entry and board each declare a role, and none of them proves it.
rows.why: It repeats the names-are-labels and seat-check content.

rows.name: Route colliding exclusive claims
rows.does: Sends a collision over an exclusive seat to the coordinator or the operator, and never treats silence as resolving it.
rows.why: Short, and it prevents two workers holding one tree.

rows.name: Message etiquette and shape
rows.does: Checks busy status, batches questions, opens with the blast radius, states who is writing and what is not asked, keeps actionable content inline, and follows a copyable template.
rows.why: The blast-radius first line and not-a-request line are non-obvious house conventions that make messages cheap to triage, and the template teaches it fastest.

rows.name: Interrupt test for busy peers
rows.does: Sends to a busy or leashed peer only when silence would cost something expensive to unwind, and sends shared-tree warnings at once.
rows.why: Without it, models over-message busy peers, and the exception list inside it could shrink.

rows.name: Anchor handoff on sha
rows.does: Anchors a handoff on a commit sha, and has the warm predecessor send its brief unprompted.
rows.why: It duplicates the anchor-commit rule under Standing.

rows.name: Cite claim's artifact class
rows.does: Marks each factual claim with its source, such as HEAD, the installed plugin or file:line, and re-derives cross-seat claims from git show HEAD.
rows.why: The doctrine's confirmed-inferred-reported rule owns this, and only the git show HEAD-over-shared-worktree line adds anything.

rows.name: Leashed peers take no work
rows.does: Hands a leashed session only information, never work, routes a work request to the operator, and lets only a traced plan artifact hand it work.
rows.why: The rule is essential, but the file restates the list of exceptions and the grant-tracing logic from earlier sections.

rows.name: BLOCKED declaration and resolution
rows.does: Declares with a BLOCKED: first line, and resolves only on a warranted channel, a quoted relay the worker checks, or a seat's own answer within its mandate, recorded with provenance.
rows.why: The kit-specific stop-hook behavior and the relay-quote check are needed, but the file spreads them across four dense paragraphs that overlap executing-work and the doctrine's relay bullet.

rows.name: Send is not informed
rows.does: Never claims a peer was informed on a send alone, only on a reply or an explicit send result.
rows.why: Models otherwise claim a peer was informed on a send alone, and the rule is cheap.

rows.name: No laundering denied work
rows.does: Never asks a peer to do what your session was denied, refuses such a request as receiver, and the Admin seat routes all peer work requests to the operator.
rows.why: This is a real cross-session privilege-escalation guard, and a model would not apply it unprompted.

rows.name: PROJECT: Role naming
rows.does: Names a session PROJECT: Role, with the hostname for a machine-scoped seat, and keeps a fleet-assigned name.
rows.why: It is a house convention other skills read, and it cannot be inferred.

rows.name: Skill trigger description
rows.does: Loads the skill for any multi-passage prose, such as documents, tickets, emails and PR bodies, and for any piece that names a voice.
rows.why: The trigger is the only thing that routes a session here, and the voice-naming clause is not guessable.

rows.name: Ownership routing preamble
rows.does: Tells the session that the rule lives in the doctrine, the sentence bars in writing-skills and the review procedure in the prose-reviewer charter, and that a rule stated here is a defect.
rows.why: This is maintainer-facing bookkeeping that costs a working session three pointers to follow, and one line naming the owners would serve.

rows.name: Writer move plus reviewer check
rows.does: Frames each recipe item as a concrete move the writer makes and a check the reviewer runs, rather than a restated requirement.
rows.why: The dual framing is useful, but it is visible from the items themselves and needs no separate sentence explaining it.

rows.name: Answer-first relocation pass
rows.does: Has the writer read the last sentence of each unit and move any point found there to the front, has the reviewer read first sentences alone, and requires marketing copy to declare its override.
rows.why: Current models still drift toward build-up-then-conclusion in long prose, and the last-sentence scan is a concrete technique the doctrine rule alone does not give.

rows.name: Heading shape and TOC check
rows.does: Limits headings to lookup topics shaped as short titles with no period, article, question or instruction, and has the reviewer read headings alone as a table of contents.
rows.why: The doctrine's structure bullet already states the heading shape almost word for word, so only the read-headings-as-TOC check is new here.

rows.name: Reason separate from rule
rows.does: Puts each rule's reason in the next sentence, hunts for an embedded because or so that, and keeps bold leads to scannable catalogs, never arguments.
rows.why: It is a genuine house preference that models violate by default, but the doctrine carries the rule and this needs only the hunt and the bold-lead check.

rows.name: Case closes, lists stay open
rows.does: Allows one closing example only where needed, marks it illustrative, writes an open class as open, and has the reviewer hunt for leading or surplus cases.
rows.why: The doctrine and writing-skills already own it, so the recipe should keep only the reviewer's four-item hunt list.

rows.name: Checkable claim form
rows.does: Has the writer supply what a reader needs to check each claim, and has the reviewer flag any claim needing a research pass.
rows.why: This entirely defers to the doctrine's claim bullet and its Verify section and adds only a one-line reviewer test.

rows.name: Two-reading scaling matrix
rows.does: Sizes a piece by asking whether readers look it up and whether it is an argument or a catalog, and maps the four combinations to passage, short list, titled piece and document.
rows.why: The matrix is kit-defined and not guessable, but it points back at a doctrine scaling bullet that points here, so the loop and instance commentary could be cut to the table.

rows.name: Voice tag to reference
rows.does: Maps Voice: scott to references/voice-scott.md, gives every other voice value the bare register, and admits only name-dependent rules to a voice file.
rows.why: A session cannot know the tag, the file or the admission rule unless told, and a wrong voice on an operator-signed piece matters.

rows.name: AI-tells catalog read
rows.does: Has the writer read references/ai-tells.md before finishing a draft and the reviewer hunt its patterns by name and quote them regardless of voice.
rows.why: Machine-written patterns survive the other rules and a current model does not self-detect them, so the pointer to the catalog carries real weight.

rows.name: Headings and section titles
rows.does: Structures the skill into Recipe, Scaling, Voice Layer and Tells Catalog sections.
rows.why: This is minimal navigation overhead, and I counted it only so the entries sum to the document's length.

rows.name: Writer-avoids, reviewer-quotes-by-name contract
rows.does: Makes a drafting session scrub these patterns before finishing and a reviewing session cite each tell by its catalog name with the quoted passage.
rows.why: The named catalog is the kit's review vocabulary, and a model cannot know to report findings by these names unless told.

rows.name: Frequency-not-instance finding rule
rows.does: Makes a reviewer judge most tells by uniformity across the document rather than one occurrence, and say which basis a finding rests on.
rows.why: Without it a reviewer flags every triad or tail singly and produces noisy, wrong findings.

rows.name: Rhetorical and question-form headings ban
rows.does: Bans rhetorical questions in body prose, question openings and question headings, licensing one self-answer device per document.
rows.why: Current models do open with rhetorical questions, but half the words are cross-references to which surface owns question-form column headings.

rows.name: Emoji ban
rows.does: Forbids emoji anywhere in prose.
rows.why: The harness system prompt already bars emoji and 5-family models rarely emit them in agentic work.

rows.name: Em dash pointer
rows.does: Lists em dashes as a banned tell and points to the doctrine Style bullet as owner.
rows.why: The doctrine owns the rule; the pointer exists only to complete the hunt list and could be one word in a merged list.

rows.name: Hype and generated vocabulary lists
rows.does: Bans motivational words and unsupported hype adjectives, and flags generated words like delve, robust, seamless and weightless intensifiers by density and figurative use.
rows.why: Models still reach for these words, so the lists matter, but three separate sections (Banned Outright, Generated Vocabulary, Weightless Intensifiers) carry one rule and could be one list plus the add-a-fact reason.

rows.name: No closing-summary signposting
rows.does: Bans 'In conclusion' openers and closing sections that only restate the body, requiring the close to state a new result.
rows.why: Restating closes are a strong default of current models and the end-state distinction is non-obvious.

rows.name: Single-hedge limit
rows.does: Forbids stacking more than one hedge on a single claim.
rows.why: Cheap, and stacked hedging is a real 5-family habit.

rows.name: Triadic rhythm tell
rows.does: Makes the session vary enumeration size instead of defaulting to three-item lists and clauses.
rows.why: Triads are the most persistent machine cadence and a model does not break them unprompted.

rows.name: Negation-then-correction tell
rows.does: Makes the session drop 'not X, it is Y' reversals against straw positions while keeping real-reader 'However' pivots.
rows.why: This is a signature 5-family tell and the straw-versus-real distinction needs stating.

rows.name: Uniform sentence length measurement
rows.does: Makes a reviewer read the spread of sentence lengths in a section and flag clustering, with a long worked example.
rows.why: The positive rule already lives in the doctrine plain-prose bullet; the measure is useful but the 60-word example paragraph and rewrite are more than the rule needs.

rows.name: Bold lead-in overuse tell
rows.does: Limits bold term leads to scannable catalogs and flags them on argument bullets.
rows.why: The doctrine's rule-then-reason bullet already owns this bound, as the section itself admits.

rows.name: Throat-clearing cut test
rows.does: Makes the session delete signpost phrases like 'it is worth noting' by testing whether the sentence changes when cut.
rows.why: Models emit these constantly, and the cut test is a crisp, checkable procedure.

rows.name: Structural preview deletion
rows.does: Makes the session delete paragraphs previewing the next section's structure, licensing one early scope statement.
rows.why: Real tell, but it is a special case of answer-first and needs two sentences, not a full tell/rewrite block.

rows.name: One-line moral endings tell
rows.does: Makes the session end sections on a concrete consequence rather than an aphorism.
rows.why: Aphoristic section closers are a strong current-model habit and the rewrite shows the replacement.

rows.name: Over-parallel headers tell
rows.does: Flags header sets built from one template such as 'Understanding X' repeated.
rows.why: Real but less common in agent prose, and most of the words negotiate ownership with the doctrine heading bullet and voice file.

rows.name: Trailing participial clauses tell
rows.does: Makes the session split ', ensuring/allowing/making' benefit tails into argued sentences.
rows.why: Participial tails are among the densest 5-family tells and models do not suppress them unprompted.

rows.name: Non-committal verdict tell
rows.does: Makes the session pick an option in a close rather than listing merits and deferring.
rows.why: The doctrine's answer-first and recommendation-at-a-fork bullets already require a verdict; this is a restatement with an example.

rows.name: Bullets restating the paragraph
rows.does: Makes the session cut a bullet list that only re-says the preceding paragraph, keeping whichever carries new detail.
rows.why: A real habit worth catching, but the double tell/rewrite with two bullet lists spends three times what the rule and reason take.

rows.name: Tell-and-rewrite example format
rows.does: Pairs each tell with a concrete bad sentence and a rewrite that adds a fact, teaching that swapping words without adding content fixes nothing.
rows.why: The examples are what make the catalog actionable for Haiku-tier readers, and the add-a-fact lesson is the core fix.

rows.name: Voice tag and scope statement
rows.does: Tells the session that this file applies when a piece carries `Voice: scott`, that it holds voice rules only, and where its rules came from.
rows.why: The trigger tag is kit vocabulary a model cannot guess and must be kept, but the provenance and the rule about what the file admits are maintainer notes a writing session does not need.

rows.name: Blunt premise opener
rows.does: Makes the piece open with a flat declarative statement of its core premise, never a question, quote, anecdote or scene.
rows.why: The doctrine's answer-first bullet already owns this, and the bullet itself cites that owner, so only the ban on anecdote and scene openers is new.

rows.name: Frame-setter opening sentence
rows.does: Makes the first sentence lead with a framing clause such as 'The most valuable resource to the business is...'.
rows.why: This is a distinctive signature of the operator's voice that a model would not produce by default.

rows.name: Opening paragraph length band
rows.does: Holds the opening paragraph to one to three sentences and 25 to 55 words.
rows.why: A numeric house threshold that a model cannot infer and would otherwise overrun.

rows.name: Email acknowledgement line
rows.does: In an email reply, puts a one-line thanks such as 'Thanks [Name]!' before the frame-setter.
rows.why: A cheap, specific voice trait a model would not reliably produce.

rows.name: Pronoun defaults by genre
rows.does: Defaults to 'we' in technical and proposal writing, uses 'I' only for subjective framing or one-to-one email, and uses 'you' only for instructions.
rows.why: A real house choice between defensible options, and a model left alone mixes pronouns across genres.

rows.name: Active construction default
rows.does: Makes the session write in the active voice and reserve the passive for a third-party system's behavior.
rows.why: Current models already default to active voice, so only the third-party passive carve-out adds anything.

rows.name: Status-quo pivot move
rows.does: Makes the argument build the reader's status quo and then pivot with 'However,' 'By comparison,' or 'Comparatively,' after the answer is stated.
rows.why: This signature reasoning move and its pivot words are specific to the operator and would not appear unprompted.

rows.name: Italic and bold emphasis rules
rows.does: Allows at most one italic word per sentence and bolds a number together with its unit.
rows.why: These are specific typographic choices that a model would otherwise apply inconsistently.

rows.name: Caveat as own sentence
rows.does: Keeps a scope-limiting caveat to one clause, placed as its own sentence after its claim.
rows.why: A distinctive shape that counters the model's habit of embedding hedges inside the claim.

rows.name: Short paragraph-ending sentence
rows.does: Ends each paragraph on a sentence of five to twelve words.
rows.why: A concrete house threshold that the model would not follow without being told.

rows.name: Heading case by display surface
rows.does: Uses Title Case where markdown renders and ALL CAPS where text is read raw, defers to the C# or SQL style skill inside code, and holds one case per document.
rows.why: A non-obvious house rule with a routing carve-out that a model would get wrong.

rows.name: Contraction and exclamation limits
rows.does: Bans contractions and exclamation marks in a technical document body and allows both in email.
rows.why: Cheap genre-specific mechanics that a model would not apply consistently on its own.

rows.name: Oxford comma consistency
rows.does: Holds one Oxford-comma convention throughout a document.
rows.why: A current model is already consistent within a document, and the rule does not pick a side.

rows.name: End-state close
rows.does: Closes in two to four short sentences on what the reader now has, in past or present tense, never on a promise, rhetorical question or rallying cry.
rows.why: A distinctive closing shape that counters the model's pull toward forward-looking or rallying closes.

rows.name: Final section labels
rows.does: Labels the close END RESULT, Aftermath or Resolution, or leaves it unlabeled.
rows.why: Specific label vocabulary that a model cannot guess.

rows.name: Email close and CTA placement
rows.does: Closes an email with an invitation to respond and a signoff, and allows a call to action nowhere else.
rows.why: A short, specific rule on where a call to action goes that a model would otherwise break.

rows.name: Pointer map to other layers
rows.does: Routes a writer looking here for structure, sentence or tell rules to the doctrine bullets, the SKILL.md recipe and ai-tells.md.
rows.why: A writing session loads the doctrine and SKILL.md anyway, so one line naming the owners would serve in place of nine bullets.

rows.name: Retired unowned conventions
rows.does: Records that numbered lists, per-section summaries, denser status nesting and Title Case sub-sections under ALL CAPS sections are retired.
rows.why: This is journey history about what was cut, and a writer gets no working rule from it that 'one case per document' does not already give.

rows.name: Section headings overhead
rows.does: Organizes the rules under eight headings.
rows.why: The headings are the minimal scaffolding for a reader to scan the catalog.

rows.name: Skill trigger description
rows.does: Loads the skill when review findings arrive, when the operator gives feedback, or when a 'you're right' is about to be typed.
rows.why: Nothing else routes the session to this skill, and the triggers are specific and cheap.

rows.name: Findings are fallible, adjudicate each
rows.does: Treats every review-agent finding as input to judge, allows pushback with a reason, and bans rubber-stamping or reflexive deference.
rows.why: Current models over-defer to subagent output, so the rule earns a place, but the list of eight named lenses and the restated framing take about three times the words the rule needs.

rows.name: Trace-first routing of findings
rows.does: Reads a finding's trace before its severity, re-traces a `trace: none` Major, and sends findings by lens type (blind, correctness Critical, advisory, docs-curator Drift Report, mistake Basis) to specific paragraphs in executing-work and finishing-work.
rows.why: This is kit-defined routing that executing-work step 4 and finishing-work step 5 already own, so here it should be a single pointer, not a partial copy that can drift.

rows.name: Operator feedback is trusted
rows.does: Implements the operator's feedback once understood, but still checks unclear scope and flags problems.
rows.why: It sets the trust asymmetry against agent findings in one sentence, and without it the adjudication rule could be over-applied to the operator.

rows.name: Read whole set first
rows.does: Reads all findings before acting on any one of them.
rows.why: A current model reading a returned report takes it in whole before acting, so this guards against a failure it rarely shows.

rows.name: Verify finding against code
rows.does: Confirms each finding in the actual code before fixing, and treats an absence finding as a scope claim checked against the spec section, routing out-of-scope ones to executing-work.
rows.why: Fixing phantom findings and scope creep from absence findings are real failures, and the absence-as-scope-claim framing is not something the model does unprompted.

rows.name: YAGNI check on suggestions
rows.does: Greps for a caller before adding pushed-for configurability or abstraction, and leaves it out when unused.
rows.why: The doctrine's write-the-minimum rule already carries it, and the grep-for-caller test could be one clause on step 2.

rows.name: Pushback and bare-challenge protocol
rows.does: Pushes back with evidence, holds under tone, re-verifies once on a bare challenge, downgrades out loud if the evidence thins, and concedes plainly when wrong.
rows.why: The doctrine's 'Disagree up front' bullet states the same one-re-check rule almost word for word, so a pointer to it would do.

rows.name: Triage defers to executing-work
rows.does: Hands Critical, Major and Minor handling to executing-work's Address findings step.
rows.why: It is a short, necessary pointer that stops this skill from redefining triage.

rows.name: Corroboration outranks severity
rows.does: Orders fixes so that a Major two independent lenses agree on goes ahead of a Critical only one lens found, while still verifying the lone Critical.
rows.why: It is a non-obvious house ordering rule, and a model would sort by severity by default.

rows.name: Lens independence accounting
rows.does: Counts converging findings as one observation when they share a lens, each other's output, framing, or standing-brief content such as Standing Brief Amendments, and explains that dispatch order does not break independence.
rows.why: The rule that shared inputs make one observation is needed for the corroboration rule to work, but the dispatch-order digression and repeated examples spend far more words than the rule and one reason take.

rows.name: Effort-authored artifacts not corroboration
rows.does: Refuses to count two lenses citing a fixture or stub this effort wrote as corroboration of an external fact, while counting pre-effort artifacts toward independence.
rows.why: The self-confirming-fixture trap is real and subtle, but the merge-state aside and the instances-not-boundary hedging could come down to two sentences.

rows.name: Contract claims cite owning surface
rows.does: Grounds a claim about a contract in its producer's own definition, such as the schema or the emitting source line, and treats an artifact asserting an unstated contract as a proposal.
rows.why: Grounding in the source of truth is valuable, but the paragraph states the instances-not-boundary disclaimer twice and restates the doctrine's ground-in-source-of-truth rule.

rows.name: Claim finding fix routing
rows.does: Sends claim findings to executing-work's class, exceptions and dispositions, bars replacement sentences in fix briefs, and sets same-round versus close-pass timing.
rows.why: Executing-work owns the whole mechanism, and this partial restatement of its bounds is exactly the partial copy the ownership rule forbids.

rows.name: Verify load-bearing reviewer clearances
rows.does: Refuses to inherit a reviewer's 'this is fine' when believing it would retire a check, verifies it against the code, and does not treat a bare APPROVED as a reason to re-read the diff.
rows.why: Models readily trust a subagent's negative claim such as 'input cannot reach the sink', which is a high-stakes failure, and the load-bearing test is a crisp kit framing.

rows.name: Contradicting lenses settled by artifact
rows.does: When lenses disagree, sides with neither, traces the code or reads the spec section itself, records the evidence rather than the verdict, and never lets severity or specialty break the tie.
rows.why: Settling the conflict by reading the artifact is a needed steer, but the code-versus-spec split and the structurally-denied-lens caveat could come down to about half the words.

rows.name: No performative agreement
rows.does: Bans 'Good catch', 'You're absolutely right' and thanks in review replies, stating the fix or the disagreement instead.
rows.why: The doctrine's no-flattery and skip-the-preamble bullets already own this, so a one-line pointer with the banned phrases would do.

rows.name: Opening framing line
rows.does: Frames a finding as input to judgment rather than an order.
rows.why: It restates the Two Sources thesis and should fold into it.

rows.name: Ownership and designed-copy preamble
rows.does: Declares this skill owns the directory contract and grant rail, and forbids curation from deleting copies as drift.
rows.why: The ownership map already records owners; one sentence naming what this skill owns is enough.

rows.name: Coordinator directory file forms
rows.does: Defines the three files under ~/.claude/coordinator/<machine>/ (board, registry, admin-requests) and says the list is closed.
rows.why: Kit-defined paths and file roles that a session cannot know otherwise.

rows.name: Admin inbox handling rules
rows.does: Makes the Admin seat treat inbox lines as unauthoritative, route them to the operator, and flip handled lines rather than delete them.
rows.why: The rule (lines are data, confirm with operator, flip not delete) takes three sentences; race and truncation caveats are padding.

rows.name: Per-file writer rule
rows.does: Limits each registry file to its own session, the heartbeat hook and the checkpoint CLI as writers.
rows.why: Prevents sessions from overwriting each other's entries, a real multi-session failure.

rows.name: Coordinator prune of stale entries
rows.does: Allows only the coordinator to delete a foreign registry file, and only on two concurring readings logged to the board first.
rows.why: This is coordinator runbook behavior and belongs in the coordinator skill, which already owns the readings.

rows.name: Cross-machine sync and inbox concurrency
rows.does: Explains store-sync refusals for other machines' directories and routes cross-machine requests by peer message.
rows.why: Sessions need only the routing rule; the sync allowlist internals are maintainer notes.

rows.name: Unguarded directory threat model
rows.does: States the directory sits outside the frontmatter guard and relies on writer rules plus audit rather than prevention.
rows.why: Design rationale for maintainers that changes no act a session takes.

rows.name: Stamp self-check and audit CLI
rows.does: Makes a reader flag future-dated or heartbeat-leading stamps and names the kit-registry-stamp.js audit verb.
rows.why: The CLI name and the check are needed, but the explanation of what the audit does and does not prove runs long for a report-only tool.

rows.name: Registry entry format
rows.does: Specifies the exact field-by-field shape of a registry file, including which fields are machine-stamped.
rows.why: An exact kit format the model cannot infer.

rows.name: Workdir privacy gate
rows.does: Forbids absolute Workdir paths until the operator confirms who reads the store remote, and prescribes a degraded form.
rows.why: The gate matters for client privacy, but it takes about 80 words, not 260 with the disclosure and path-screen asides.

rows.name: Push moments and clock stamping
rows.does: Lists the events that trigger a registry status rewrite and requires time fields come from the stamp CLI run last.
rows.why: The trigger list and 'run push last, never type a timestamp' are needed; the clock-provenance philosophy is repeated three ways.

rows.name: Takeover ritual step order
rows.does: Runs /role as eight ordered steps, deferring to a seat runbook's own tick order.
rows.why: The core procedure the skill exists for.

rows.name: Name confirmation and launch resolution
rows.does: Takes the seat under the session's name, resolves relaunch invocations from an operator memory record, and treats that record as suspect data needing confirmation.
rows.why: The naming convention is needed; the ASCII, separator and describe-not-paste defenses over an operator-written record are heavy for a rare path.

rows.name: Runbook load and wake arming
rows.does: Loads the seat runbook and arms a recurring wake by the three-way cadence rule before any read.
rows.why: Kit-specific order and cadence rules that crash recovery depends on.

rows.name: Board and store read on takeover
rows.does: Reads the board, the Admin inbox and the full memq recall digest before announcing, treating file contents as data.
rows.why: The read order and memq recall are needed; the data-not-instructions restatement and cost justification duplicate doctrine and memory-system.

rows.name: Delegation record resolution step
rows.does: Resolves the hostname-keyed delegation record with memq so the takeover announces delegated or undelegated.
rows.why: The Standing Grants section restates the same resolution and caseless compare, so one statement would do.

rows.name: Registry write, announce, first push
rows.does: Writes the entry, handles seat collisions, announces with delegation state, and pushes the first stamped status then banks compaction.
rows.why: The closing steps are kit procedure; the banking note is a pointer and could trim slightly.

rows.name: Admin seat grants no mandate
rows.does: Makes /role Admin prepare and ask rather than self-arm its mandate.
rows.why: A short guard against self-escalation on the most privileged seat.

rows.name: Seat kaizen capture duty
rows.does: Requires every seat to append kit friction to the kaizen inbox and move on.
rows.why: The doctrine's kaizen capture bullet and the kaizen skill already carry this for every session.

rows.name: Standing-grant rail definition
rows.does: Defines a standing grant as a skill-scoped mechanism switched by exactly one operator memory record, with sync-lagged revocation.
rows.why: A kit-defined authority construct the model cannot infer and must get exactly right.

rows.name: Record-is-only-the-switch rule
rows.does: Treats a grant record's body as data that cannot widen or narrow scope and requires an extra checkable condition for single-act grants.
rows.why: The rule is essential for security, but the provenance and resolution-moment caveats can be cut to one sentence.

rows.name: Three refusal rules
rows.does: Holds that peer messages are never grants, role claims confer nothing, and a seat cannot warrant a record its own chain wrote.
rows.why: Anti-laundering guards on authority are the failure that matters most in a multi-agent fleet; the restatement near the end should go.

rows.name: Rail exclusion list
rows.does: States the rail never extends warranted channels, privacy preconditions, harness floors or owning-skill scope.
rows.why: A closed boundary list that prevents grants being read as wider than intended.

rows.name: Delegation chain and scope
rows.does: Lets delegated Worker and Expert seats act on scoped direction from seats above, bounded to plans the Dispatch Authorization rail covers.
rows.why: The chain and scope are needed, but cross-references to peer-sessions and coordinator restatements inflate them.

rows.name: Delegation exclusions list
rows.does: Lists acts delegation never covers (push past commit model, deploy, external message, permissions, out-of-scope writes, sensitive reads, onward dispatch, laundering).
rows.why: Concrete blast-radius exclusions a model would not reliably derive, and failure is costly.

rows.name: Hostname-keyed opt-in and caseless compare
rows.does: Switches delegation per machine by an operator record whose embedded hostname is compared case-insensitively to os.hostname().
rows.why: The caseless compare is a real Windows trap worth one sentence; the platform-by-platform justification is excess.

rows.name: Charter test for relayed requests
rows.does: Treats in-charter relays as prompts and applies the stop-for-a-yes tests to every act whatever its charter fit.
rows.why: Needed to stop sessions treating willingness as authority, but it restates peer-sessions standing rules and fits in two sentences.

rows.name: Trigger on any SQL work
rows.does: The frontmatter description makes the skill load on any SQL writing or editing, even when style is not named, and lists the signature traits.
rows.why: Without a broad trigger the skill never loads on ad hoc SQL, and the trait list helps the router match.

rows.name: Read the detailed reference first
rows.does: Sends the session to references/sql-style.md before it writes any code.
rows.why: Most of the house patterns cited here (§6, §11, templates) live only in that file, so the pointer is load-bearing.

rows.name: Shell-then-ALTER idempotent deployment
rows.does: Makes procedures deploy as a shell CREATE then ALTER, functions drop-and-recreate, and tables and indexes sit behind IF NOT EXISTS, and it repeats this in the antipatterns and the checklist.
rows.why: A model defaults to CREATE OR ALTER, so the rule is needed, but it is stated three times where once plus the exemplar would do.

rows.name: Tab-aligned lists
rows.does: Makes names, types and defaults align in parameter, DECLARE, column and SET lists, restated in the checklist.
rows.why: A house layout choice a model will not produce unprompted, and the words spent are small.

rows.name: Leading commas and semicolons
rows.does: Makes every continuation line start with a comma and every statement start with a semicolon, with the missing-terminator reason.
rows.why: An unusual house convention a model would never adopt on its own.

rows.name: Banner comments divide phases
rows.does: Makes procedures carry /**** TITLE ****/ banners per phase and a SCRIPT/AUTHOR/DATE/VERSION/NOTES header, restated in antipatterns and checklist.
rows.why: Needed and distinctive, but the header field list appears three times across philosophy, antipatterns and checklist.

rows.name: Mimic an existing sibling
rows.does: Makes the session copy the layout of a similar existing procedure or table when unsure, falling back to the exemplar in a greenfield repo.
rows.why: A current model mimics neighbors unprompted; only the carve-out that a messy foreign sibling does not override the style needs saying.

rows.name: Precedence against repo configs
rows.does: States that only a committed formatter config, .editorconfig or CI lint gate overrides this style and that a legacy sibling does not.
rows.why: The doctrine's Defaults section already owns this exact precedence rule, so this is a copy that one owner would carry.

rows.name: Annotated deployment exemplar
rows.does: Gives a full template procedure showing shell, ALTER, parameter banner, EXECUTE AS, SET lines, TRY/CATCH and guarded error logging, with placeholder notes.
rows.why: One concrete template conveys the whole layout faster and more reliably than the prose rules, and it is the thing a model will actually copy.

rows.name: Grep outline for large files
rows.does: Gives a regex for CREATE/ALTER definitions, a banner grep with -A 1, and rules to read past false hits, never anchor on GO, add -i for vendor scripts, and find LOGIN/ROLE/SEQUENCE/SYNONYM by name.
rows.why: The pattern itself is useful, but the corpus statistics (936 GOs, 9 of 5,332 missed) are journey detail and the caveats run far longer than the rule and one reason take.

rows.name: UPPERCASE keywords, bracketed columns
rows.does: Bans lowercase keywords and unbracketed column names.
rows.why: Cheap house choices a model would not apply consistently unprompted.

rows.name: Log errors, do not re-throw
rows.does: Makes CATCH blocks call the project's error-logging proc behind an OBJECT_ID guard instead of RAISERROR or THROW, except a nested CATCH that must propagate.
rows.why: A model defaults to THROW, and swallowing errors is a deliberate, surprising choice that must be stated with its exception.

rows.name: Parameterized dynamic SQL only
rows.does: Bans concatenated dynamic SQL, citing privilege escalation under EXECUTE AS, and requires sp_executesql with typed parameters and a justifying comment where unavoidable.
rows.why: The EXECUTE AS escalation angle is specific and the security failure matters, even though models broadly know to parameterize.

rows.name: NOCOUNT plus isolation level
rows.does: Requires SET NOCOUNT ON paired with an isolation level at the top, READ UNCOMMITTED for Get procs and READ COMMITTED for writes.
rows.why: The paired requirement and the per-verb isolation choice are house decisions a model would not guess.

rows.name: Current-state comment rule
rows.does: Bans change-narrative comments and makes section comments state what the next block does, with a WHY comment adding its reason as its own sentence.
rows.why: The doctrine's current-state and prose-register rules already own this; only the SQL-specific comment shapes need to stay here.

rows.name: SYSDATETIMEOFFSET for audit times
rows.does: Bans GETDATE() for audit timestamps in favor of SYSDATETIMEOFFSET().
rows.why: A cheap, specific house choice a model would not make on its own.

rows.name: Left-hand column aliases
rows.does: Bans expr AS Alias in SELECT in favor of [Alias] = expression.
rows.why: An unusual house form a model would not produce unprompted.

rows.name: No SELECT star to callers
rows.does: Bans SELECT * in result sets returned to callers.
rows.why: A current model already avoids SELECT * in procedure result sets unprompted.

rows.name: EXECUTE AS placement rule
rows.does: Puts WITH EXECUTE AS on procs and scalar or multi-statement functions where the codebase impersonates, never on inline TVFs.
rows.why: The inline-TVF exclusion is a compile-time trap and a project-conditional choice a model would get wrong.

rows.name: Naming and label conventions
rows.does: Sets @p_ parameters, @PascalCase locals, an @True/@False BIT pair, BEGIN -- PROCEDURE label, first list item with a leading space, and comment period rules.
rows.why: These are pure house conventions that exist only in the text.

rows.name: Table and index layout
rows.does: Makes tables group columns under comment labels with audit fields and PK_<Table> last, and indexes named IX_<Table>_<Cols> in their own guarded block in the table's file.
rows.why: Placement and naming choices a model cannot infer.

rows.name: Banner version history
rows.does: Makes a new version add a note line to the header rather than rewriting it, with ordinal English dates.
rows.why: A specific house rule a model would otherwise violate by rewriting the header.

rows.name: File ends with GO
rows.does: Requires every SQL file to end with GO.
rows.why: Trivial cost, and a model often omits the final GO.

rows.name: Completion checklist as gate
rows.does: Presents a checklist to run before calling SQL work done, largely restating the philosophy and antipatterns.
rows.why: A final check helps, but most lines duplicate rules stated above, so it should carry only items not stated elsewhere.

rows.name: Substitute names, follow sibling files
rows.does: Makes the session replace the example project's schema, audit proc and owner names with the current project's own, and copy a sibling file's layout inside such a repo.
rows.why: Without it a model copies `usp_AuditError` and `<schema_owner>` literally. Note that 'follow its layout exactly' contradicts the doctrine's rule that house style beats sibling code, so one owner should settle the precedence.

rows.name: Numbered deployment folders and file names
rows.does: Makes the session place scripts in numbered folders (3-Tables, 4-Functions, 5-Procedures and so on) and name files `<schema>.<object>.sql`, with table files unprefixed.
rows.why: The file-name rule and the main folder numbers are needed, but the folder table carries one client's specifics (LoadMaster, TL2000, TMS, reserved gaps) that do not transfer to other projects.

rows.name: Shell-then-ALTER procedure deployment
rows.does: Makes the session create a stub procedure via EXEC when absent and then ALTER it, never CREATE OR ALTER, with the shell EXEC indented two spaces, a tabbed `BEGIN	-- PROCEDURE` label and a closing GO.
rows.why: A current model defaults to CREATE OR ALTER, so this signature pattern will not appear unless stated.

rows.name: EXECUTE AS placement rule
rows.does: Makes the session add `WITH EXECUTE AS` only where the project impersonates, on every proc and scalar or multi-statement function, and never on an inline TVF.
rows.why: Short, and it prevents both copying impersonation into projects that do not use it and an invalid-syntax error on inline TVFs.

rows.name: Function drop-and-recreate deployment
rows.does: Makes the session deploy functions by dropping them if present and recreating, with scalar RETURN on its own line and inline TVFs as RETURN ( query ).
rows.why: It is the opposite of the procedure pattern, and a model would not guess the split.

rows.name: Guarded table DDL layout
rows.does: Makes the session guard CREATE TABLE with a sys.schemas-to-sys.tables existence check, a TABLE banner, grouped and tab-aligned columns, bottom audit fields on SYSDATETIMEOFFSET, unnamed inline defaults, and a last-position PK_<Table> constraint.
rows.why: Every point is a house choice a model would get differently by default, such as named constraints, OBJECT_ID guards or GETDATE.

rows.name: Guarded index blocks in table file
rows.does: Makes the session put each index in its table's file inside its own sys.indexes IF NOT EXISTS block, introduced by a fixed comment line.
rows.why: Cheap, and a model would otherwise emit separate index files or unguarded CREATE INDEX.

rows.name: Procedure header metadata banner
rows.does: Makes the session open every procedure body with an asterisk-bordered SCRIPT/AUTHOR/DATE/VERSION/NOTES banner, ordinal-English dates and append-only version notes.
rows.why: Needed, but the banner block is printed in full three times (sections 6, 19 and 21), and the template alone plus the date and append-only rules would carry it.

rows.name: Parameter declaration layout
rows.does: Makes the session declare parameters in parentheses under a column-header comment, tab-aligned, defaulting to NULL, 0 or 1, with OUTPUT last and TVPs READONLY.
rows.why: The column-header comment and default conventions are house choices a model would not produce.

rows.name: NOCOUNT and isolation level defaults
rows.does: Makes the session open each body with semicolon-led SET NOCOUNT ON and an isolation level chosen by proc kind (READ UNCOMMITTED for Get, READ COMMITTED for Save and Process), and never use XACT_ABORT.
rows.why: READ UNCOMMITTED by default and no XACT_ABORT are non-obvious choices that a model would not make, and the second changes error behavior.

rows.name: Grouped DECLARE blocks and locals
rows.does: Makes the session declare locals in semicolon-led, leading-comma, tab-aligned DECLARE blocks, use @True and @False bits, and name locals plain @PascalCase without @p_.
rows.why: The @True and @False idiom and the prefix split are house rules a model would not infer.

rows.name: Ordered section banners
rows.does: Makes the session divide each body into banner-titled phases in a fixed order (SET, DECLARE, temp tables, base data, guards, main logic, datasets, cleanup) with single-line period-ended sub-section comments.
rows.why: The banner shape and phase order are the style's most visible trait and are not inferable.

rows.name: Non-rethrowing audit CATCH
rows.does: Makes the session wrap main logic in TRY/CATCH whose CATCH calls the audit-error proc behind an OBJECT_ID guard and does not re-throw, with END ELSE BEGIN on one line.
rows.why: Swallowing errors is a load-bearing, counter-default choice worth keeping, but the long upsert example repeats the section 19 template's CATCH and section 13's upsert.

rows.name: Leading commas, tabs, brackets
rows.does: Makes the session lay out every wrapped list with a leading space then leading commas, align with 4-column tabs, and bracket every column name.
rows.why: A core signature trait that a model will not produce unprompted.

rows.name: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE forms
rows.does: Makes the session write `[Alias] = expr` output columns, short AS-less table aliases, the specific INSERT and UPDATE layouts, the upsert shape, and no SELECT * outside controlled SELECT INTO.
rows.why: The alias-first form and statement layouts are distinctive and are needed as shown.

rows.name: JOIN and CTE conventions
rows.does: Makes the session write LEFT JOIN and INNER JOIN spellings, parenthesized multi-condition ONs, free OUTER APPLY, and semicolon-led, cte-prefixed chained CTEs.
rows.why: Short house choices, several of which differ from a model's defaults, such as bare JOIN and no ;WITH.

rows.name: Built-in function preferences
rows.does: Makes the session prefer CONCAT, COALESCE, TRY_ functions, FORMAT only for user-facing strings, CONVERT internally, and SYSDATETIMEOFFSET for audit timestamps.
rows.why: These are defensible alternatives where the house pick has to be stated. It is cheap.

rows.name: Temp table existence and scoping
rows.does: Makes the session guard temp-table creation with a tempdb OBJECT_ID check, comment its purpose, declare shared temp tables in the outer proc, and allow SELECT INTO.
rows.why: Brief, and the existence-check habit is not a default.

rows.name: Comment styles and period rule
rows.does: Makes the session use banner, block, group and inline comment forms per a table, ending sentence comments with a period and labels without one.
rows.why: The sentence-versus-label period rule is subtle and applies to every comment the session writes.

rows.name: No history in comments
rows.does: Makes the session keep sentence comments to short imperative descriptions, with no history, rationale essays or narrative.
rows.why: The doctrine's 'documents ship the current state' rule and the C# style already carry this. One owner would do.

rows.name: Object naming convention table
rows.does: Makes the session name objects by a fixed pattern table: usp_, udf_, @p_, PK_, IX_<Table>_<Cols>, cte, # temp, plus project-specific proc suffixes.
rows.why: The core table is needed and compact. It restates the locals rule from section 9, and the suffix list (_TMS, _Custom_<Vendor>, _Maintenance) is one client's catalog.

rows.name: Full procedure, table, function templates
rows.does: Gives the session copyable skeletons for a new procedure, table-plus-index and inline or scalar function that combine all the rules above.
rows.why: Templates are the most reliable carrier of whitespace-level style for any tier, and they could let the prose sections above shrink rather than repeat them.

rows.name: Trigger description and framing thesis
rows.does: Loads the skill for watch loops and frames the core risk: the loop's own notes go stale while still reading as fact.
rows.why: The description is what routes to the skill, and the one-paragraph thesis gives the reason every later rule rests on.

rows.name: Runbook and ledger split
