rows.does: Makes the watch keep exactly two artifacts: a committed procedural runbook and a gitignored ledger under .kit/ that is rewritten in place.
rows.why: This is a kit-defined structure with a kit path, and without it a session keeps loop state in context or in an appended log.

rows.name: Safety arm versus paced arm
rows.does: Defines a repeating heartbeat whose only job is to guarantee some wake, plus a one-shot that paces the next pass, both armed as ensure rather than add.
rows.why: It restates the tick order's steps 1 and 4 and the pacing paragraph, so the tick order alone should own it.

rows.name: Standing versus situational sections
rows.does: Splits the ledger into standing content (prohibitions, source-confirmed mechanisms, do-not-reopen traps) and situational content (the board, open interventions, pings, quiet streak).
rows.why: It is the core ledger contract, and it decides what a later pass may act on without re-measuring.

rows.name: Ledger admission test
rows.does: Admits a line only if a successor with no context needs it to resume, and refuses lines that argue or whose subject is the keeper's reasoning.
rows.why: Keeping narrative out of the ledger is a real failure worth guarding, but the rule, its two tells and one reason fit in about 60 words.

rows.name: Admission doubt falls off-ledger
rows.does: When the keeper cannot say a successor needs a line, keeps it off, and argues the cost of each misplacement through supersede, prune and rewrite rules.
rows.why: The tie-break is one sentence plus one reason, and the rest is proof that the other rules never re-ask admission.

rows.name: Residual default and exemptions
rows.does: Explains which named classes the admission default cannot remove, exempts prohibitions and traps from doubt, and requires consuming skills to name every class their ledger is the sole record of.
rows.why: This is a self-referential legal apparatus about how rules interact that no 5-family model would apply faithfully mid-watch, and the operative rule (prohibitions and traps stay until their source retires them) fits in one sentence under the prune rule.

rows.name: Kind fork by misfiling cost
rows.does: Settles doubt about a line's kind toward situational, except that prohibitions and traps fall to standing, and explains why each misfiling costs what it does.
rows.why: The rule and its one carve-out take two sentences, and the paragraph spends about 250 words deriving them.

rows.name: Evidence time and re-derive command
rows.does: Requires every situational sentence to carry the time of its evidence and the command that re-derives it.
rows.why: A model does not do this unprompted, and it is what makes the ledger checkable by a later pass.

rows.name: Supersede lines in place
rows.does: Rewrites a changed fact's line rather than stacking a new baseline under the old one.
rows.why: It is cheap, and appending is the default habit that leaves two readable baselines.

rows.name: Read protocol at ledger top
rows.does: Puts a section at the top of the ledger stating what a constrained pass reads first, so it still reads what prevents damage.
rows.why: It is a kit-specific format a model would not invent, and it protects low-context passes.

rows.name: Quiet-tick prune with hash-verified archive
rows.does: Prunes only on quiet ticks into a byte-identical dated archive verified at the destination, keeps traps live forever, and re-derives offsets after the last edit.
rows.why: Keeping traps live and pruning only on quiet ticks matter, but the hash-verified byte-identical archive costs more than the failure a gitignored scratch ledger risks.

rows.name: Fixed four-step tick order
rows.does: Fixes each pass as arm heartbeat, re-derive the board from the source of truth, re-measure standing conditions, then act, write, arm next, sleep.
rows.why: This is the skill's load-bearing procedure, and arming first and re-deriving rather than trusting the ledger are things a model skips without being told.

rows.name: Plan doc outranks ledger
rows.does: Re-reads the governing plan doc before obeying a standing line that concerns that plan's gate.
rows.why: It is short, and a stale ledger line overriding a changed plan is a realistic failure.

rows.name: Wake prompt carries only prohibitions
rows.does: Limits a self-authored wake prompt to the standing prohibitions and a ledger pointer, with no situation report.
rows.why: Models naturally stuff status into a wake prompt, and the next pass then follows stale instructions.

rows.name: Timer staleness and idle firing
rows.does: Checks the timer list against the clock, treats an elapsed one-shot as stale, and knows timers fire only when idle.
rows.why: These are harness facts a model cannot infer, and without them it misreads the timer's wakes.

rows.name: Pacing by board activity
rows.does: Gives a static board the heartbeat only and an active or uncertain board a one-shot 15 to 60 minutes out.
rows.why: It is a concrete house threshold with a sound doubt rule, stated compactly.

rows.name: Ping part order
rows.does: Orders a ping as corrections first, then the ask in client-briefing register, then an evidence line naming the source and subject of each figure.
rows.why: The order is kit-specific and worth keeping, but the evidence-line rule restates the doctrine's Before You Send check and could point to it.

rows.name: Dedup key per condition
rows.does: Sends one ping per condition and never re-sends an ask that is still pending.
rows.why: Loops re-ask by default, and repeated pings spend the operator's attention on phone notifications.

rows.name: Escalation and cannot-measure pointers
rows.does: Points to the doctrine's blocker set and its cannot-measure rule, rather than restating when to escalate.
rows.why: The doctrine already owns both rules, so a one-line pointer is all this document needs.

rows.name: One-way-door preflight
rows.does: Before any closure, dismissal, delete or resume, names what will act on the item afterward, and does not close it if the answer is the mechanism being removed.
rows.why: Watch loops tidy up aggressively, and this concise test prevents losing the thing that would have brought an item back.

rows.name: Probe before killing agents
rows.does: On every pass with a dispatch in flight, reads finishing-work's unavailability rule, derives windows from it, and never treats directory quiet alone as a stall.
rows.why: The warning that a watch manufactures stall signals is valuable, but the path-resolution detail and the restated doctrine could be a single pointer.

rows.name: Retirement distillation and destination routing
rows.does: At retirement, distils what the interventions taught into lessons for the watched system and for the kit, and throughout the run routes plan decisions to Chapters and instrument lessons to memory.
rows.why: The routing of three homes is needed, especially for standing seats, but it re-explains the ledger definition and the admission tells it already relies on.

rows.name: Skill trigger description
rows.does: Loads the skill for any bug, failure or failing test before a fix is proposed, and especially after a failed fix.
rows.why: Without the trigger text the skill never loads, and the 'previous fix did not work' clause is the high-value trigger.

rows.name: No fix without root cause
rows.does: Bars proposing or applying a fix until the failure is reproduced and its cause understood.
rows.why: Current models still jump to plausible patches under pressure, and this single line is the skill's thesis at minimal cost.

rows.name: Five-bin failure classification
rows.does: Makes the session sort a failure into code, environment, tool, external service or unknown before reproducing, and never alter working code to dodge an environment fault.
rows.why: The 'never change working code for an environment problem' rule earns its place, but the five-bin taxonomy adds little a 5-family model lacks.

rows.name: Reproduce before investigating
rows.does: Requires a reliable repro via a temporary script or test, or evidence gathering when it will not reproduce, and bans speculative 'should help' changes.
rows.why: The ban on unreproduced speculative fixes addresses a real, recurring agent failure, and the cross-reference avoids duplicating the doctrine's repro rule.

rows.name: Read the whole actual error
rows.does: Makes the session read full messages, stacks and logs, including the project's server-side error log or audit table.
rows.why: Reading the error is default behavior; only the pointer to the server-side log or audit table is house knowledge worth keeping.

rows.name: Check what changed recently
rows.does: Directs a look at git log, diff and deployment history around the onset.
rows.why: A current model checks recent changes unprompted when debugging.

rows.name: Trace data flow backward
rows.does: Traces from symptom to first divergence and dispatches the Explore subagent for unfamiliar code instead of guessing.
rows.why: Backward tracing is standard practice; the Explore-dispatch steer is the only kit-specific part.

rows.name: SQL stack root-cause checklist
rows.does: Checks deployment drift against sys.sql_modules, EXECUTE AS security context, actual data shapes, and READ UNCOMMITTED isolation in stored procedures.
rows.why: These are house-stack-specific causes, such as a silent stale proc under shell-then-ALTER, that a model would not suspect first without being told.

rows.name: One falsifiable hypothesis at a time
rows.does: Makes the session state one 'X causes Y because Z' hypothesis, test it with the smallest falsifying check, and never bundle changes.
rows.why: Bundled shotgun changes remain a common agent failure, and the rule is already compact.

rows.name: Fix cause, verify, bank learning
rows.does: Fixes the cause rather than the symptom, re-runs the repro and the targeted lane, banks the gotcha to memory, and records the finding in the plan Chapter.
rows.why: The lane, memory banking and Chapter steps are owned by the doctrine and testing-discipline, so this section can point rather than restate.

rows.name: Two-failed-fixes stop and consult
rows.does: After two failed fixes, forces the session to stop, list and verify assumptions, widen the frame, convene a consult, and report with the ruling.
rows.why: Models loop on a third and fourth patch without a hard counter, and the consult hook is a kit mechanism a model cannot infer.

rows.name: Design-level cause goes to operator
rows.does: Routes a root cause that implicates a design decision to the operator with evidence instead of patching around it.
rows.why: Quiet workaround patches of design faults are a plausible and costly failure, and the line is short.

rows.name: Trivial-fix exemption and re-entry
rows.does: Lets a directly visible trivial cause skip the phases, and sends a failed first fix back into this skill.
rows.why: The exemption duplicates the description's skip clause; only the 'failed first fix means debugging' re-entry line adds anything.

rows.name: Skill trigger description
rows.does: Loads the skill when a session writes, audits, selects or reads tests, or reads a wall-clock figure.
rows.why: Without the frontmatter the skill never loads, and the trigger list is specific to the moments that need it.

rows.name: Lane commands live in memory
rows.does: Tells the session to look lane commands up in the project memory tier, and to record them there when a repo first defines its lanes.
rows.why: Where the commands live is kit-specific, and without the pointer a session guesses the commands or rediscovers them each time.

rows.name: What earns a test
rows.does: Admits a test only for an acceptance criterion, a machine-only path, a cross-surface pin or a real defect, all instances of a contract no other gate catches.
rows.why: Left alone, models over-test, so the class rule matters, but the one-sentence class plus the four names would do the job.

rows.name: CRLF normalization in prose pins
rows.does: Makes a pin that reads shipped prose normalize CRLF to LF before comparing.
rows.why: This Windows checkout gotcha is concrete and cheap to state, and a model will not anticipate it unprompted.

rows.name: Requirement-or-choice test
rows.does: Makes the session ask whether an edit the test forbids could be made on its own authority, and refuses to write the test if so, with detailed rules on runtime readers, shipped surfaces and whole-tree pins.
rows.why: The core question is valuable against brittle pins, but the carve-outs are repeated in the retirement section, and the rule plus one reason fits in about 80 words.

rows.name: Flag case four requirements
rows.does: Stops the session pinning a flag's configured value, and has it pin on/off behavior, the unreadable-input direction, degrade-not-throw and the exact disabling value.
rows.why: The doctrine already says to prove a flag both ways, so only the fail-direction and silent-allow points add anything, and they fit in two sentences.

rows.name: Test price and Chapter trade
rows.does: Weighs a test's wall-clock cost and churn against the break it catches, and makes a Chapter name the spawn sites a spawning test adds.
rows.why: The Chapter disclosure is a real kit contract worth keeping, but the cost prose restates the earning rule.

rows.name: Prefer whole-tree family pins
rows.does: Steers toward one invariant pinned across a whole family, and away from a test per function, extending the family pin when a member is added.
rows.why: This house choice runs against a model's default of writing a unit test per function, and it catches the drift defects that matter.

rows.name: Retirement classes
rows.does: Retires or refuses mirrors, redundant counts, wording pins, duplicates, orphans and choice pins, with carve-outs and a repair-before-delete rule.
rows.why: Retiring tests is needed and non-default, but the choice-pin item re-litigates the requirement-or-choice section at length, and the list collapses to its closing class sentence plus the six names.

rows.name: Security-model citation guard
rows.does: Bars retiring a test that docs/security-model.md cites as a control unless the same section amends that document, after the session searches and reads the citing paragraph.
rows.why: This repo-specific cross-surface rule cannot be inferred, and breaking it silently removes a security control.

rows.name: Control legs never retire
rows.does: Protects a leg whose job is to prove the neighboring comparison had something to compare.
rows.why: The doctrine's withheld-control bullet already carries the concept, so a one-line pointer from the retirement list would do.

rows.name: Shape bar
rows.does: Holds the session to one focused test per stated behavior, sized like its neighbors, and adds another only where it sees what the first cannot.
rows.why: This restates the earning and duplicate rules, and a current model already writes neighbor-sized focused tests.

rows.name: Lifecycle and red ruling
rows.does: Makes a test change track the code change, makes a Chapter explain adding tests while retiring none, and has each test the change reddened ruled a defect, a named contract change or a choice, never fixed by widening the assertion.
rows.why: Widening an assertion to go green is a real model failure, and the ruling vocabulary is a kit contract.

rows.name: Shared-setup blind spot
rows.does: When every test in an area shares a setup that avoids a hazard, makes the session pin that hazard with one test outside the setup.
rows.why: Models rarely notice this blind spot unprompted, and the rule costs very little.

rows.name: Price the shape at authoring
rows.does: Swaps spawn-per-assertion, per-test fixtures, fixed ports and shared state for batched spawns, copied fixtures, owned temp dirs and a parallel runner from day one.
rows.why: The trades are sound, but a current model knows most of them, so the closing class sentence plus parallel-from-day-one carries the weight.

rows.name: Targeted lane definition
rows.does: Defines the targeted lane as the changed files' tests plus any family pin over them, and assigns it to fix rounds and section close.
rows.why: The doctrine's gate bullet states the same moment assignment nearly verbatim, so one owner should hold it.

rows.name: Whole-gate moments
rows.does: Runs the whole gate at finishing and handoff, at a merge, and before a push to an ungated consumer trunk, with the reasons for each.
rows.why: The doctrine copies this moment list almost word for word, so it has two owners where the map wants one.

rows.name: Merge rebuilds stamped artifacts
rows.does: Makes a merge that touches the hook sources rebuild the local build artifact with build.ps1 or build.sh before gating.
rows.why: This kit-repo fact is invisible without the text, and a stale stamp hides with no conflict.

rows.name: Contention lane
rows.does: Moves tests over machine-shared state into a serial lane that runs beside the whole gate, and at section close when that state is touched, instead of retrying the main gate.
rows.why: The lane is kit-defined, and it stops retry-until-green on the main gate.

rows.name: Peer suspects in-flight plan
rows.does: Makes a peer whose baseline reddens outside its own diff suspect the in-flight plan first, because mid-plan only targeted lanes run.
rows.why: The doctrine's gate bullet already carries this sentence.

rows.name: Doctrine pointer on baselines
rows.does: Points to the doctrine for same-lane baselines and no-regression claims.
rows.why: This pointer restates what the doctrine, loaded every session, already owns.

rows.name: Red discrimination protocol
rows.does: Captures the exit code and output from the run, isolates the red by running solo, then the class, then an unchanged re-run, then a clean tree, and names it flake or regression from the evidence.
rows.why: Models otherwise re-run until green or call a flake on feel, and the ordered protocol is compact.

rows.name: Contention red to kaizen
rows.does: Files a kaizen note naming which suite cannot share the box with which other load, when a red occurred beside a neighbor's load and passes on a solo re-run.
rows.why: This routing is kit-specific and cheap.

rows.name: Clock captured with baseline
rows.does: Records the suite wall clock and lane beside the pass/fail baseline, and routes established growth to a fast lane.
rows.why: The rule is useful, but the routing clause duplicates the lane design.

rows.name: Moment-pin measured figures
rows.does: Tags every measured figure with its producer, time, host and contention, and keeps such figures only at journal-layer sites of a plan doc or memory.
rows.why: The pin format is kit-specific and worth stating, but the placement rules restate the doctrine's journey ban at length.

rows.name: Contention beside the clock
rows.does: Records the process count and free memory with each wall-clock figure, and compares growth only at comparable contention, with a quiet-versus-loaded run to size the effect.
rows.why: The comparability rule matters, but the experiment recipe is more than the rule needs.

rows.name: Check the box before suites
rows.does: Polls for foreign runners or builds before a suite, treats the poll as a sample, names missed overlap as contention, and says in reports how old the poll is.
rows.why: The doctrine's machine-budget bullet carries nearly identical text, so this is a second copy of one rule.

rows.name: Frontmatter trigger description
rows.does: Makes the frontmatter description list when-to-load symptoms so the skill triggers on the right tasks.
rows.why: Skill routing depends on this field, and it is cheap.

rows.name: Skill-as-behavior opening thesis
rows.does: Frames a skill as prose that must change behavior under pressure, not documentation.
rows.why: It is one sentence, and it sets the test every later rule applies.

rows.name: When to create a skill
rows.does: Limits new skills to non-obvious, recurring, general techniques, sends project conventions to CLAUDE.md and mechanical checks to hooks, and prefers folding into an existing skill.
rows.why: Left alone, a model adds files readily, and a lean kit is a real house choice.

rows.name: Size budget ledger sync
rows.does: Requires moving the caps in test/size-budget.json with kit-size.js sync in the same change, and tells reviewers to judge only whether the added words earn their place.
rows.why: A model cannot guess the command or the ratchet, but the review-weighting and bare-form audit clauses could be cut to about half.

rows.name: Skill file anatomy rules
rows.does: Sets one SKILL.md in the kit voice, a quoted description, tables for scanned content and prose for the why, and flowcharts only for decisions the agent could get wrong.
rows.why: Quoting the description is the load-bearing line, and a current model already follows the tables-versus-prose and flowchart advice.

rows.name: One owner, grep key phrases
rows.does: Makes the editor grep a rule's key phrases across the kit and fix the owning copy, not the nearest one, and point at curating-docs for the plan-doc contract.
rows.why: The doctrine's one-owner bullet and the ownership map already carry the principle, so only the grep step needs to stay here.

rows.name: Rule-form-by-failure table
rows.does: Makes the author name the failure first, then pick the matching form: prohibition, positive recipe, required slot or observable conditional.
rows.why: This is non-obvious prompt-engineering knowledge, and it is the core value of the skill.

rows.name: No nuance or exemption clauses
rows.does: Bans 'unless it matters' clauses and exemption clauses, and requires a real exception to be written as its own observable conditional or removed by restructuring.
rows.why: Models write hedged rules by default, and the text is short.

rows.name: Close enumerations with class
rows.does: Requires every list in a rule to state whether it is closed, or that it gives instances and not the boundary.
rows.why: The doctrine's 'never write an open list as closed' says the same thing, so the Checkable Facts entry duplicates it.

rows.name: Checkable-framing and open-list facts
rows.does: Makes the author frame facts so the reader can verify them, and state observed lists as open unless a contract closes them.
rows.why: The doctrine's 'written in the form a reader can check' bullet and its open-list line already cover this almost verbatim.

rows.name: Sentence-shape bars
rows.does: Applies three bars to curated prose: one idea at about twenty words, the literal phrase over metaphor, and a pointer where another site owns the rule.
rows.why: The doctrine's plain-prose bullet and the prose-register skill own these bars, and this section re-argues them at length.

rows.name: Paragraph-unit claim correction
rows.does: When correcting a claim, the writer re-derives the whole paragraph and then hunts every other surface that carries the same claim.
rows.why: A model patches the one sentence and leaves the stale carriers by default, a real and silent failure.

rows.name: Anchor-restore on insertion
rows.does: Makes an insertion anchored on neighboring text restore that anchor byte for byte, then re-grep it with a control at HEAD.
rows.why: The failure is real with Edit anchors, but the control-at-HEAD step is heavy for a rare case, so one sentence would do.

rows.name: Carrier disposition routing
rows.does: Routes each other-surface carrier by type: fix the owner, land parity sets together, update in-scope restatements together, and send out-of-scope files through the fix-round route.
rows.why: Parity-pin sets and out-of-scope routing are needed kit knowledge, but the open-class hedging and backstop discussion inflate it.

rows.name: RED-GREEN-REFACTOR skill testing
rows.does: Makes the author watch a fresh subagent fail without the wording, add minimal guidance until it complies, close loopholes under combined pressures, and read every flagged rep.
rows.why: Without it, skill edits are untested guesses, and a model would not run behavioral probes unprompted.

rows.name: Probe runner before-after pair
rows.does: Makes kit-repo changes to probe-covered passages run tools/probe-corpus/run.mjs before and after, match changed paths to probe shapes, and handle ruled versus proposed probes.
rows.why: The command and the trigger are needed, but the path-matching and leg-selection detail belongs in the probe-corpus README, which already owns the runner.

rows.name: Four-way pair reading taxonomy
rows.does: Classifies each probe pair result as held, repair, corpus-owned or an intent-test finding, and handles errored or designed rows.
rows.why: Finishing-work step 6 and the probe README already own row status and dispositions, so this is a second owner of the same moment.

rows.name: Probe timing and recording
rows.does: Runs the pair once at section close, never per fix round, sends home/*.md changes to reps with cache staging, and records the reading in the Chapter's Decisions / Surprises line.
rows.why: The timing and where the reading is recorded are needed, but most of the text points at owners in other documents.

rows.name: Doctrine probe in fresh session
rows.does: Makes a doctrine-change GREEN run in a headless claude -p with the candidate wording staged in the plugin cache, never in the user doctrine file or a same-session subagent.
rows.why: A model cannot know that same-session subagents miss the edit, and staging in the user's doctrine file is a harmful mistake.

rows.name: Contaminated-RED shipping rationale
rows.does: Lets a doctrine-adjacent rule ship without a reproduced RED only when it records a point-of-action rationale, and otherwise leaves it out.
rows.why: The decision rule is useful, but the explanation of inheritance contamination could fit in two sentences.

rows.name: Correction rule binds every writer
rows.does: Tells every writer to assume no downstream review backstop for curated prose, and points at finishing-work and executing-work for which pass reads which surface.
rows.why: This is a pointer paragraph that adds no action beyond the correction rule it follows.

rows.name: Antipatterns list
rows.does: Warns against narrative skills, unconditional harness-injection claims and guidance written from imagination.
rows.why: The harness-setting caveat is non-obvious and worth keeping, while the other two restate the doctrine's journey rule and the RED requirement.

rows.name: Kaizen rewrite-not-append pointer
rows.does: Tells the author that accepted lessons are folded by rewriting the owning passage, never appended, and that the doctrine decides whether a sentence belongs.
rows.why: The kaizen skill and the doctrine own both rules, so this is pure pointer text.
